17ac2877573759eb8216244d031502153d9804f8.sourceText: Arizona officially kicked off its first Arizona Tech Week during the past week, presenting the event as a statewide platform to highlight the state’s growing technology economy. The Arizona Commerce Authority said the April 6 to April 12 schedule was expected to attract thousands of attendees, making it a broad promotional effort rather than a single conference concentrated in one venue.
17ac2877573759eb8216244d031502153d9804f8.translatedText: 亞利桑那州在過去一周正式啟動了首屆亞利桑那科技週，將該活動作為全州範圍的平台來展示該州不斷增長的科技經濟。亞利桑那州商務局表示，4 月 6 日至 4 月 12 日的日程預計將吸引數千名與會者，使其成為一項廣泛的促銷活動，而不是集中在一個地點的單一會議。

a1112f90c1301e0d3a83f4f5384d6c5d3503d10f.sourceText: What makes the initiative notable is its decentralized structure. Instead of centering everything in one convention hall, organizers described Arizona Tech Week as a network of events hosted across the state, designed to showcase founders, investors, startups, employers, and the broader innovation community. The ACA also highlighted a shared RSVP management tool offered to hosts so they could track attendance and communicate with participants more easily.
a1112f90c1301e0d3a83f4f5384d6c5d3503d10f.translatedText: 該計劃的引人注目之處在於其分散的結構。主辦單位沒有將所有內容集中在一個會議廳，而是將亞利桑那州科技週描述為在全州舉辦的活動網絡，旨在展示創始人、投資者、新創公司、雇主和更廣泛的創新社區。 ACA 還強調了為主辦方提供的共享 RSVP 管理工具，以便他們可以更輕鬆地追蹤出席情況並與參與者溝通。

93e5a3cb40d88e2567c668672a6fc92d39c06e4f.sourceText: That approach fits Arizona’s current economic branding. State officials have spent the last several years arguing that Arizona is not just landing large manufacturers, but also building a wider technology identity that includes software, entrepreneurship, research, venture activity, and talent development. For residents, the week functions as a public-facing sign of that ambition. For founders, recruiters, and service providers, it is also a practical networking window tied directly to Arizona’s effort to strengthen its position as a regional tech center.
93e5a3cb40d88e2567c668672a6fc92d39c06e4f.translatedText: 這種方法符合亞利桑那州目前的經濟品牌。過去幾年，州官員一直認為亞利桑那州不僅要吸引大型製造商，還要建立更廣泛的技術身份，包括軟體、創業、研究、創投活動和人才開發。對居民來說，這一週是這項雄心壯志的面向公眾的標誌。對於創辦人、招募人員和服務提供者來說，這也是一個實用的網路窗口，與亞利桑那州加強其區域技術中心地位的努力直接相關。

3663ede3eb4b48e84db87117653748e2dfe09ae9.sourceText: A well-known Arizona food brand is making a bigger move into metro Phoenix dining. Queen Creek Olive Mill is partnering with In Good Spirits Hospitality, the restaurant group behind concepts such as The Gladly and Citizen Public House, to launch a new restaurant, bar, and market in Phoenix.
3663ede3eb4b48e84db87117653748e2dfe09ae9.translatedText: 亞利桑那州的一個知名食品品牌正大舉進軍鳳凰城的餐飲業。 Queen Creek Olive Mill 正在與 In Good Spirits Hospitality（The Gladly 和 Citizen Public House 等概念背後的餐廳集團）合作，在鳳凰城開設一家新餐廳、酒吧和市場。

3a5ccbd44a2fce6871488f85d54258bd66232967.sourceText: The new concept will be called The Olive Farmer and is scheduled to open this fall at 44th Street and Osborn Road, in the former Santo Arcadia space. KTAR reported that the project is designed as an all-day, Italian-inspired operation, giving the olive mill a more direct presence in one of the Valley’s established restaurant corridors.
3a5ccbd44a2fce6871488f85d54258bd66232967.translatedText: 新概念將被稱為 The Olive Farmer，計劃於今年秋天在 44 街和奧斯本路（Osborn Road）的前 Santo Arcadia 空間開業。 KTAR 報導稱，該項目設計為全天營業，受義大利風格啟發，使橄欖磨坊能夠更直接地出現在山谷中一處成熟的餐廳走廊中。

e5a618cfc35c6bf8286e25f9bd2d255e3691b1db.sourceText: Owner Perry Rea said the partnership is built around ingredient quality, while hospitality veteran Bernie Kantak will lead the kitchen. Kantak, a multiple-time James Beard semifinalist, brings a recognizable local culinary name to the project, and the operators are emphasizing local sourcing along with a seed-oil-free menu philosophy.
e5a618cfc35c6bf8286e25f9bd2d255e3691b1db.translatedText: 業主 Perry Rea 表示，合作夥伴關係是圍繞原料品質建立的，而酒店業資深人士 Bernie Kantak 將領導廚房。多次入圍 James Beard 半決賽的 Kantak 為該項目帶來了一個知名的當地烹飪名稱，經營者強調本地採購以及無籽油菜單理念。

d6d3cb3a7eb33a63d4c8d6c8c3ef23f04d3ec1e4.sourceText: For Phoenix diners, the opening adds another locally rooted concept in a market where national chains and chef-driven independents are competing heavily for attention. For local suppliers and nearby businesses, it is also a reminder that strong Arizona brands are continuing to expand beyond their original footprint and trying to turn regional identity into a broader hospitality business.
d6d3cb3a7eb33a63d4c8d6c8c3ef23f04d3ec1e4.translatedText: 對於鳳凰城的食客來說，在全國連鎖店和主廚驅動的獨立餐廳激烈競爭的市場中，這家餐廳的開業增加了另一個根植於當地的概念。對於當地供應商和附近企業來說，這也提醒人們，強大的亞利桑那州品牌正在繼續擴大其原始的足跡，並試圖將區域特徵轉變為更廣泛的酒店業務。

a31691ea40fbd4cb6dab56daf459b58fc5dc5547.sourceText: White Pocket is a unique and visually stunning geological formation located in the Vermilion Cliffs National Monument in northern Arizona . It is situated within the Paria Canyon-Vermilion Cliffs Wilderness, a protected area known for its rugged beauty and remarkable rock formations. The closest developed town is Page, Arizona, about an hour east of the trailhead.
a31691ea40fbd4cb6dab56daf459b58fc5dc5547.translatedText: 白口袋是位於亞利桑那州北部朱紅懸崖國家紀念碑的獨特且令人驚嘆的地質結構。它位於帕里亞峽谷-朱紅懸崖荒野內，該保護區以其崎嶇的美景和非凡的岩層而聞名。最近的已開發城鎮是亞利桑那州佩吉市，位於步道起點以東約一小時車程。

8d0db7e32a7b2d51c9f20e0df916d335968b87fb.sourceText: White Pocket is characterized by its swirling and intricate patterns of white and red Navajo sandstone, which have been sculpted over millions of years by the forces of wind and water erosion. The result is a mesmerizing landscape that resembles a frozen wave or a surreal painting. The rock formations at White Pocket often feature delicate, contorted layers, creating an otherworldly and dreamlike atmosphere.
8d0db7e32a7b2d51c9f20e0df916d335968b87fb.translatedText: White Pocket 的特點是其白色和紅色納瓦霍砂岩的旋轉和複雜圖案，這些圖案是數百萬年來風和水侵蝕的力量雕刻而成的。結果是令人著迷的風景，類似於凍結的波浪或超現實的繪畫。白袋的岩層往往具有細膩、扭曲的層次，營造出一種超凡脫俗、夢幻般的氛圍。

37380261f9efb2e29529b084e9fe29dca44a030d.sourceText: Due to its remote location, White Pocket sees fewer visitors compared to other famous landmarks in Arizona like the Grand Canyon or Antelope Canyon. This relative seclusion adds to the appeal for those seeking a quieter and more intimate outdoor experience.
37380261f9efb2e29529b084e9fe29dca44a030d.translatedText: 由於地處偏遠，與大峽谷或羚羊峽谷等亞利桑那州其他著名地標相比，白袋的遊客較少。這種相對僻靜的環境對那些尋求更安靜、更親密的戶外體驗的人來說更具吸引力。

737dc8669adacd3284114f954e4ebffe85be4d04.sourceText: Photographers and nature enthusiasts are particularly drawn to White Pocket for its unique and photogenic landscapes. The intricate patterns, textures, and vibrant colors of the sandstone formations provide endless opportunities for creative compositions. It is also a popular destination for hikers and backpackers who enjoy exploring the wilderness and the surrounding area.
737dc8669adacd3284114f954e4ebffe85be4d04.translatedText: 攝影師和自然愛好者特別喜歡白口袋，因為它獨特且上鏡的風景。砂岩地層的複雜圖案、紋理和鮮豔的色彩為創意作品提供了無限的機會。它也是喜歡探索荒野和周邊地區的徒步旅行者和背包客的熱門目的地。

33f7b3ce138783089deee30d8ddf0dc6ac3c3e87.sourceText: Access to White Pocket is challenging, as it is located in a remote and rugged area. The journey typically requires a four-wheel-drive vehicle and navigation skills, as the roads are unpaved and can be rough. Visitors are advised to come prepared with plenty of water, food, and fuel, as there are no facilities or services available.
33f7b3ce138783089deee30d8ddf0dc6ac3c3e87.translatedText: 進入 White Pocket 具有挑戰性，因為它位於偏遠且崎嶇的地區。由於道路未鋪砌且崎嶇不平，因此旅程通常需要四輪驅動車輛和導航技能。由於沒有任何設施或服務，建議遊客準備充足的水、食物和燃料。

944637aceb726a437a0630c8db20755b9b851226.sourceText: It is highly recommended that visitors plan their trip in advance and check the official website of the Bureau of Land Management for up-to-date information.
944637aceb726a437a0630c8db20755b9b851226.translatedText: 強烈建議遊客提前規劃行程，並查看土地管理局官方網站以了解最新資訊。

f509c193a536bde97320dd14a8ba9dd9241c42a0.sourceText: HGTV’s Hometown Kickstart has revealed the public project they have spent the last few months creating. The Art Car project can be seen along First Street in Winslow and features several classic cars turned works of art.
f509c193a536bde97320dd14a8ba9dd9241c42a0.translatedText: HGTV 的 Hometown Kickstart 公佈了他們過去幾個月創建的公共專案。沿著溫斯洛的第一街可以看到藝術車項目，其中有幾輛經典車變成了藝術品。

b2a544e6eafe62cd01453043da59773a2e3a9c64.sourceText: A stone pillar commemorates the surrender of the extraordinary Apache leader.
b2a544e6eafe62cd01453043da59773a2e3a9c64.translatedText: 一根石柱紀念這位非凡的阿帕奇領袖的投降。

4ee29702e732025aade6bf9948aa8cfb2a981c90.sourceText: On September 4, 1886, the Apache leader Geronimo and his band of followers surrendered to General Nelson Miles in Skeleton Canyon, Arizona . After years on the run and guerrilla warfare with both United States and Mexican soldiers, the formidable medicine man and war leader submitted to U.S. custody for the final time.
4ee29702e732025aade6bf9948aa8cfb2a981c90.translatedText: 1886 年 9 月 4 日，阿帕奇領袖傑羅尼莫和他的追隨者在亞利桑那州骷髏峽谷向納爾遜·邁爾斯將軍投降。經過多年的逃亡以及與美國和墨西哥士兵的遊擊戰，這位令人敬畏的醫生和戰爭領袖最後一次被美國拘留。

33885494035e207fdfb6a2c144499c1b907e780b.sourceText: Geronimo was born in June of 1829 near present-day Turkey Creek, New Mexico (at the time it was Mexico) into the Bedonkohe band of the Apache tribe. When Geronimo was 28 years old his camp was attacked by Mexican soldiers. He and most of the Apache men were away at the time and returned to see many of the women and children had been slaughtered, including Geronimo's mother, wife, and his three children. This massacre set him on a path of resistance against the colonizing forces that sought to control and oppress the Apache.
33885494035e207fdfb6a2c144499c1b907e780b.translatedText: 傑羅尼莫於 1829 年 6 月出生在現在的新墨西哥州土耳其溪附近（當時是墨西哥），出生於阿帕奇部落的貝東科希部落。傑羅尼莫 28 歲時，他的營地遭到墨西哥士兵的襲擊。他和大多數阿帕奇人當時不在，回來時看到許多婦女和兒童被屠殺，其中包括傑羅尼莫的母親、妻子和他的三個孩子。這次屠殺使他走上了反抗殖民勢力的道路，這些殖民勢力試圖控制和壓迫阿帕契人。

5d0432654b1a7d97aab6702683fbe5f8d923d2e7.sourceText: For several decades thereafter, Geronimo helped lead raids against incursions of settlers into traditional Apache lands. His guerrilla raids became notorious for their ferocity and efficiency, often successfully taking on units of soldiers much larger than his own. He frustrated pursuing armies by escaping seemingly hopeless situations and crossing back and forth across international borders to thwart his enemies. His exploits became the stuff of legend. According to one possibly apocryphal tale, American troops cornered Geronimo and his warriors, who then fled into a cave. The soldiers waited outside, ready to arrest or kill him and his men. But while the soldiers were waiting, they received reports that Geronimo and his band were spotted elsewhere. They searched the cave and found it empty. Bafflingly, it did not appear have another exit.
5d0432654b1a7d97aab6702683fbe5f8d923d2e7.translatedText: 此後的幾十年裡，傑羅尼莫幫助領導了針對定居者入侵阿帕契傳統土地的攻擊行動。他的遊擊襲擊因其兇猛和高效而臭名昭著，經常成功地對付比他自己大得多的士兵部隊。他透過逃離看似絕望的境地並穿越國際邊界來挫敗敵人，從而挫敗了追擊的軍隊。他的功績成為傳奇。根據一個可能是杜撰的故事，美國軍隊將傑羅尼莫和他的戰士們逼入絕境，然後他們逃進了一個山洞。士兵們在外面等候，準備逮捕或殺死他和他的部下。但當士兵們等待時，他們收到報告稱傑羅尼莫和他的樂隊在其他地方被發現。他們搜查了山洞，發現裡面空無一人。令人費解的是，它似乎沒有其他出口。

2280d91750915efb1b1c0684ea6e17d48684cab3.sourceText: Geronimo led three rebellions against the United States, recruiting Apaches who refused to continue living in restrictive reservations and wished to return to living in their former nomadic ways. The last of these rebellions began in 1885, when Geronimo and his recruits escaped from the San Carlos Reservation and into Mexico. On the run and running out of supplies, Geronimo was persuaded to surrender. He and his band camped out in Mexico and prepared to cross the border to surrender the next day. An American soldier who sold them whiskey warned them that the plan was to wipe them out as soon as they crossed into the United States. Once again, Geronimo and his men fled and evaded capture.
2280d91750915efb1b1c0684ea6e17d48684cab3.translatedText: 傑羅尼莫領導了三場針對美國的叛亂，招募了拒絕繼續生活在限制性保留地並希望恢復以前游牧生活方式的阿帕奇人。最後一次叛亂始於 1885 年，當時傑羅尼莫和他的新兵逃離聖卡洛斯保留地並進入墨西哥。在逃跑和補給耗盡的過程中，傑羅尼莫被說服投降。他和他的樂隊在墨西哥露營，準備第二天越過邊境投降。一名向他們出售威士忌的美國士兵警告他們，計劃是在他們進入美國後立即消滅他們。傑羅尼莫和他的部下再次逃跑並逃脫了追捕。

30fd23f6f4fc4d35a410671dcab2f3685fcda055.sourceText: A few months later, Geronimo and his group were again tracked down and a U.S. soldier he respected was sent to talk with him. Captain Henry Lawton spoke the Apache language and respected their culture and customs. Geronimo allegedly saw Lawton as a formidable and honorable opponent whose word was trusted more than most soldiers. Lawton was able to convince Geronimo to surrender again, and that he and his band would not be attacked if he agreed to do so. Lawton then escorted Geronimo and his followers to Skeleton Canyon where General Miles was camped.
30fd23f6f4fc4d35a410671dcab2f3685fcda055.translatedText: 幾個月後，傑羅尼莫和他的團隊再次被追踪，並派了一名他尊敬的美國士兵與他交談。亨利·勞頓上尉講阿帕奇語，並尊重他們的文化和習俗。據稱，傑羅尼莫將勞頓視為一個令人畏懼且值得尊敬的對手，他的話比大多數士兵更值得信賴。勞頓說服傑羅尼莫再次投降，並且如果他同意的話，他和他的團隊就不會受到攻擊。隨後，勞頓護送傑羅尼莫和他的追隨者前往邁爾斯將軍駐紮的骷髏峽谷。

6119657287654cce5057d100aca9a9e9d8641e19.sourceText: Geronimo spent the rest of his life as a prisoner of war. The territory of Arizona wished to have him tried and executed for his many decades of guerrilla warfare, so in order to prevent that the U.S. Army had him and his family transferred to military bases in Florida. There, a group of businessmen convinced military authorities to allow them to display Geronimo in his prison cell as a tourist attraction.
6119657287654cce5057d100aca9a9e9d8641e19.translatedText: 傑羅尼莫以戰俘的身份度過了餘生。亞利桑那州領地希望對他數十年的遊擊戰進行審判和處決，因此為了防止美軍將他和他的家人轉移到佛羅裡達州的軍事基地。在那裡，一群商人說服軍事當局允許他們將傑羅尼莫的監獄牢房展示為旅遊景點。

6a2a45d8591b8ebeed119f9301d7f643c51a3730.sourceText: In a remote corner of Arizona at the end of a dusty dirt road lies a collection of crumbling adobe walls. A few stone brick buildings bake in the desert heat. An American flag waving high on a pole is the only hint of active human presence. While it may not look like much now, this was once home to the fourth-largest community in Arizona, and one of the most important forts in the western frontier.
6a2a45d8591b8ebeed119f9301d7f643c51a3730.translatedText: 在亞利桑那州的一個偏遠角落，在一條塵土飛揚的土路盡頭，矗立著一堆搖搖欲墜的土磚牆。一些石磚建築在沙漠的炎熱中烘烤。桿子上高高飄揚的美國國旗是人類活躍的唯一跡象。雖然現在看起來可能不太像，但這裡曾經是亞利桑那州第四大社區的所在地，也是西部邊境最重要的堡壘之一。

7ac007ffdffa78b9fb36d123d1bad15f185a4f19.sourceText: Throughout the late 1800s, Fort Bowie was the main staging point for the United States Army’s conflicts with the Chiricahua Apache, led by figures such as Cochise and Geronimo. US forces engaged with the Apache throughout the region, including the Battle of Apache Pass, which is located inside the park. These conflicts were not limited to fighting men, atrocities against civilian targets were committed on both sides. On September 5, 1886, Geronimo gave his final surrender. He was held at Fort Bowie for a time before being sent to prison in Florida.
7ac007ffdffa78b9fb36d123d1bad15f185a4f19.translatedText: 在整個 1800 年代末，鮑伊堡是美國陸軍與科奇斯和傑羅尼莫等人物領導的奇里卡瓦阿帕奇人衝突的主要集結地。美軍在整個地區與阿帕契作戰，包括位於公園內的阿帕契山口戰役。這些衝突不僅限於戰鬥人員，雙方都對平民目標實施了暴行。 1886 年 9 月 5 日，傑羅尼莫最後投降。他在鮑伊堡被關了一段時間，然後被送往佛羅裡達州的監獄。

225f018fc19a4c529fa51f2530d5962e8ec22c52.sourceText: At the end of its days, Fort Bowie was much more relaxed. Cottonwood trees were planted along the streets. The fort sported a tennis court, plumbing, and an ice machine. For eight years, life continued at this leisurely pace until 1894, when the remaining troops were reassigned to Fort Logan in Colorado. The adobe walls soon collapsed, leaving only a decaying reminder of the days when the West was a constant battlefield.
225f018fc19a4c529fa51f2530d5962e8ec22c52.translatedText: 在日子結束時，鮑伊堡輕鬆多了。街道兩旁種植了三葉楊樹。堡壘裡有網球場、管線系統和製冰機。八年來，這種悠閒的生活一直持續到 1894 年，當時剩餘的部隊被重新分配到科羅拉多州的洛根堡。土坯牆很快就倒塌了，只剩下腐爛的痕跡，讓人回想起西部戰場不斷的日子。

d87c3557b053a2b358458f198092dfc9ae159f21.sourceText: Fort Bowie is rather far from civilization. You’ll be fifteen miles from the nearest gas station, and out of cell service range. There is a water spigot by the ranger station, so be sure to fill up while you’re there!
d87c3557b053a2b358458f198092dfc9ae159f21.translatedText: 鮑伊堡距離文明社會相當遙遠。您距離最近的加油站有十五英里，並且超出了手機服務範圍。護林站旁邊有一個水龍頭，所以一定要在到達時加滿水！

d2e1c136afd5e3a348de591ed7ff76599c719828.sourceText: The Museum Club, known locally as "The Zoo", is a Route 66 icon. It began as a taxidermy museum/shop in 1931 when taxidermist Dean Eldredge purchased federal land just outside Flagstaff , Arizona . He constructed what he believed was "the largest log cabin in the nation." The upper floor and roof are supported by several massive tree trunks and the doorway is under an arch constructed from the crook of a large tree. The building is designated as a Historic Landmark.
d2e1c136afd5e3a348de591ed7ff76599c719828.translatedText: 博物館俱樂部，在當地被稱為“動物園”，是 66 號公路的標誌。 1931 年，動物標本剝制師 Dean Eldredge 在亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫郊外購買了聯邦土地，最初是一家動物標本剝制博物館/商店。他建造了他認為是“全國最大的小木屋”。上層和屋頂由幾根巨大的樹幹支撐，門口位於一棵大樹的彎曲處建造的拱門下方。該建築被指定為歷史地標。

cfb3a193249d7c4eddfc79a05cd2f9f1362207f3.sourceText: Unfortunately, Dean passed in 1936 and most of his collection was sold. The building was purchased by a local saddle maker who took advantage of its proximity to Route 66 and opened a nightclub.
cfb3a193249d7c4eddfc79a05cd2f9f1362207f3.translatedText: 不幸的是，迪恩於 1936 年去世，他的大部分藏品都被出售。該建築被當地一家馬鞍製造商買下，利用其靠近 66 號公路的優勢，開設了一家夜總會。

8a281db978cfc36964f1ba01f3bee9ef4a120ee4.sourceText: Over the years, the nightclub passed through several owners. By the 1950s, the building had become somewhat run down and was commonly associated with late-night brawls.
8a281db978cfc36964f1ba01f3bee9ef4a120ee4.translatedText: 這些年來，這家夜總會幾經易主。到了 1950 年代，這棟建築已經有些破舊，經常與深夜鬥毆聯繫在一起。

6565e67cdd4780cf8ad6a658248b5dc2e9115824.sourceText: " The Zoo" nickname arose because of all the fighting that took place at the club. The alternative origin of the name dates back to its days as a taxidermy museum.
6565e67cdd4780cf8ad6a658248b5dc2e9115824.translatedText: 由於俱樂部發生的所有打架事件，「動物園」的綽號出現了。這個名字的另一個起源可以追溯到它作為動物標本博物館的時代。

5bc870cecdd0273932e0963331c5525776de873b.sourceText: In 1963, guitarist Don Scott bought the club and converted it to a country music venue. Scott had many contacts in the industry and was able to attract some excellent acts.
5bc870cecdd0273932e0963331c5525776de873b.translatedText: 1963 年，吉他手 Don Scott 買下了這個俱樂部，並將其改造成一個鄉村音樂場所。斯科特在業內有很多人脈，能夠吸引一些優秀的表演者。

ce4efec78c0a4450d9073622164e6a347ea64838.sourceText: The Museum Club continues to be a popular country music honky-tonk, with a legendary happy hour. The neon guitar sign at the side of the road has become an icon of Route 66. The menu items for lunch and dinner often carry the names of famous country music stars.
ce4efec78c0a4450d9073622164e6a347ea64838.translatedText: 博物館俱樂部仍然是一個流行的鄉村音樂酒吧，擁有傳奇的歡樂時光。路邊的霓虹吉他標誌已成為 66 號公路的標誌。午餐和晚餐的菜單上經常印有著名鄉村音樂明星的名字。

65dcdd39f98593c0168320f85e69f0182b301228.sourceText: Deep in Oak Creek Canyon, a trail meanders among the crumbling remains of some stone buildings. Mostly forgotten and partially consumed by vegetation, these former buildings were the home to some unusual occupants and visitors.
65dcdd39f98593c0168320f85e69f0182b301228.translatedText: 在橡樹溪峽谷深處，一條小路蜿蜒在一些石頭建築的搖搖欲墜的遺跡中。這些以前的建築大多已被遺忘，部分被植被所吞噬，但它們是一些不尋常的居住者和遊客的家。

d04187db74a021e0791fc2673e54716a823d8c5c.sourceText: In the 1870s, before there was even a road through the canyon, Jesse Jefferson “Bear” Howard constructed the first cabin on the site. Howard was a hunter who moved to the area to settle a score with the local wildlife. His friend was mauled to death by a bear in the canyon and Howard vowed to kill every bear in the region in retaliation.
d04187db74a021e0791fc2673e54716a823d8c5c.translatedText: 在 1870 年代，在穿過峽谷的道路還沒有出現之前，傑西·傑斐遜“熊”霍華德在此建造了第一座小屋。霍華德是一名獵人，他搬到該地區是為了與當地野生動物算帳。他的朋友在峽谷中被熊咬死，霍華德發誓要殺死該地區的每一頭熊以示報復。

47654853fa1cb940a34cb526f6f92e25f39fdf8f.sourceText: A legendary figure in the early days of Flagstaff , Arizona 's settlement, Howard was said to have stood 6-foot-4-inches tall and frequently hunted his quarry armed with just a knife. Mostly reclusive, he only went into town to sell his bear meat to butchers, restaurants, and encampments of railroad workers. Thankfully, Howard was unsuccessful in exterminating bears from the local ecosystem, though he reportedly kept up this profession until he was 90 years old.
47654853fa1cb940a34cb526f6f92e25f39fdf8f.translatedText: 霍華德是亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫定居點早期的傳奇人物，據說身高 6 英尺 4 英寸，經常隻手持一把刀狩獵他的獵物。他大多與世隔絕，只進城把熊肉賣給屠夫、餐廳和鐵路工人的營地。值得慶幸的是，霍華德在消滅當地生態系統中的熊方面並沒有成功，儘管據報道他一直從事這一職業直到 90 歲。

596bdd65dc594225fe7a16518772570b8b89c2e0.sourceText: The next inhabitants of the cabin were the Thomas family, who engaged in somewhat less violent pursuits. They expanded the cabin, added some other structures to the property, and planted an apple orchard. It was during this time that famed Western novelist Zane Grey visited and was so inspired by the area that he set his novel, The Call of the Canyon at the location.
596bdd65dc594225fe7a16518772570b8b89c2e0.translatedText: 小屋的下一個居民是托馬斯一家，他們從事的暴力活動稍微少一些。他們擴建了小屋，增加了一些其他建築，並種植了一個蘋果園。正是在這段時間，著名的西方小說家贊恩‧格雷來到了這裡，並受到了這裡的啟發，他的小說《峽谷的呼喚》就以此為背景。

431ecbb5ff975a026ea7016c735bf1b99ba81006.sourceText: Grey's novel was adapted into a silent movie that was filmed around the area. The production team hired local photographer Carl Mayhew to help with the project. He was so enchanted by the cabin and its surroundings that he purchased the property in 1923. Mayhew spent the next few years renovating and expanding the cabins and opened the Mayhew Lodge in 1926. It acted as a bed and breakfast for passersby and tourists. Over the subsequent decades, notable guests at the cabin included former President Herbert Hoover and Hollywood figures Walt Disney, Clark Gable, and Jimmy Stewart.
431ecbb5ff975a026ea7016c735bf1b99ba81006.translatedText: 格雷的小說被改編成一部無聲電影，並在該地區拍攝。製作團隊聘請了當地攝影師 Carl Mayhew 來幫助這個專案。他對小屋及其周圍環境非常著迷，因此於 1923 年購買了這處房產。梅休在接下來的幾年裡對小屋進行了翻修和擴建，並於 1926 年開設了梅休旅館。它為路人和遊客提供住宿加早餐。在接下來的幾十年裡，小屋的著名客人包括前總統赫伯特·胡佛和好萊塢明星沃爾特·迪士尼、克拉克·蓋博和吉米·斯圖爾特。

f77ed67d6446ba837daf467f85a4f6d9a8520dad.sourceText: In 1968, the lodge closed and the Mayhew family sold the property to be added to the adjacent Coconino National Forest. In 1980, a wildfire severely damaged the cabin complex, leaving for the most part only a scattering of foundations and walls, a chicken coop, and a recess dug into the canyon cliff likely used for food storage.
f77ed67d6446ba837daf467f85a4f6d9a8520dad.translatedText: 1968 年，小屋關閉，梅休家族出售了該地產，並添加到了鄰近的可科尼諾國家森林。 1980 年，一場野火嚴重損壞了小屋建築群，大部分只剩下零散的地基和牆壁、雞舍以及在峽谷懸崖上挖出的一個凹處，可能用於儲存食物。

c75aa90481746e1bc48c2ab810ea6b044c3e1888.sourceText: When it was built in 1929, this historic bridge was the only place to cross the Colorado River for 600 miles.
c75aa90481746e1bc48c2ab810ea6b044c3e1888.translatedText: 這座歷史悠久的橋樑建於 1929 年，是唯一一座橫跨 600 英里科羅拉多河的地方。

2749fd2542dcb12e3aa3afc53ad605566f453695.sourceText: The beauty of the Colorado River was captivating to early explorers as its green-blue waters wound through the dramatic red canyons of northern Arizona . As a vital source of water in a rugged and desolate landscape in which few things could survive, the river seemed like a gift aiding their exploration—until they tried to cross it. It turns out there is only one place in hundreds of miles from which the river can be easily accessed from both sides, making travel in that area extremely difficult.
2749fd2542dcb12e3aa3afc53ad605566f453695.translatedText: 科羅拉多河的美麗令早期的探險家著迷，因為它碧綠的河水蜿蜒穿過亞利桑那州北部引人注目的紅色峽谷。在這片崎嶇荒涼的土地上，幾乎沒有任何東西能夠生存，這條河作為重要的水源，似乎是幫助他們探索的禮物——直到他們試圖穿越它。事實證明，數百英里內只有一個地方可以從兩側輕鬆到達河流，這使得該地區的旅行變得極其困難。

93cbf80c19f38666ed3e268c7aee0dce3c3eb915.sourceText: Prior to the completion of the Navajo Bridge in 1929, travelers between Utah and Arizona had to cross using Lee’s Ferry river crossing. Several months prior to the bridge’s completion the ferry sank in an accident, killing three men. Until the bridge was completed, there was no direct route between Utah and Arizona and travelers had to trek hundreds of miles around the canyon to cross the Colorado River.
93cbf80c19f38666ed3e268c7aee0dce3c3eb915.translatedText: 在 1929 年納瓦荷大橋完工之前，猶他州和亞利桑那州之間的旅客必須使用李氏費里河渡口。大橋完工前幾個月，渡輪在一次意外中沉沒，造成三人死亡。在大橋建成之前，猶他州和亞利桑那州之間沒有直達路線，旅行者必須繞著峽谷跋涉數百英里才能穿越科羅拉多河。

f1392ca2ea4730a8c0f5e24566a55572c8dd8ddf.sourceText: When it was first built, Navajo Bridge was the only place to cross the Colorado River for 600 miles. The bridge was so significant that nearly 7,000 people in 1,217 automobiles attended the dedication ceremony. At the time it was the highest steel arch bridge in the world and quite the engineering marvel. Most importantly, it created a safe new travel route across the mighty Colorado River.
f1392ca2ea4730a8c0f5e24566a55572c8dd8ddf.translatedText: 納瓦荷大橋剛建成時，是全長 600 英哩的唯一跨越科羅拉多河的地方。這座橋意義重大，共有 1,217 輛汽車、近 7,000 人參加了落成典禮。當時它是世界上最高的鋼拱橋，堪稱工程奇蹟。最重要的是，它創造了一條橫跨浩瀚的科羅拉多河的安全新旅行路線。

0cbe7ef6aac8ae1ef4b7454080373227bae48fff.sourceText: As automobiles and trucks became larger and heavier it became apparent the bridge had not been built to accommodate the size of these vehicles and wasn’t adequate. A new bridge was built just downstream from the existing bridge and dedicated on September 14, 1995. The historic bridge was converted to a pedestrian crossing.
0cbe7ef6aac8ae1ef4b7454080373227bae48fff.translatedText: 隨著汽車和卡車變得越來越大、越來越重，很明顯這座橋的建造無法適應這些車輛的尺寸，而且還不夠。在現有橋樑的下游建造了一座新橋，並於 1995 年 9 月 14 日投入使用。這座歷史悠久的橋樑被改造成人行橫道。

c533834c01953f3c1e68221d40a40f830296d286.sourceText: California condors can sometimes be seen at Navajo Bridge in the early mornings. These majestic beauties are one of the world’s largest and rarest birds, and the largest flying land bird in North America, with a wingspan of 9-10 feet. The population in the Southwest was in serious decline by the early 1900s, with the last sighting of a wild condor in Arizona occurring in 1924. California condors were listed as endangered in 1967, and by 1982 the total population had dwindled to just 22 birds. The only hope to save these flying giants was to begin a captive breeding program and the last known wild California condor was captured as part of the program in 1987. The first captive California condors were released from the breeding program in California in 1992. In 1996 six captive California condors were released at the Vermilion Cliffs, not far from Navajo Bridge. As of December 2020, the total population had increased to 504, with 103 in Arizona.
c533834c01953f3c1e68221d40a40f830296d286.translatedText: 清晨，有時可以在納瓦荷橋上看到加州禿鷹。這些雄偉美麗的鳥類是世界上最大、最稀有的鳥類之一，也是北美最大的陸地飛行鳥類，翼展長達 9-10 英尺。到 1900 年代初，西南部的禿鷹數量嚴重下降，最後一次在亞利桑那州看到野生禿鷹是在 1924 年。加州禿鷹於 1967 年被列為瀕危物種，到 1982 年，總數量已減少至僅 22 隻。拯救這些飛行巨人的唯一希望是開始圈養繁殖計劃，最後一隻已知的野生加州禿鷹在 1987 年被捕獲，作為該計劃的一部分。第一批圈養加州禿鷹於 1992 年從加州的繁殖計畫中被釋放。 1996 年，六隻圈養加州禿鷹在距離納瓦霍橋不遠的朱紅懸崖被釋放。截至 2020 年 12 月，總人口已增至 504 人，其中亞利桑那州有 103 人。

c066c3bf7d77d6648ce68aff27e73f561e82e9e6.sourceText: Herb Applegate moved to Phoenix from Detroit in the 1960s. With a successful background in restaurant management, he quickly found investors in his newest venture: an affordable, family-friendly coffee shop and restaurant.
c066c3bf7d77d6648ce68aff27e73f561e82e9e6.translatedText: 赫伯·阿普爾蓋特 (Herb Applegate) 於 20 世紀 60 年代從底特律搬到菲尼克斯。憑藉在餐廳管理方面的成功背景，他很快就為自己的最新事業找到了投資者：一家經濟實惠、適合家庭的咖啡店和餐廳。

873f589c27754b30f0f5bc4353c1b429584fd340.sourceText: Hobo Joe's Coffee Shops were represented by an eponymous mascot who was meant to be a mixture of urbane sophistication and lovable tramp. Described in ad copy as a "World Traveler, Philosopher, and Connoisseur of Good Food," he was meant to evoke refined taste and thriftiness. Although he wore dilapidated shoes and a rope belt he also carried a copy of the Wall Street Journal and a key denoting membership in the Phi Beta Kappa honor society. One Hobo Joe's Coffee Shop featured a 22-foot-tall statue of Hobo Joe, whereas other locations had smaller versions.
873f589c27754b30f0f5bc4353c1b429584fd340.translatedText: Hobo Joe's 咖啡店以同名吉祥物為代表，該吉祥物是文雅精緻和可愛流浪漢的混合體。廣告文案將他描述為“世界旅行者、哲學家和美食鑑賞家”，旨在喚起人們高雅的品味和節儉的精神。儘管他穿著破舊的鞋子，繫著繩帶，但他還帶著一份《華爾街日報》和一把鑰匙，表明他是美國大學優等生榮譽協會的成員。一家 Hobo Joe's 咖啡店設有 22 英尺高的 Hobo Joe 雕像，而其他地點則有較小的版本。

0668c88b58e23d23c6651b279ebd136a7a42aa7d.sourceText: Hobo Joe's Coffee Shops took off quickly in the Phoenix area. In only a few years, there were at least half a dozen locations with further regional expansions planned. But despite this apparent success, there were deep problems behind the scenes. According to local reporters , Herb Applegate apparently lived a double-life, embezzling over a million dollars out of the business to fund an extravagant lifestyle that included a mansion with a light-up waterfall and mistresses. Additionally, he was unofficially suspected of involvement in a deadly shooting in Las Vegas.
0668c88b58e23d23c6651b279ebd136a7a42aa7d.translatedText: Hobo Joe's 咖啡店在鳳凰城地區迅速崛起。在短短幾年內，至少有六個地點計劃進一步進行區域擴張。但儘管取得了表面上的成功，幕後卻存在著深層的問題。據當地記者報道，赫伯·阿普爾蓋特顯然過著雙重生活，他從生意中挪用了超過一百萬美元，以資助奢侈的生活方式，其中包括一座帶有發光瀑布的豪宅和情婦。此外，他還被非正式地懷疑參與了拉斯維加斯的致命槍擊事件。

40b275a7c7e53ad3ff670740785efada250228c5.sourceText: Applegate sold Hobo Joe's in the early 1970s and the chain died out by the 1980s. Applegate himself passed away in 1974. By that point, investigative reporter Don Bolles had begun digging into political and financial corruption in Arizona and had suspicions about Hobo Joe's, its founder, and its possible connections to organized crime. Bolles had uncovered personal and financial ties between Herb Applegate and members of the Detroit mafia. Unfortunately, on June 2, 1976, Bolles was murdered via a remote-controlled bomb attached to his car, hindering his many investigations into corruption across Arizona.
40b275a7c7e53ad3ff670740785efada250228c5.translatedText: Applegate 在 1970 年代初期出售了 Hobo Joe's，該連鎖店到了 1980 年代就停業了。阿普爾蓋特本人於 1974 年去世。此時，調查記者唐·博爾斯 (Don Bolles) 開始深入調查亞利桑那州的政治和金融腐敗，並對 Hobo Joe's 的創始人及其與有組織犯罪的可能聯繫產生懷疑。博爾斯揭露了赫伯·阿普爾蓋特與底特律黑手黨成員之間的個人和財務關係。不幸的是，1976 年 6 月 2 日，博爾斯被安裝在汽車上的遙控炸彈殺害，這阻礙了他對亞利桑那州各地腐敗問題的多項調查。

7626efe778aaf78dae00be6ae8e54ea3d13564fa.sourceText: The story of Hobo Joe's is filled with mystery, and the statue that stands in Buckeye, Arizona, is no different. Applegate's widow swears this giant statue is not an authentic Hobo Joe's mascot. In an article on AZ Central , writer David Madrid presents several theories, including one that suggests the statue was created for a Hobo Joe's branch that never came to fruition. According to this theory, the artist was never paid for his work and kept the massive mascot for himself, eventually gifting it to a friend who erected it outside a slaughterhouse in Buckeye.
7626efe778aaf78dae00be6ae8e54ea3d13564fa.translatedText: 流浪漢喬的故事充滿神秘色彩，矗立在亞利桑那州巴克艾的雕像也不例外。阿普爾蓋特的遺孀發誓這座巨大的雕像不是真正的流浪漢喬的吉祥物。在 AZ Central 的一篇文章中，作家大衛馬德里提出了幾種理論，其中一種認為這座雕像是為流浪漢喬的分支創建的，但從未實現。根據這個理論，藝術家從未為自己的作品獲得報酬，並為自己保留了這個巨大的吉祥物，最終將其贈送給了一位朋友，後者將其豎立在七葉樹的一家屠宰場外。

d8c6f60679f7e0b1afd6a501348e692b5061091c.sourceText: Authentic or not, the giant Hobo Joe stood outside the slaughterhouse for several decades, becoming a local icon long after the original Hobo Joe restaurant brand had mostly been forgotten. When the statue had become worn and faded, a local campaign raised enough money to fund the statue's refurbishment and move to a more central location in town. In 2020, that project was completed and the restored Hobo Joe now stands on a pedestal, surveying the downtown area.
d8c6f60679f7e0b1afd6a501348e692b5061091c.translatedText: 無論真假，巨大的 Hobo Joe 餐廳在屠宰場外矗立了幾十年，在最初的 Hobo Joe 餐廳品牌幾乎被遺忘很久之後，它就成為了當地的標誌。當雕像磨損和褪色時，當地的一項活動籌集了足夠的資金來翻新雕像並搬到鎮上更中心的位置。 2020 年，該項目完成，修復後的 Hobo Joe 現在矗立在基座上，俯瞰著市中心地區。

5a91c50290d1f286cc25b96a1a44eaeb7b090dd3.sourceText: Named for the elephant-like entrance to one of the structures, Elipante is a bizzare sculptural home built starting in 1979 by an artist couple, and was the first of several mixed media structures now housed on three acres of land in Cornville, Arizona. The structures were created with found materials over a period of 28 years by artist Michael Kahn and his wife Leda Livant.
5a91c50290d1f286cc25b96a1a44eaeb7b090dd3.translatedText: Elipante 因其建築中大象般的入口而得名，是一座奇特的雕塑住宅，由一對藝術家夫婦於 1979 年開始建造，是目前位於亞利桑那州康維爾佔地三英畝的幾座混合媒體建築中的第一座。這些結構是由藝術家 Michael Kahn 和他的妻子 Leda Livant 在 28 年間用發現的材料建造而成。

a65e92a750e0b3662703bdb1eec9f02189bffcd0.sourceText: Eliphante is one of the wackier examples of outsider architecture, and is listed as a part of the Smithsonian's SOS initiative (Save Outdoor Sculptures). Eliphante been visited by thousands over the years.
a65e92a750e0b3662703bdb1eec9f02189bffcd0.translatedText: Eliphante 是外來建築中比較古怪的例子之一，並被列為史密森學會 SOS 計劃（拯救戶外雕塑）的一部分。多年來，埃利芬特 (Eliphante) 已有數千人參觀過。

118e79d345ceaa17dd59a42d141166314b6d31a9.sourceText: Update March, 2018: Eliphante is a private residence and is closed to the public.
118e79d345ceaa17dd59a42d141166314b6d31a9.translatedText: 2018 年 3 月更新：Eliphante 是一處私人住宅，不對外開放。

4be5c803bc832dee8ec515dcc2988d880272f9df.sourceText: Slightly off the beaten path of Sedona's busy areas lies this park. Established in 2004, the park is a favorite of those seeking to tap into their spirituality, or who wish to have a quiet place to reflect in a beautiful setting. People of all faiths are welcome. The park offers a 36-foot stupa (Amitabha, the site's namesake) and a smaller stupa where visitors can pray, meditate, or just enjoy a sense of peace.
4be5c803bc832dee8ec515dcc2988d880272f9df.translatedText: 這個公園位於塞多納繁忙地區的人跡罕至的地方。公園成立於 2004 年，是那些尋求挖掘靈性或希望有一個安靜的地方在美麗的環境中沉思的人的最愛。歡迎各種信仰的人。公園內有一座 36 英尺高的佛塔（阿彌陀佛，該地的同名佛塔）和一座較小的佛塔，遊客可以在那裡祈禱、冥想或只是享受平靜的感覺。

822e224c09fd1834cf0ad9802d8c72a78e5497d4.sourceText: A stupa is considered a living presence of Buddha, and as such, many people bring a small offering to place at the foot of the stupa. There are few stupas in the United States and this is the only one located in Arizona .
822e224c09fd1834cf0ad9802d8c72a78e5497d4.translatedText: 佛塔被認為是佛陀的活生生的存在，因此，許多人會在佛塔腳下放置一些小祭品。美國很少有佛塔，這是唯一一座位於亞利桑那州的佛塔。

7f60651b251e0a172d6324e0c3017ba062bac071.sourceText: Park highlights include many areas adorned with prayer flags, wooden boards where visitors can sit and meditate, benches, a medicine wheel, and a stunning wooden statue of Buddha overlooking the Amitabha Stupa. The park has no paved trails, but it is an easy walk/hike throughout for people of all ages. Admission is free, however, donations are accepted.
7f60651b251e0a172d6324e0c3017ba062bac071.translatedText: 公園的亮點包括許多裝飾著經幡的區域、遊客可以坐下來冥想的木板、長凳、藥輪，以及俯瞰阿彌陀佛塔的令人驚嘆的木製佛像。公園沒有鋪砌的小徑，但適合所有年齡段的人輕鬆步行/徒步旅行。入場免費，但接受捐款。

1a429b62f422bd5abbc8436e7a9b3ac53af59ecd.sourceText: The park is located at the base of Thunder Mountain and overlooks Sedona proper, offering a beautiful and largely unobstructed view of several of Sedona's stunning red rock mountains.
1a429b62f422bd5abbc8436e7a9b3ac53af59ecd.translatedText: 公園位於雷霆山腳下，俯瞰塞多納市區，可以一覽無餘地欣賞塞多納幾座令人驚嘆的紅色岩石山脈的美麗景色。

3451db6219752205c7a372ad5a428c404fe18e65.sourceText: The universe is vast and full of mysteries. Though we still have a long way to go, over time and with careful observation, many once-mysterious phenomena have been observed and understood. These days, many of those observations and discoveries are made possible by teams of scientists with access to large collections of instruments. But until not too long ago, a single person with a single telescope could discover a whole new planet... or a dwarf planet.
3451db6219752205c7a372ad5a428c404fe18e65.translatedText: 宇宙浩瀚充滿奧秘。儘管我們還有很長的路要走，但隨著時間的推移和仔細的觀察，許多曾經神秘的現像已經被觀察到並被理解。如今，許多觀察和發現都是由擁有大量儀器的科學家團隊實現的。但直到不久之前，一個人用望遠鏡就可以發現一顆全新的行星……或是一顆矮行星。

175b63bb6991a9080b345f3bc555462e1f25cf61.sourceText: The Pluto Discovery Telescope is an honorary member of an exclusive club of telescopes used to discover planets, since at that time Pluto was considered a planet. The other two members are the 40-foot telescope that William Herschel used for the first observation of Uranus in 1781, and the Fraunhofer Refractor that Johann Gottfried Galle used for the first observation of Neptune in 1846.
175b63bb6991a9080b345f3bc555462e1f25cf61.translatedText: 冥王星發現望遠鏡是用來發現行星的望遠鏡俱樂部的榮譽成員，因為當時冥王星被認為是一顆行星。另外兩位成員是威廉·赫歇爾 (William Herschel) 在 1781 年首次觀測天王星時使用的 40 英尺望遠鏡，以及約翰·戈特弗里德·加勒 (Johann Gottfried Galle) 在 1846 年首次觀測海王星時使用的弗勞恩霍夫折射儀。

afd6bfbf630313c5ad080fb335a6ffcf48fc8ad7.sourceText: A number of astronomers theorized that another planet might exist beyond Uranus, but Percival Lowell was especially convinced. In 1894, he founded the Lowell Observatory , where he dedicated the final years of his life to the search for "Planet X." Unfortunately when he died in 1916, the hypothetical planet was still undiscovered.
afd6bfbf630313c5ad080fb335a6ffcf48fc8ad7.translatedText: 許多天文學家推測天王星之外可能存在另一顆行星，但 Percival Lowell 尤其確信這一點。 1894年，他創立了洛威爾天文台，並在那裡將生命的最後幾年奉獻給了尋找「X行星」。不幸的是，當他於 1916 年去世時，這顆假想的行星仍未被發現。

3ebedcec4bdad9a3871cd9482f769ecda0887ca4.sourceText: More than a decade later, Percival's nephew Roger Lowell Putnam had taken over the observatory and Percival's hunt for Planet X. With $10,000 from Abbott Lawrence Lowell, Percival’s younger brother he built a new telescope. Built in 1928-1929, the Lawrence Lowell Telescope is a 13-inch photographic instrument known as an astrograph. It had an unusual design compared to other telescopes of that time, because it was built specifically as a planet hunter. It has three lenses, which could focus light from distant objects in space onto a glass photographic plate. The design had a large field of view that is more common for survey telescopes these days, but was a bit of an oddity a century ago.
3ebedcec4bdad9a3871cd9482f769ecda0887ca4.translatedText: 十多年後，珀西瓦爾的侄子羅傑·洛厄爾·帕特南 (Roger Lowell Putnam) 接管了天文台，並接管了珀西瓦爾對 X 行星的搜尋。珀西瓦爾的弟弟阿伯特·勞倫斯·洛厄爾 (Abbott Lawrence Lowell) 為他提供了 10,000 美元，並建造了一架新望遠鏡。勞倫斯·洛厄爾望遠鏡建於 1928 年至 1929 年，是一種 13 英寸的攝影儀器，也被稱為占星儀。與當時的其他望遠鏡相比，它的設計很不尋常，因為它是專門為行星獵人而建造的。它具有三個鏡頭，可以將來自太空中遙遠物體的光線聚焦到玻璃照相板上。設計具有大視野，這在如今的巡天望遠鏡中更為常見，但在一個世紀前卻顯得有些奇怪。

3f182287449a9cf694da6ff6c6819cc51406d410.sourceText: Not long after the telescope was built, on February 18, 1930, observatory assistant Clyde Tombaugh first identified the object that would later be named Pluto. Though Percival Lowell was not alive to witness the result of his life's work, he was commemorated in the creation of the Pluto symbol: ♇. The symbol combines the first two letters of the (dwarf) planet's name, as well as Percival Lowell's initials.
3f182287449a9cf694da6ff6c6819cc51406d410.translatedText: 望遠鏡建成後不久，即 1930 年 2 月 18 日，天文台助理克萊德·湯博 (Clyde Tombaugh) 首次發現了這個天體，後來將其命名為冥王星。儘管 Percival Lowell 未能在世親眼見證他畢生工作的成果，但冥王星符號 ♇ 的誕生仍對他進行了紀念。這個符號結合了（矮）行星名稱的前兩個字母，以及珀西瓦爾·洛厄爾的姓名首字母縮寫。

769245e5fff677bb5af40296df9ff607d0360f29.sourceText: Today, the telescope is no longer in active use, mainly because it relied on photographic plates to image the sky and does not have an actual eyepiece to allow anyone to look through it. This combined with its historical significance has made the staff at Lowell Observatory hesitant to modify it for current use, instead focusing on preservation.
769245e5fff677bb5af40296df9ff607d0360f29.translatedText: 如今，該望遠鏡已不再使用，主要是因為它依靠照相底片對天空進行成像，並且沒有實際的目鏡可供任何人觀看。再加上它的歷史意義，洛威爾天文台的工作人員猶豫是否要對其進行改造以供當前使用，而是將重點放在了保存上。

577f518fb275ca03d027dc3ae6284a1b378b72fc.sourceText: On July 14, 1882, a local laborer from Turkey Creek, Arizona , came across the body of a dead man sitting against a tree. A bullet wound pierced the man's temple and a revolver with one bullet missing was found dangling in his hand. The deceased was identified as Johnny Ringo, an infamous criminal and vigilante.
577f518fb275ca03d027dc3ae6284a1b378b72fc.translatedText: 1882 年 7 月 14 日，亞利桑那州土耳其溪的一名當地工人發現一具靠在樹上的屍體。這名男子的太陽穴有槍傷，他的手上還掛著一把少了一顆子彈的左輪手槍。死者被確認為約翰尼林戈 (Johnny Ringo)，一名臭名昭著的罪犯和義務警員。

396a96bd2184b0a82a7291fe2482f46ac29f1db1.sourceText: His death was ruled a suicide and he was buried where his body was found. Upon learning of his death, the Tombstone Epitaph published that, "Many friends will mourn him. And many others will take secret delight in learning of his death." Many have also questioned the circumstances of his demise.
396a96bd2184b0a82a7291fe2482f46ac29f1db1.translatedText: 他的死亡被裁定為自殺，並被埋葬在屍體被發現的地方。得知他的死訊後，墓碑墓誌銘上寫道：「許多朋友會哀悼他。還有許多人會因為得知他的死而暗自高興。」許多人也質疑他的死亡原因。

9da0dd076bde1ba4152bf7e78d63c1e5ad971677.sourceText: To understand the uncertainty around his death, you must first understand his tumultuous life. Ringo was born on May 3, 1850 in Greens Fork, Indiana , although his family moved frequently in his youth. In Wyoming , when he was 14 years old and his family was emigrating from Missouri to California , his father accidentally shot himself and died. Still, the family continued their journey to California, where Ringo spent the rest of his childhood.
9da0dd076bde1ba4152bf7e78d63c1e5ad971677.translatedText: 要了解他死亡的不確定性，你必須先了解他動盪的一生。林戈於 1850 年 5 月 3 日出生於印第安納州格林福克，儘管他的家人在他年輕時經常搬家。在懷俄明州，當他14歲的時候，他的家人從密蘇裡州移民到加州，他的父親意外開槍自殺。儘管如此，一家人還是繼續前往加州，林戈在那裡度過了餘下的童年。

8a6c5de3514a0c7820e92a31f263652ccd7be49d.sourceText: Ringo moved to Mason County, Texas , in the 1870s. There, he befriended a former Texas Ranger who mentored Johnny in gunfighting and with whom he participated in several conflicts between factions of ranchers and rustlers as a vigilante. During this period, he was arrested and charged with murder but either escaped or was acquitted (the official court records are missing). Ringo, who counted John Wesley Hardin as one his colleagues, was not a typical outlaw. While he had limited education, he enjoyed quoting Shakespeare.
8a6c5de3514a0c7820e92a31f263652ccd7be49d.translatedText: 林戈於 1870 年代搬到德克薩斯州梅森縣。在那裡，他結識了一位前德克薩斯遊騎兵，後者指導約翰尼進行槍戰，並作為義務警員與約翰尼一起參與了牧場主和竊賊派系之間的幾場衝突。在此期間，他被捕並被指控犯有謀殺罪，但要么逃脫，要么被無罪釋放（官方法庭記錄丟失）。林戈將約翰·韋斯利·哈丁視為他的同事之一，他並不是典型的亡命之徒。雖然他受的教育有限，但他喜歡引用莎士比亞的話。

658e3cd7fb92fa3488d748f6ffee5a1f130bbd7b.sourceText: History first records Ringo being in Arizona in 1879, where at a saloon in Safford he bought a fellow customer a shot of whiskey. The man refused, saying that he preferred beer. Ringo shot the man in the gut, but he survived. Ringo then made his way to the mining boomtown of Tombstone , where he began rustling cattle and associating with a local gang known as the Cowboys.
658e3cd7fb92fa3488d748f6ffee5a1f130bbd7b.translatedText: 歷史首次記錄林戈於 1879 年在亞利桑那州，在薩福德的一家酒館裡，他買了一杯威士忌給一位顧客。男子拒絕了，說他更喜歡啤酒。林戈開槍射中男子的腹部，但他倖存下來。隨後，林戈前往礦業新興城鎮墓碑鎮，在那裡他開始偷牛，並與當地一個名為「牛仔」的幫派交往。

6cb10c44e719e76d8c350b5c898e0768e8eecd22.sourceText: During his time in Tombstone, he developed rivalries with lawmen and gunfighters Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday. In several interviews later in his life, Earp seems to take credit for Ringo’s death. However, according to other sources, Earp had already left Arizona and was in Colorado at the time of the shooting. It has also been alleged that Holliday killed him, which was portrayed in the blockbuster 1993 movie Tombstone . The majority of the evidence, however, seems to support the original conclusion that Ringo died by suicide.
6cb10c44e719e76d8c350b5c898e0768e8eecd22.translatedText: 在墓碑鎮期間，他與執法人員和槍手懷亞特·厄普和霍利迪醫生展開了競爭。在厄普晚年的幾次訪談中，他似乎將林戈的死歸功於自己。然而，根據其他消息來源，厄普在槍擊事件發生時已經離開亞利桑那州並在科羅拉多州。也有人指控霍利迪殺了他，這點在 1993 年賣座電影《墓碑》中有所描述。然而，大多數證據似乎都支持林戈自殺身亡的最初結論。

5e93bb45be2d01cac1741182c9567e116adf9fff.sourceText: As networks of railroads spread across the United States , engineers were also busy building thousands of dams. Steam locomotives required large amounts of water, and in areas of the arid west, that was often hard to come by. Thus, reservoirs were constructed adjacent to tracks to supply the trains with water.
5e93bb45be2d01cac1741182c9567e116adf9fff.translatedText: 隨著鐵路網遍布美國各地，工程師也忙著建造數千座水壩。蒸汽機車需要大量的水，而在乾旱的西部地區，這往往很難獲得。因此，水庫建在鐵軌附近，為火車供水。

8267a127482359e6b7e558044a1f696829d4325a.sourceText: Dams were usually constructed with masonry and large blocks of quarried stone, which was very labor-intensive. Atchison , Topeka , and Santa Fe Railway engineer Francis H. Bainbridge had an idea. The railroad company was already purchasing steel in bulk for the construction of tracks, trestles, and bridges. If steel could be used to build the dams as well, it would save the company time and money.
8267a127482359e6b7e558044a1f696829d4325a.translatedText: 水壩通常是用磚石和大塊採石料建造的，這是非常勞動密集的。艾奇遜、托皮卡和聖達菲鐵路工程師弗朗西斯·H·班布里奇想到了一個主意。該鐵路公司已經大量採購鋼材用於建造軌道、棧橋和橋樑。如果也可以使用鋼材來建造水壩，那麼將為公司節省時間和金錢。

aec1c6517c2752eeac35bee49daa3a820fc25d61.sourceText: Construction on the dam began in 1897 and was finished early the next year. Pieces of the dam were constructed off-site and assembled in Johnson Canyon. The final cost was a relatively inexpensive $63,500, or approximately $2 million today. Although the steel dam proved much cheaper and faster to construct than masonry dams, there were justified concerns about its long-term integrity. Only three steel dams were constructed in the U.S., and today the Ashfork-Bainbridge Dam is the only one that still holds a reservoir.
aec1c6517c2752eeac35bee49daa3a820fc25d61.translatedText: 水壩的建設於 1897 年開始，並於次年初完工。大壩的各個部分是在場外建造並在約翰遜峽谷組裝的。最終成本相對低廉，為 63,500 美元，相當於今天的 200 萬美元。儘管事實證明，鋼壩比磚石壩建造成本更低、速度更快，但人們對其長期完整性的擔憂是有道理的。美國祇建造了三座鋼壩，如今阿什福克-班布里奇大壩是唯一一座仍保留水庫的水壩。

5cf00ef027c9a21a85886e7e1f744d0a90876d5c.sourceText: Although they supported the experiment, from the start, the railroad company didn't trust that the steel dam would work. Around 13 years later, a masonry dam was constructed a mile upstream from the Ashfork-Bainbridge Dam, so that if the steel dam failed, there was still a reservoir in place to supply water for their needs. Although the railroad is gone, both dams are still functional today.
5cf00ef027c9a21a85886e7e1f744d0a90876d5c.translatedText: 儘管他們支持這項實驗，但鐵路公司從一開始就不相信鋼壩能夠發揮作用。大約 13 年後，在阿什福克-班布里奇大壩上游一英里處建造了一座磚石壩，這樣，即使鋼壩潰決，仍然有一個水庫可以滿足他們的用水需求。雖然鐵路已不復存在，但兩座水壩至今仍在運作。

3e795435c92fdabbdcc521af0d31f881355b8283.sourceText: The land around the Ashfork-Bainbridge Steel Dam is now a part of the Kaibab National Forest. The steel dam was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1976.
3e795435c92fdabbdcc521af0d31f881355b8283.translatedText: 阿什福克-班布里奇鋼壩周圍的土地現已成為凱巴布國家森林的一部分。 1976 年，這座鋼壩被列入國家歷史名勝名錄。

2d2af6582201d904ca1accfc0a045491c01b83e6.sourceText: On August 30, 1869, Major John Wesley Powell and five companions brought their rowboats ashore at St. Thomas, Nevada . Having departed from Green River , Wyoming , with nine men three months earlier, Powell and his crew became the first white people confirmed to have traveled through the entirety of the Grand Canyon.
2d2af6582201d904ca1accfc0a045491c01b83e6.translatedText: 1869 年 8 月 30 日，約翰·韋斯利·鮑威爾少校和五位同伴將他們的划艇在內華達州聖托馬斯上岸。三個月前，鮑威爾與九名男子從懷俄明州格林河出發，成為第一批被確認穿越整個大峽谷的白人。

49389f72a6650ce44edb25564beae142664b9e66.sourceText: Powell grew up in rural Illinois and had a largely self-taught education. As a young man, he frequently set off on journeys to satisfy his own need for adventure, including spending four months walking across the state of Wisconsin and rowing a boat down the Mississippi River from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico. In part because of these exploits, when he was 25 years old he was admitted to the Illinois Natural History Society and began taking classes at Oberlin College. His studies were interrupted by the American Civil War, however, and he dropped out of school and enlisted in the Union Army.
49389f72a6650ce44edb25564beae142664b9e66.translatedText: 鮑威爾在伊利諾州農村長大，基本上是自學成才。年輕時，他經常出發旅行，以滿足自己的冒險需要，包括用四個月的時間徒步穿越威斯康辛州，並划船沿著密西西比河從明尼蘇達州到達墨西哥灣。部分由於這些功績，他在 25 歲時被伊利諾伊州自然歷史學會錄取，並開始在歐柏林學院上課。然而，他的學業因美國內戰而中斷，他輟學並加入了聯邦軍隊。

9890d7bb1fec300c87fdd25fcfd8da5e74c3b5b1.sourceText: Powell was initially put to work scouting and creating maps, but was eventually promoted to leading artillery brigades. During the Battle of Shiloh, a bullet hit his right arm, requiring most of it to be amputated. Despite this, he returned to military service for the rest of the war, earning the rank of Lieutenant Colonel. After the war, Powell accepted a position as professor of geology at Illinois Wesleyan University, but soon found a new calling in the exploration and mapping of the American West.
9890d7bb1fec300c87fdd25fcfd8da5e74c3b5b1.translatedText: 鮑威爾最初從事偵察和繪製地圖的工作，但最終被提升為領導砲兵旅。在示羅之戰中，一顆子彈擊中了他的右臂，導致其大部分被截肢。儘管如此，他在戰爭剩餘時間裡重返軍隊服役，並獲得了中校軍銜。戰後，鮑威爾接受了伊利諾伊衛斯理大學地質學教授的職位，但很快就在美國西部的勘探和測繪中找到了新的使命。

f5133a905c60587fe6bc5fd3a4efa158c4262c66.sourceText: After proving his capability with several smaller surveys in the Rocky Mountains, Powell was able to convince the Smithsonian Institute and the United States Army to provide material support to a much more ambitious project, the mapping and geological study of the Green and Colorado Rivers, including the Grand Canyon. Powell recruited a team of frontiersmen, Civil War veterans, and amateur scientists, and they departed from Green River on May 24, 1869, in four wooden rowboats.
f5133a905c60587fe6bc5fd3a4efa158c4262c66.translatedText: 在透過落基山脈的幾次小型勘測證明了自己的能力後，鮑威爾說服了史密森學會和美國陸軍為一個更雄心勃勃的計畫提供物質支持，即對格林河和科羅拉多河（包括大峽谷）進行測繪和地質研究。鮑威爾招募了一支由拓荒者、內戰老兵和業餘科學家組成的團隊，於 1869 年 5 月 24 日乘坐四艘木製划艇從格林河出發。

b98b5821a880ad309844c273d68b8371ad27c603.sourceText: The Powell Expedition of 1869 was fraught with perils. Only a few days into the journey, one of the four rowboats capsized and many supplies were lost. Also early on in the trip, Englishman Frank Goodman, who traveled to the American West seeking a thrilling adventure and paid to join the expedition, decided that he had had enough and simply left, settling down and spending the rest of his life in nearby Vernal , Utah .
b98b5821a880ad309844c273d68b8371ad27c603.translatedText: 1869 年的鮑威爾探險充滿了危險。旅程剛開始幾天，四艘划艇中的一艘就傾覆了，許多補給品都遺失了。同樣在旅程的早期，英國人弗蘭克·古德曼前往美國西部尋求一次驚心動魄的冒險，並付費參加了這次探險，他覺得自己受夠了，乾脆離開了，在附近的猶他州弗納爾定居下來並度過了餘生。

b9e3601f5e2b68bfc3764f3ec56aba2c71bd289d.sourceText: The river rapids provided most of the hurdles along their way. As they ventured, Powell would attempt to judge whether it was better to try and run them, which was risky and could easily result in the injury of men and the loss of supplies, or to pull the boats ashore and carry everything downriver to a safer point, which was tedious and tiring work. Having already lost one of his four boats, Powell frequently erred on the side of caution and ordered everything carried around the troublesome parts of the river. This greatly slowed their progress and required them to ration food.
b9e3601f5e2b68bfc3764f3ec56aba2c71bd289d.translatedText: 沿途的障礙大多是急流。當他們冒險時，鮑威爾會嘗試判斷是否應該嘗試運行它們，因為這是有風險的，很容易導致人員受傷和物資損失，或者將船隻拉上岸，然後將所有東西帶到下游到更安全的地方，這是一項乏味而累人的工作。鮑威爾已經失去了四艘船中的一艘，他經常因謹慎而犯錯，並下令將所有船隻轉移到河流的麻煩部分。這大大減慢了他們的進度，並要求他們配給食物。

6b9c90111351becac3fe204ad52185b4eded606f.sourceText: In the summer of 1876, a group of settlers from Boston , Massachusetts crossed into the Little Colorado River Valley in northern Arizona . They had been drawn to the area by rumors of fertile land for farming and easily accessed mineral deposits for mining. However when they arrived, they were disappointed to see that the area was much more arid than they had been led to believe and it was already being settled by Mormon pioneers who had come south from Utah . Still, having come so far, they continued on towards the snow-capped mountains within sight to the west.
6b9c90111351becac3fe204ad52185b4eded606f.translatedText: 1876 年夏天，一群來自麻薩諸塞州波士頓的定居者越過亞利桑那州北部的小科羅拉多河谷。他們被傳言吸引到該地區，那裡有肥沃的土地可供耕種，而且易於開採開採。然而，當他們到達時，他們失望地發現該地區比他們想像的要乾旱得多，而且從猶他州南下的摩門教先驅已經在那裡定居。儘管如此，儘管已經走了這麼遠，他們還是繼續向西邊視線範圍內的雪山前進。

5d011de601dc3e9998a96b21ddbbd8f9e18e5218.sourceText: In early July, the Bostonians reached a ranch owned by Thomas McMillan and camped nearby. On July 4, 1876, to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the United States ' independence, the settlers chopped down a large Ponderosa pine tree, stripped it of its branches, attached an American flag, and stood the tree back up.
5d011de601dc3e9998a96b21ddbbd8f9e18e5218.translatedText: 七月初，波士頓人到達了 Thomas McMillan 擁有的牧場，並在附近紮營。 1876 年 7 月 4 日，為了紀念美國獨立 100 週年，定居者砍倒了一棵大黃松樹，剝去樹枝，貼上一面美國國旗，然後將樹重新豎立起來。

6dddbd43b4ba9d3953314c5bbf8dba657c3f1491.sourceText: In the following years, the area around McMillan's homestead began to be developed. An economy grew around timber and ranching, and soon the community was large enough to warrant having its own post office. With the arrival of the post office, the community needed a name and chose to name itself after the landmark created on the nation's centennial.
6dddbd43b4ba9d3953314c5bbf8dba657c3f1491.translatedText: 在接下來的幾年裡，麥克米倫宅基地周圍的地區開始開發。經濟圍繞著木材和牧場發展，很快社區就足夠大，可以擁有自己的郵局。隨著郵局的到來，社區需要一個名字，並選擇以建國一百週年時創建的地標來命名。

738d12db7d72e75830208e36be7ae20303b8f55a.sourceText: The town of Flagstaff , Arizona continued to grow and became a major regional transportation hub. By 1886 it was the largest city on the railway between Albuquerque , New Mexico and Los Angeles , California . At some point, however, the original Boston party Ponderosa flagpole fell and its precise location became lost to history.
738d12db7d72e75830208e36be7ae20303b8f55a.translatedText: 亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫鎮不斷發展，成為主要的地區交通樞紐。到 1886 年，它已成為新墨西哥州阿爾伯克基和加利福尼亞州洛杉磯之間鐵路上最大的城市。然而，在某個時候，原來的波士頓黨黃松旗桿倒塌了，它的確切位置也消失在歷史之中。

887b82c2cf969f6fc48427dca636069ca048e0b4.sourceText: In 1985, a monument to the original Flagstaff flag staff was constructed in the general area of where the original group of settlers from Boston camped. The governor of Arizona dedicated the monument to the spot from which the city of Flagstaff grew.
887b82c2cf969f6fc48427dca636069ca048e0b4.translatedText: 1985 年，在波士頓最初的定居者群體露營的地方，建造了一座紀念原來的弗拉格斯塔夫旗桿的紀念碑。亞利桑那州州長將這座紀念碑獻給了弗拉格斯塔夫市的發源地。

3208ecf5d4934ffcd9dc8a9d971662ea7d60d7f2.sourceText: McDonald’s is famous for having served billions and billions of burgers throughout the course of the franchise’s history, but until January 24, 1975, no McDonald’s burger had ever been served in quite this way before. It was on that day that the first drive-through opened in Sierra Vista, Arizona, forever changing one’s ability to eat Quarter Pounders in their car.
3208ecf5d4934ffcd9dc8a9d971662ea7d60d7f2.translatedText: 麥當勞因在整個特許經營歷史中提供了數十億個漢堡而聞名，但直到 1975 年 1 月 24 日，以前還沒有麥當勞漢堡以這種方式提供過。就在這一天，第一家得來速餐廳在亞利桑那州的謝拉維斯塔開業，永遠改變了人們在車上吃四分之一磅漢堡的能力。

87a8126012b9b966d721ec4dd1d73b5d9d36571f.sourceText: To be clear, drive-through restaurants were not a new innovation–many restaurants have a claim to the first drive-through burger, including the popular west coast chain In-N-Out Burger. McDonald’s, however, emphasized counter service and the local diner feel. But by 1974, a franchise in Oklahoma City was intending to open a drive-through window, and Dave Rich, the operator of the Sierra Vista McDonald’s, was intrigued by the possibility .
87a8126012b9b966d721ec4dd1d73b5d9d36571f.translatedText: 需要明確的是，得來速餐廳並不是一項新的創新——許多餐廳都聲稱擁有第一家得來速漢堡，其中包括廣受歡迎的西海岸連鎖店 In-N-Out Burger。然而，麥當勞強調櫃檯服務和當地用餐的感覺。但到了 1974 年，俄克拉荷馬城的一家特許經營店打算開設免下車窗口，Sierra Vista 麥當勞的經營者戴夫·里奇 (Dave Rich) 對這種可能性很感興趣。

266aba088faf586b34e746c9275dc44f884ff536.sourceText: Sierra Vista was and is a military town, with many residents working and living at nearby Fort Huachuca. Military officers who were on duty could not be seen wearing their uniforms in public due to the fort’s rules on military decorum, making a sit-down lunch impossible. However, they could grab lunch and go with no one being the wiser. So Dave Rich cut a hole in the wall of his McDonald’s franchise, put up glass and an intercom, and burger history was made.
266aba088faf586b34e746c9275dc44f884ff536.translatedText: Sierra Vista 過去是、現在仍然是一個軍事城鎮，許多居民在附近的華丘卡堡工作和生活。由於堡壘的軍事禮儀規定，執勤的軍官不能在公共場合穿著制服，因此無法坐下來吃午餐。不過，他們可以吃完午餐就走，沒人知道。於是，戴夫·里奇在他的麥當勞特許經營店的牆上開了一個洞，安裝了玻璃和對講機，漢堡的歷史就這樣被創造了。

3690b011ad137d8d1d4fa75f9419be2ecef18016.sourceText: Although the original building is no longer standing, travelers can still visit a McDonald’s franchise at this location. In front, a sign reads “World’s First McDonald’s Drive Thru,” and inside, there’s a small display of memorabilia, including the original Ronald McDonald figure used as the intercom. The glass from the drive-through window has ended up at the Henry F. Hauser Museum, a museum of local Sierra Vista history.
3690b011ad137d8d1d4fa75f9419be2ecef18016.translatedText: 雖然原來的建築已不復存在，但遊客仍然可以參觀這裡的麥當勞特許經營店。前面有一個標牌，上面寫著“世界上第一個麥當勞得來速”，裡面有一小塊紀念品展示，包括用作對講機的麥當勞叔叔雕像。免下車窗口的玻璃最終被送到了亨利·F·豪瑟博物館，這是一座展示塞拉維斯塔當地歷史的博物館。

121268b52b3b44954db74feb8363596d98f905cc.sourceText: Sierra Vista’s unique desert conditions and military background may have led the town to become a part of McDonald’s history, but perhaps it was also destiny. Once upon a time, the town of Sierra Vista was known by another name: Fry .
121268b52b3b44954db74feb8363596d98f905cc.translatedText: 賽拉維斯塔獨特的沙漠條件和軍事背景也許讓這個小鎮成為了麥當勞歷史的一部分，但也許這也是命運。曾幾何時，謝拉維斯塔鎮還有另一個名字：弗萊。

c023a8a2f05ea950da19c419eb17b14e18791219.sourceText: For thousands of years the distinctive silhouette of Picacho Peak has guided travelers across the Sonoran Desert. In 1858 the Butterfield Overland Mail Company, a stagecoach delivery company, began using the nearby lowlands on their route connecting Tucson and Phoenix . The most notable event in the mountain's history occurred several years later, after the outbreak of the American Civil War.
c023a8a2f05ea950da19c419eb17b14e18791219.translatedText: 數千年來，皮卡喬峰獨特的輪廓引導著旅行者穿越索諾蘭沙漠。 1858 年，驛站馬車運送公司巴特菲爾德陸上郵政公司 (Butterfield Overland Mail Company) 開始在連接圖森和菲尼克斯的路線上使用附近的低地。這座山歷史上最引人注目的事件發生在幾年後，美國內戰爆發後。

d08ad57463b303637086d39f626ba1a077c52065.sourceText: On March 28, 1861 a delegation in Tucson declared that Arizona was a territory of the Confederacy and opposed to the United States. Without soldiers or political power, the declaration by secessionists in Arizona seemed to have little impact. About a year later, however, cavalry from Texas began harassing Arizonans who were still loyal to the United States. The rebel cavalry reportedly wanted to make a loud entrance into the American Southwest to attract sympathizers from California into joining the conflict. This mostly backfired, instead leading to a successful recruitment of Union volunteer regiments to push the Confederates out of the neighboring territory.
d08ad57463b303637086d39f626ba1a077c52065.translatedText: 1861 年 3 月 28 日，圖森的代表團宣布亞利桑那州是南部邦聯的領土，反對美國。沒有士兵或政治權力，亞利桑那州的分離主義者的宣言似乎沒有什麼影響。然而，大約一年後，來自德克薩斯州的騎兵開始騷擾仍然忠於美國的亞利桑那州人。據報道，叛軍騎兵想要大舉進入美國西南部，以吸引來自加州的同情者加入衝突。這大多適得其反，反而導致聯邦志願軍成功招募，將南方聯盟軍趕出鄰近領土。

2bff5b819ccbcd7f5f039ca5b0ed9b806585dfec.sourceText: The larger goal of the Confederate incursions into Arizona was to control the Butterfield Overland Mail stagecoach road and with it, the easiest access to California. Subsequently, a number of conflicts occurred along that route. On April 15, 1862 a group of Union scouts were on patrol, searching for Confederate scouts that were rumored to be nearby. About a mile north of the Picacho Pass mail station, the Union scouts surprised three Confederate lookouts who surrendered immediately and gave up the Confederate scouts’ location.
2bff5b819ccbcd7f5f039ca5b0ed9b806585dfec.translatedText: 南方聯盟入侵亞利桑那州的更大目標是控制巴特菲爾德陸上郵政驛站馬路，並以此控制通往加州的最便利通道。隨後，沿著這條路線發生了一些衝突。 1862 年 4 月 15 日，一群聯邦偵察兵正在巡邏，尋找據傳在附近的南部邦聯偵察兵。在皮卡喬山口郵局以北約一英里處，聯邦偵察兵令三名南方邦聯瞭望員大吃一驚，他們立即投降並交出南方邦聯偵察兵的位置。

746ef3a359f79c67e01ce80d2fcb465ef89af052.sourceText: Although their orders were to report their position and wait for reinforcements, Union officer Lieutenant James Barrett was eager for a chance to prove himself. The Union soldiers charged at the Confederates and they exchanged fire for 90 minutes. Barrett died almost immediately, and eventually the leaderless Union soldiers retreated. The final toll of the battle was three dead and three wounded on the Union side and two wounded and three captured among the Confederates.
746ef3a359f79c67e01ce80d2fcb465ef89af052.translatedText: 雖然他們的命令是報告位置並等待援軍，但聯邦軍官詹姆斯·巴雷特中尉卻渴望有機會證明自己。北軍士兵向南軍發動衝鋒，雙方交火長達 90 分鐘。巴雷特幾乎立刻就死了，最後群龍無首的聯邦士兵撤退了。這場戰鬥的最終傷亡人數為聯邦方面三人死亡、三人受傷，南部聯盟方面兩人受傷和三人被俘。

7280e31ed7880a994254ea62d068dc727494582a.sourceText: Although this was a fairly inconsequential engagement in the larger picture of the American Civil War, the Battle of Picacho Pass is now remembered by history as the war’s westernmost battle. (A skirmish occurred further west at Stanwix Station, but the encounter was so brief and small that most historians don't regard it as a true battle.) It was also the high-water mark of the Confederate’s westward advance. Retreats were ordered across Arizona and New Mexico , and by July 1862 Confederate troops had returned to Texas.
7280e31ed7880a994254ea62d068dc727494582a.translatedText: 雖然從美國內戰的大局來看，這是一場相當無關緊要的交戰，但皮卡喬山口戰役現在被歷史銘記為這場戰爭中最西端的戰役。 （在更西邊的斯坦尼克斯車站發生了一場小衝突，但這次遭遇是如此短暫和小規模，以至於大多數歷史學家並不認為這是一場真正的戰鬥。）這也是南部邦聯向西推進的高潮。亞利桑那州和新墨西哥州下令撤退，到 1862 年 7 月，南方聯盟軍隊已返回德克薩斯州。

5963945a8f2b59c37c7fcd58ea095e886ee55f51.sourceText: Today, the site of the battle is memorialized within Picacho Peak State Park. Each year, actors put on a reenactment of the battle—the event has grown so popular that many more actors take part in the engagement than actually happened. Many monuments to the battle have been placed at the site, though many were made of wood and fell apart over time. The only remaining monument at the site is a stone pillar commemorating the Confederate soldiers who fought there.
5963945a8f2b59c37c7fcd58ea095e886ee55f51.translatedText: 今天，這場戰鬥的地點被紀念在皮卡喬峰州立公園內。每年，演員都會重演這場戰鬥——這一活動變得如此受歡迎，以至於參加戰鬥的演員比實際發生的要多得多。現場安置了許多這場戰鬥的紀念碑，儘管許多紀念碑是用木頭製成的，隨著時間的推移而倒塌。該遺址僅存的紀念碑是一根石柱，紀念在那裡戰鬥的南方聯盟士兵。

3eed74a15f979d5d1365bb83e0eece5c877b7712.sourceText: Alongside a preserved section of the historic Route 66 sits an abandoned, fenced off red brick building. Constructed in 1903, the building is what's left of the Truxton Canyon Training School, a school that belonged to the Office of Indian Affairs and was designed to sever Native American childrens' connections to their cultures.
3eed74a15f979d5d1365bb83e0eece5c877b7712.translatedText: 沿著歷史悠久的 66 號公路的一段保留下來的路段，坐落著一座廢棄的、用柵欄圍起來的紅磚建築。該建築建於 1903 年，是特魯克斯頓峽谷培訓學校 (Truxton Canyon Training School) 的遺跡，該學校隸屬於印第安事務辦公室，旨在切斷美國原住民兒童與其文化的聯繫。

51388d6b818a68a16e3289b7ba4db17458b9d78f.sourceText: Children lived in boarding rooms at the school, kept away from their families, and were spoken to exclusively in English. In addition to classes in reading, math, history, and other usual school subjects, children were given instructions on what to wear, how to do household chores, and given work skills that were more in line with Euroamerican industrial culture.
51388d6b818a68a16e3289b7ba4db17458b9d78f.translatedText: 孩子們住在學校的寄宿室，遠離家人，只用英語交談。除了閱讀、數學、歷史和其他學校常規課程外，孩子們還被指導穿什麼、如何做家務，並獲得更符合歐美工業文化的工作技能。

27ddaa2525a23c209afa998d1f751620aff8d86f.sourceText: The Office of Indian Affairs hoped that preventing Native children from growing up in their culture and using their language would force them to live in a manner the United States government preferred. It would also prevent them from passing on their heritage to future generations.
27ddaa2525a23c209afa998d1f751620aff8d86f.translatedText: 印第安事務辦公室希望，阻止原住民兒童在他們的文化中成長並使用他們的語言將迫使他們以美國政府喜歡的方式生活。這也會阻止他們將自己的遺產傳給子孫後代。

329935cb87f8c53930da662382ef0d79deab2849.sourceText: The Truxton Canyon Training School primarily targeted children of the Hualapai tribe but also housed Apache, Havasupai, Hopi, Navajo, Tohono O'odham, Pima, and Yavapai children. The school operated from 1903 until it was finally closed in 1937. The schoolhouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2003. Today, the Hualapai tribe owns the building and has plans to renovate and reopen it as a community center.
329935cb87f8c53930da662382ef0d79deab2849.translatedText: 特拉克斯頓峽谷訓練學校主要針對華拉派部落的兒童，但也收養阿帕奇、哈瓦蘇派、霍皮人、納瓦霍、托霍諾·奧德姆、皮馬和亞瓦派的兒童。該學校從 1903 年開始運營，直至 1937 年最終關閉。該校舍於 2003 年被列入國家歷史古蹟名錄。如今，華拉派部落擁有該建築，並計劃將其翻新並重新開放為社區中心。

ff8cb713efae6f13aa49608de2327ec85a08a502.sourceText: From a distance, what looks like a giant stick figure raising its hands is actually, upon closer inspection, a jumble of guns, knives, and other weapons melted together. “Release the Fear” in Phoenix ’s Roosevelt Row neighborhood is symbolic of the fight against violence. As such, the 24-foot-tall figure is meant to be a metaphor for rising above violence. Around it are the names of the donors who funded the sculpture , and on the surrounding pavement are quotes by famous figures who have championed nonviolence.
ff8cb713efae6f13aa49608de2327ec85a08a502.translatedText: 遠遠望去，像一個舉起雙手的巨大火柴人，仔細一看，其實是一堆槍、刀和其他武器融化在一起。鳳凰城羅斯福街社區的「釋放恐懼」是反暴力鬥爭的象徵。因此，這個 24 英尺高的人物象徵著超越暴力。周圍刻著為雕塑提供資金的捐助者的名字，周圍的人行道上還刻著倡導非暴力的著名人物的名言。

1ddcbc987284b538384de6c30020e35b90ead607.sourceText: The sculpture’s creator, Robert Miley, founded a local nonprofit of the same name dedicated to helping at-risk youth through art workshops. His outreach has reduced the recidivism rate of participants, and he has spread this work to Central-American countries. It took Miley 10 years to secure funding and material for his sculpture, with the latter partially becoming criminals’ weapons confiscated and donated by the Phoenix Police Department. Those constitute 8,000 of the 17,000 pounds of metal in the sculpture. Miley also received assistance in creating the sculpture from local high school students and convicts.
1ddcbc987284b538384de6c30020e35b90ead607.translatedText: 雕塑的創作者 Robert Miley 創立了當地一家同名非營利組織，致力於透過藝術工作坊幫助高風險青少年。他的外展活動降低了參與者的再犯率，並將這項工作推廣到中美洲國家。麥莉花了10年時間為他的雕塑籌集到資金和材料，後者的部分成為鳳凰城警察局沒收和捐贈的犯罪分子武器。這些構成了雕塑中 17,000 磅金屬中的 8,000 磅。麥莉也得到了當地高中生和囚犯的幫助來創作雕塑。

cac73c8fc4b54c8635a58fd9dea17e956c0cb1ba.sourceText: Built in the 1920s, this abandoned hot spring resort is rumored (though unproven) to have been the vacation spot of the notorious gangster, Al Capone.
cac73c8fc4b54c8635a58fd9dea17e956c0cb1ba.translatedText: 這個廢棄的溫泉度假村建於 1920 年代，有傳言（儘管未經證實）是臭名昭著的黑幫阿爾·卡彭 (Al Capone) 的度假勝地。

29d32cdacb3b5c824c7e6a55695fffa65d85e662.sourceText: In 1962, the once sought after resort burned down leaving only foundation stones and two hot springs overlooking the Verde Valley. The smaller spring is housed within the last nearly-intact structure on the abandoned resort and is a balmy 100˚farenheit and large enough for three or four adults to sit and relax.
29d32cdacb3b5c824c7e6a55695fffa65d85e662.translatedText: 1962 年，這個曾經備受追捧的度假村被燒毀，只剩下基石和兩個俯瞰 Verde 山谷的溫泉。較小的泉水位於廢棄度假村最後一個幾乎完好無損的建築內，溫度為 100 華氏度，溫度宜人，足夠三到四個成年人坐下來放鬆。

9ee5ad6bf47a2b9f82d4e9d748b029119d012cd9.sourceText: There is no roof to this little hut, and no windows although a doorway and all four walls remain. These walls are wildly decorated with art and inscriptions dating back decades. The paintings and drawings range from the inspirational to the commemorative to the downright naughty.
9ee5ad6bf47a2b9f82d4e9d748b029119d012cd9.translatedText: 這個小小屋沒有屋頂，也沒有窗戶，但門和所有四面牆都保留著。這些牆壁上裝飾著數十年前的藝術品和銘文。這些繪畫和圖畫的範圍從鼓舞人心的到紀念性的，再到徹頭徹尾的頑皮。

363787533b49d4ec31761fdd2dd9fa9d8af2f54f.sourceText: To access the former resort, explorers need to walk about a mile northwest from Child's Dispersed Campground in the Verde Valley, not far from Fossil Creek. No permits are required and campfires are permitted, but be ready to cross the river to get to the hot springs. Proceed with caution.
363787533b49d4ec31761fdd2dd9fa9d8af2f54f.translatedText: 要進入以前的度假村，探險家需要從佛得谷的兒童分散營地向西北步行約一英里，距離化石溪不遠。不需要許可證，也允許生篝火，但要準備好過河去溫泉。謹慎行事。

aa0b99dc47fbbbbeb8e47c783668bdeebd3aef62.sourceText: While traveling on I-8 between Phoenix and San Diego, consider stopping by the Space Age Lodge and Restaurant. Originally built in 1965, it was designed by Al Stovall, a man who made his fortune in the plastics and metals industries during World War II.
aa0b99dc47fbbbbeb8e47c783668bdeebd3aef62.translatedText: 當沿著 8 號州際公路往返於鳳凰城和聖地牙哥之間時，請考慮前往太空時代旅館和餐廳 (Space Age Lodge and Restaurant)。它最初建於 1965 年，由二戰期間在塑膠和金屬行業發家的阿爾·斯托瓦爾 (Al Stovall) 設計。

66a59eeb3420a021366e4afc807fe9b4eeeaf519.sourceText: Mr. Stovall designed five space-themed hotels: four in Anaheim, California (just near Disneyland) and one in Pima Bend, Arizona. The Pima Bend location is the only remaining hotel designed by Stovall that has retained its Jetsons-like feel. The lobby entrance is topped with a UFO with outer space seen throughout the decor—even the umbrella table by the pool is a flying saucer.
66a59eeb3420a021366e4afc807fe9b4eeeaf519.translatedText: Mr.斯托瓦爾設計了五家太空主題飯店：四家位於加州阿納海姆（靠近迪士尼樂園），一家位於亞利桑那州皮馬本德。皮馬彎 (Pima Bend) 酒店是斯托瓦爾 (Stovall) 設計的唯一一家保留了傑森一家 (Jetsons) 風格的酒店。大廳入口頂部有一個不明飛行物，整個裝飾中都可以看到外太空——就連泳池邊的傘桌也是一個飛碟。

6efea0595ffdcb687dbd01f7f9050a7a4ec07c3e.sourceText: The original Space Age restaurant caught fire in 1998—owners claimed that it was attacked by aliens but a malfunctioning neon sign appears to be the more likely culprit—but was rebuilt with the same outer space theme.
6efea0595ffdcb687dbd01f7f9050a7a4ec07c3e.translatedText: 最初的太空時代餐廳於 1998 年起火，業主聲稱它受到外星人襲擊，但故障的霓虹燈似乎是罪魁禍首，但以相同的外太空主題重建。

55c4a594c33e0f46c8f063210b8216dfa9daeaea.sourceText: Inside are murals depicting astronauts and spaceships, including the USS Enterprise . The food is typical diner fare with out-of-this-world names like the Jupiter Burger (cheeseburger with grilled onions and bacon). If you want a piece of nostalgia to take home, there are coffee mugs for sale with the iconic sign on them.
55c4a594c33e0f46c8f063210b8216dfa9daeaea.translatedText: 裡面有描繪太空人和太空船，包括企業號航空母艦。食物是典型的晚餐菜餚，有著「Jupiter Burger」（木星漢堡，起司漢堡配烤洋蔥和培根）等奇特的名字。如果您想要懷舊之情帶回家，可以購買帶有標誌性標誌的咖啡杯。

2e984347cb8c9035bb9cd0f4cd7c803efad94b0c.sourceText: Christmas traditions can be a challenge in places that rarely see a day of cold all year, but in the Arizona city of Chandler , they have simply adapted their traditions to match the climate by forming a pile of tumbleweeds into the shape of a festive fir tree each year.
2e984347cb8c9035bb9cd0f4cd7c803efad94b0c.translatedText: 對於一年中很少有寒冷日子的地方來說，聖誕節傳統可能是一個挑戰，但在亞利桑那州的錢德勒市，他們只是簡單地調整了自己的傳統，以適應氣候，每年將一堆風滾草形成節日樅樹的形狀。

5ae512e27bc378b4460dee1f0382a9a011e00bd0.sourceText: Dating all the way back to 1957, the city takes its tradition quite seriously. Beginning around September, city workers begin collecting the dried invasive Russian thistle bushes (better known as tumbleweeds) that roll across the landscape. It takes around 1,000 of the iconic dead plants to create the massive "tree" each year. The collected tumbleweeds are placed around a chicken wire frame to give the attraction the shape of a wide, full tree, before being coated in a more pleasing shade of Christmas white and flame retardant (this is not the Gavle Goat ). Finally the whole thing is assaulted with over 65 pounds of glitter, and strung with Christmas lights which are activated in a yearly ceremony full of pomp and circumstance.
5ae512e27bc378b4460dee1f0382a9a011e00bd0.translatedText: 可以追溯到 1957 年，這座城市非常重視自己的傳統。從九月左右開始，城市工作人員開始收集遍布整個景觀的干燥入侵俄羅斯薊灌木（更廣為人知的名稱是風滾草）。每年需要大約 1,000 株標誌性的死亡植物才能形成這棵巨大的「樹」。收集到的風滾草被放置在鐵絲網框架周圍，使景點呈現出一棵寬闊、飽滿的樹的形狀，然後塗上更令人愉悅的聖誕白色和阻燃劑（這不是耶夫勒山羊）。最後，整個聖誕樹上覆蓋著超過 65 磅的閃光，並掛滿了聖誕燈，這些燈在一年一度的盛大儀式中被激活。

cf854df9cf0d2ed20e489b5cb4176b0161281604.sourceText: While it may not have the size or reach of something along the lines of the tree at Rockefeller Center, in its way, Chandler's Tumbleweed Christmas Tree is far more unique and Christmas-y given that they have to invent their tree each year just to show how much they love the spirit.
cf854df9cf0d2ed20e489b5cb4176b0161281604.translatedText: 雖然它的大小或範圍可能不如洛克菲勒中心的聖誕樹，但以它的方式，錢德勒的風滾草聖誕樹更加獨特和聖誕節，因為他們每年都必鬚髮明一棵樹，只是為了表達他們的喜愛程度精神。
