fb82e314e6ded5ce6c26510d0405626138cf27b2.sourceText: Binocular vision, binocular being Latin for double eye, is an amazing trait. So valuable is having double eye vision that all animals have two eyes or more. The first reason being that if you lose one eye you have a spare, the second being that it greatly expands your field of vision. In humans, among many other animals, this binocular vision is taken a step further by having our two eyes both point forward. While this gives us a narrower field of vision than say, a bird, it also gives us a special ability, stereopsis or the ability to see one image with depth perception.
fb82e314e6ded5ce6c26510d0405626138cf27b2.translatedText: 雙眼視覺，雙眼在拉丁語中是雙眼的意思，是令人驚奇的特徵。擁有雙眼視力非常有價值，因此所有動物都有兩隻或更多眼睛。第一個原因是，如果你失去一隻眼睛，你還有一隻備用眼睛，第二個原因是它可以大大擴展你的視野。在人類和許多其他動物中，透過讓我們的兩隻眼睛都指向前方，這種雙眼視覺更進一步。雖然這給了我們比鳥更窄的視野，但它也給了我們一種特殊的能力，即立體視覺或具有深度感知的圖像的能力。

59c8d524dc2030c2b6bab8a3d6f4f0a4774b2360.sourceText: In the world of telescopes, having two eyes has just as many advantages. The LBT or large binocular telescope is currently considered the largest telescope in the world, and while it does not have the largest single mirror, what it does have is two very large -- each 27ft across and weighing 17.7 metric tons each -- mirrors positioned next to each other like giant eyes. Together the mirrors allow for the combined resolution of a 75ft telescope, the light gathering surface of a single 39ft mirror and a better clarity, than the Hubble Space Telescope, which is of course located IN space.
59c8d524dc2030c2b6bab8a3d6f4f0a4774b2360.translatedText: 在望遠鏡的世界中，擁有兩隻眼睛同樣具有許多優點。 LBT（大型雙筒望遠鏡）目前被認為是世界上最大的望遠鏡，雖然它沒有最大的單面鏡子，但它擁有兩個非常大的鏡子，每個鏡子寬 27 英尺，重 17.7 噸，彼此相鄰，就像巨大的眼睛一樣。這些反射鏡組合在一起，可實現 75 英尺望遠鏡的綜合分辨率、單個 39 英尺反射鏡的聚光錶面以及比位於太空中的哈伯太空望遠鏡更好的清晰度。

274538286fadcc5e89dc059dd2b5e9f46769ea4b.sourceText: Situated in the Arizona Pinaleno Mountains, (Arizona is the location a disproportionate number of telescopes, presumably in part because of the geography and weather) the huge LBT, which cost over $120 million to build, had its massive mirrors crafted in the University of Arizona's nearby Steward Observatory Mirror Lab one of the few places in the world where over 20 tons of glass can be heated red hot and spun into a perfect parabola at roughly 2,130 degrees. They then polish the glass to a level of accuracy that is "3,000 times thinner than a human hair."
274538286fadcc5e89dc059dd2b5e9f46769ea4b.translatedText: 位於亞利桑那州皮納雷諾山脈（亞利桑那州是望遠鏡數量不成比例的地方，可能部分是由於地理和天氣的原因）巨大的 LBT 耗資超過 1.2 億美元建造，其巨大的鏡子是在亞利桑那大學附近的斯圖爾特天文台鏡子實驗室製作的，這是世界上為數不多的幾個地方之一，可以將 20 噸以上的玻璃加熱成紅色，301 度。然後，他們將玻璃拋光到「比人的頭髮細 3,000 倍」的精確度。

702bf0551b76a14ed7e9576a52df9422e64a9824.sourceText: Though there was some controversy during the building, involving both the local Native American San Carlos Apache tribe and environmentalists who were concerned about a species of endangered squirrel, by the time the telescope got to work with both mirrors in (known in the telescope as "seeing first light") January 2008 most of the concerns had died down or been resolved.
702bf0551b76a14ed7e9576a52df9422e64a9824.translatedText: 雖然在建造過程中存在一些爭議，涉及當地美洲原住民聖卡洛斯阿帕奇部落和擔心一種瀕臨滅絕的松鼠的環保主義者，但當望遠鏡於 2008 年 1 月開始使用兩個鏡子時（在望遠鏡中稱為“看到第一道光”），大多數擔憂已經平息下來或已解決。

b4e164ce23795e5c3e940dd0e2225f74153010e5.sourceText: Today the telescope is busy taking stereoscopic images of spiral galaxies, the crab nebula, and peering deep into the universe all the way back to its very beginnings.
b4e164ce23795e5c3e940dd0e2225f74153010e5.translatedText: 今天，望遠鏡正忙於拍攝螺旋星系、蟹狀星雲的立體影像，並深入觀察宇宙，一直追溯到它的起源。

019449abb72b8f30ab697e6365d2036e6e8b7453.sourceText: On July 5, 1973, workers at the Doxol Gas Distribution Plant in Kingman, Arizona, began what should have been a routine job: transferring propane gas from a railway car into storage tanks. A series of small events and errors, however, snowballed into a massive tragedy that is still used as a warning in training material for industrial workers and fire departments across the country, and led to changes in industrial regulations.
019449abb72b8f30ab697e6365d2036e6e8b7453.translatedText: 1973 年 7 月 5 日，亞利桑那州金曼的 Doxol 天然氣分配廠的工人們開始了本應是例行公事的工作：將丙烷氣體從火車車廂轉移到儲罐中。然而，一系列小事件和錯誤逐漸演變成一場巨大的悲劇，至今仍被用作全國各地產業工人和消防部門培訓材料中的警告，並導致了行業法規的變化。

1950bee19bb01734389f03dc8e438144f7db9ce3.sourceText: Tank Car #38214, filled with 33,000 gallons of propane, was left sitting out in the hot sun in a railway yard until its contents could be transferred to storage. When two workers arrived to do that in the early afternoon, they quickly discovered that the tank was leaking through a faulty fitting. One of the workers attempted to tighten the fitting by hitting it with a wrench, creating a spark that ignited the escaping gas. Flames began shooting out of the tank, badly burning the two men. One of the workers managed to flee from the railway yard and got the attention of a police officer, who alerted the fire department of the growing fire.
1950bee19bb01734389f03dc8e438144f7db9ce3.translatedText: 裝有 33,000 加侖丙烷的罐車 #38214 被留在鐵路站的烈日下，直到其內容物被轉移到倉庫。當兩名工人下午早些時候到達時，他們很快就發現水箱因接頭故障而洩漏。一名工人試圖用扳手敲擊接頭來擰緊接頭，產生的火花點燃了逸出的氣體。火焰開始從坦克中噴出，嚴重燒傷了兩人。其中一名工人設法逃離鐵路站，並引起了一名警察的注意，警方向消防部門通報了越來越火勢的情況。

7d6fd4253916f5f97b0f386a01e278aa5e0fd0bc.sourceText: Members of the Kingman Volunteer Fire Department quickly arrived to the scene and realized they were not equipped to handle the situation. Nevertheless, they tried to do what they could. They knew it would be impossible to put out the propane fire with water from their engine, but they could use their water to attempt to cool down the exterior of the tank and hopefully prevent it from losing structural integrity and exploding. The firefighters got to work preparing their pumps and hoses. Meanwhile, news of the event over local radio stations had attracted a crowd to watch the events unfold along the shoulder of a nearby highway, only 200 yards away. Police were in the process of installing roadblocks and attempting to get the onlookers to disperse when, at 2:10 p.m., the tank exploded.
7d6fd4253916f5f97b0f386a01e278aa5e0fd0bc.translatedText: 金曼志願消防隊的成員迅速趕到現場，並意識到他們沒有能力處理這種情況。儘管如此，他們還是盡力做了一些力所能及的事情。他們知道不可能用引擎中的水來撲滅丙烷火，但他們可以用水來嘗試冷卻儲罐的外部，並希望防止其失去結構完整性和爆炸。消防隊員開始準備幫浦和軟管。與此同時，當地廣播電台播送的這一事件的消息吸引了一群人沿著附近高速公路的路肩觀看事件的發生，距離該高速公路僅 200 碼。下午 2 點 10 分，警方正在設置路障並試圖驅散圍觀者，坦克發生爆炸。

de21e41585a45e30597620e9cc12533088f3a079.sourceText: The fireball from the explosion was over 1,000 feet in diameter. Burning propane and railway debris rained down over a quarter mile away. The explosion left a 10-foot-deep crater in the ground and the shockwave was felt five miles away. The Doxol Gas building, a tire shop, a restaurant, and a truck stop caught on fire in the blast. Three of the firefighters died instantly and eight others died in hospitals later. More than 100 other onlookers, police officers, and railway workers were injured. The Bureau of Land Management scrambled to get their tanker planes to combat several wildfires that were started by the explosion.
de21e41585a45e30597620e9cc12533088f3a079.translatedText: 爆炸產生的火球直徑超過 1,000 英尺。燃燒的丙烷和鐵路碎片如雨般落在四分之一英里外。爆炸在地面上留下了一個 10 英尺深的彈坑，五英里外都能感受到衝擊波。 Doxol Gas 大樓、一家輪胎店、一家餐廳和一輛卡車停靠站在爆炸中起火。其中三名消防員當場死亡，另外八名消防員隨後在醫院死亡。另有 100 多名圍觀者、警察和鐵路工人受傷。土地管理局緊急出動加油機撲滅因爆炸引發的幾場野火。

00b6188a0682a32304b4b4a490d7cc4d27a70ed9.sourceText: The Kingman Explosion led to changes in regulations on how flammable and explosive materials were transported and stored. Fire departments began using footage of the disaster in more extensive training for how to handle Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosions, or BLEVEs. Today, a memorial to the victims of the Kingman Explosion is the centerpiece of Firefighter's Memorial Park, a public park in the city.
00b6188a0682a32304b4b4a490d7cc4d27a70ed9.translatedText: 金曼爆炸導致易燃易爆材料運輸和儲存法規改變。消防部門開始使用災難鏡頭進行更廣泛的培訓，以了解如何處理沸騰液體膨脹蒸氣爆炸（BLEVE）。如今，金曼爆炸受害者紀念碑是該市公共公園消防員紀念公園的核心。

e92127e4d371dfd1b832c51b7c22ceb622320260.sourceText: Historic Bisbee, Arizona is bustling, with a renewed emphasis on art, wellness, and tourism, but in many ways, it remains a living ghost town of its heyday. At the turn of the century, Bisbee was organized around the copper industry, with stories of massive wealth and exploitation. If you are looking for a place to stay and reckon with the ghosts of the past, there’s no better option than the putatively haunted Copper Queen Hotel.
e92127e4d371dfd1b832c51b7c22ceb622320260.translatedText: 歷史悠久的亞利桑那州比斯比十分繁華，重新重視藝術、健康和旅遊業，但在許多方面，它仍然是鼎盛時期的一個活生生的鬼城。在世紀之交，比斯比圍繞著銅工業成立，講述了巨大的財富和剝削的故事。如果您正在尋找住宿地點並與過去的鬼魂打交道，那麼沒有比被認為鬧鬼的銅皇后酒店更好的選擇了。

bc7e188ea4169243b98760da6c714a75f3b0f0f4.sourceText: This Victorian-era hotel is the oldest continuously run hotel in Arizona (in fact, the hotel predates its statehood). Completed in 1902, it was built by the Phelps Dodge Mining Company, owners of the eponymous Copper Queen mine, to be the height of modern luxury, as the company entertained visiting VIPs and dignitaries. The opulent hotel featured an Italianate tile floor, a Tiffany glass ceiling, and a front desk made from Tiger Oak. All the while, Phelps Dodge was systematically underpaying (or not paying) their workers, demanding more hours in dangerous conditions, resulting in a 1917 miners’ strike that led to the arrest and deportation of more than 1300 workers.
bc7e188ea4169243b98760da6c714a75f3b0f0f4.translatedText: 這家維多利亞時代的酒店是亞利桑那州最古老的持續經營的酒店（事實上，該酒店早於建州之前）。它於 1902 年竣工，由菲爾普斯道奇礦業公司 (Phelps Dodge Mining Company) 建造，該公司是同名銅皇后 (Copper Queen) 礦的所有者，它是現代奢華的頂峰，用於接待來訪的貴賓和政要。這家華麗的飯店設有義大利風格的瓷磚地板、蒂芙尼玻璃天花板和虎橡木製成的前台。一直以來，菲爾普斯道奇公司都係統性地少付（或不付）工人工資，要求在危險條件下延長工作時間，導致 1917 年礦工罷工，導致 1300 多名工人被捕並被驅逐出境。

a8af7f45319da067ca7109dfa890894c215db820.sourceText: By 1975, the quality of the Copper Queen mine had degraded, and the mine was closed. The city in turn experienced a death and rebirth, orienting itself around tours of the mine and as a healthy free-spirited Southwest art colony. In a similar vein, the hotel has made a turn for the paranormal, alleging the existence of at least three ghosts on its premises, which has led to an article in the New York Times and appearances on multiple ghost hunter television shows.
a8af7f45319da067ca7109dfa890894c215db820.translatedText: 到 1975 年，銅皇后礦的品質下降，該礦被關閉。這座城市又經歷了死亡和重生，以礦山之旅為中心，成為一個健康、自由的西南藝術殖民地。同樣，該酒店也出現了超自然現象，聲稱其酒店內至少存在三個鬼魂，這導致了《紐約時報》的一篇文章，並出現在多個捉鬼電視節目中。

f363ecda6f632fc88875081e2379c1d11de34052.sourceText: Guests can be said to interact with a young boy named Billy, and an older gentleman wearing a cape and top hat, who has failed to properly introduce himself. The most famous ghost resident is a woman named Julia Lowell, who as legend has it, was a prostitute who worked at the hotel and took her life there. Some male guests report (or self-report, more likely) that at night, a woman whispers in their ear, or plays with their feet. If you too are a fan of ghost footplay, you can experience it for yourself by booking Room 315, the Julia Lowell room.
f363ecda6f632fc88875081e2379c1d11de34052.translatedText: 據說客人與一個名叫比利的小男孩和一位穿著斗篷和高頂禮帽的年長紳士進行了互動，後者未能正確地自我介紹。最著名的鬼魂居民是一位名叫朱莉婭·洛厄爾的女人，傳說她是一名在酒店工作的妓女，並在那裡結束了她的生命。一些男客人報告（或更有可能是自我報告），晚上有女人在他們耳邊低語，或玩弄他們的腳。如果您也是鬼足戲的粉絲，您可以預訂 315 號房間（Julia Lowell 房間）親自體驗。

ad9629b86a79436fa4ccad050f5bb00d80ba9f5a.sourceText: The gnarled old mesquite tree behind the Circle K in Wickenburg, Arizona has been sitting on the spot for over 200 years and if many in the city are to be believed, it served as the town's makeshift jail in the days of the Old West.
ad9629b86a79436fa4ccad050f5bb00d80ba9f5a.translatedText: 亞利桑那州威肯堡 Circle K 後面的一棵粗糙的老豆科樹已經在原地矗立了 200 多年，如果城裡的許多人都相信的話，它在舊西部時代是該鎮的臨時監獄。

06e98a0503697e151db9349f1fe9756527ae2ef4.sourceText: As the story goes, drunks and criminals who were apprehended in Wickenburg between 1863 to 1890 were shackled to the tree as the town had no jail of its own. The prisoners would then be left out under the elements until a proper lawman could come down from Phoenix to collect them. According to the sign that now stands on the site, there were no escapes.
06e98a0503697e151db9349f1fe9756527ae2ef4.translatedText: 據說，1863 年至 1890 年間在威肯堡被捕的醉漢和罪犯都被銬在這棵樹上。沒有自己的監獄。然後，囚犯將被留在外面，直到有合適的執法人員從菲尼克斯下來接他們。根據現在立在現場的標牌，沒有人逃脫。

463ff16b4b93129eedae5d017c7c90db53324592.sourceText: Visiting the tree today, visitors will find a convincing little tableau honoring the history of the jail tree. There is a fiberglass outlaw who is slumped under the shade of the tree which he is tethered to by a long chain. There is also a a pair of informational signs as well as an antique chest buried at the foot of the tree, seemingly for aesthetic purposes.
463ff16b4b93129eedae5d017c7c90db53324592.translatedText: 今天參觀這棵樹，遊客會發現一個令人信服的小畫面，紀念這棵監獄樹的歷史。有一個玻璃纖維亡命之徒，倒在樹蔭下，被一根長鏈拴著。樹下還埋有一對資訊標誌和一個古董箱子，似乎是出於美學目的。

a5074bb4bfadde3d8a71a4a936c98862bf365f65.sourceText: Despite the earnest little roadside attraction that it has become, Wickenburg Jail Tree may be more legend than lawful prison. According to one woman who posted on a Wickenburg website, the saw grew up in the town in the 1930's and saw no remnants of a jail near the tree. She says that the legend grew from parents threatening to chain unruly children to the old arbor.
a5074bb4bfadde3d8a71a4a936c98862bf365f65.translatedText: 儘管威肯堡監獄樹已成為路邊的小景點，但它可能更像是一個傳奇，而不是合法的監獄。據一位在威肯堡網站上發布的女士稱，這把鋸子是 1930 年代在該鎮長大的，在這棵樹附近沒有看到監獄的遺跡。她說，這個傳說源自於父母威脅要將不守規矩的孩子鎖在舊涼亭上。

a6aa2e5ab77ebd782d8aaeeac5d9eec56759c1d0.sourceText: The Phoenix Trotting Park is a relic of leisure and vice smack in middle of the desert.
a6aa2e5ab77ebd782d8aaeeac5d9eec56759c1d0.translatedText: 鳳凰快跑公園是沙漠中的休閒遺跡。

9688a71fa886d964540ded4fdfd763682d6188ea.sourceText: The horse racing park was built in 1964 and opened the following year to any eager gamblers willing to brave the (unpaved at the time) desert expanse leading to the facility. The massive concrete structure was built in a futurist style with sloping geometric shapes sprouting around the interior and shaping the exterior walls. However, despite its aspirations to be a lasting hub of gambling, the track only remained in operation for two short seasons.
9688a71fa886d964540ded4fdfd763682d6188ea.translatedText: 賽馬公園建於 1964 年，並於次年向所有願意勇敢地面對通往該設施的廣闊沙漠（當時尚未鋪砌）的熱心賭徒開放。這座巨大的混凝土結構以未來主義風格建造，傾斜的幾何形狀圍繞著內部萌芽，並塑造了外牆。然而，儘管它渴望成為持久的賭博中心，但賽道只運營了兩個短暫的賽季。

3d3853f256e02b8b5ef4153486aa756375e924eb.sourceText: The project's proposed construction budget skyrocketed from three million dollars to ten million by the time it was completed, immediately increasing pressure for the site to attract big attendance numbers. Unfortunately, the track's remote desert location and uncomfortable heat drove away most of the potential customers and the horse races were abandoned. The site was left to deteriorate with only adventurous teens and budget-minded filmmakers making the pilgrimage to the planned tracks.
3d3853f256e02b8b5ef4153486aa756375e924eb.translatedText: 該項目的擬議建設預算在竣工時從 300 萬美元猛增到 1000 萬美元，立即增加了該場地吸引大量觀眾的壓力。不幸的是，賽道地處偏遠的沙漠位置，加上令人不舒服的炎熱天氣，驅走了大部分潛在顧客，賽馬活動也被放棄。該場地的狀況日益惡化，只有富有冒險精神的青少年和精打細算的電影製片人前往計劃的賽道朝聖。

03061960593c08b1156bdfd75be9bc5f08b80e29.sourceText: In 1997, after collecting dust and graffiti for decades, the site suffered the further indignity of an explosion set off for the film No Code of Conduct which blew out all of the glass in the facility and left the Phoenix Trotting Park littered with dead pigeons. This gruesome event may have been the most action this hubristic concrete shell ever saw.
03061960593c08b1156bdfd75be9bc5f08b80e29.translatedText: 1997年，在積滿灰塵和塗鴉數十年後，該場地因電影《無行為準則》引發的爆炸而遭受進一步的侮辱，爆炸炸毀了設施內的所有玻璃，鳳凰城快步公園裡散落著死鴿子。這可怕的事件可能是這個狂妄的混凝土外殼所見過的最激烈的行動。

b5dfd5a57eb7750cec61f6c3cf493809fb948b8a.sourceText: Update November 2017: The structure has been demolished.
b5dfd5a57eb7750cec61f6c3cf493809fb948b8a.translatedText: 2017 年 11 月更新：該結構已被拆除。

099113931fe54526ceeb44972e125f634abf6d5f.sourceText: Sweet Time Bakery is listed within Mekong Plaza in Mesa. This profile was generated from plaza directory sources and map-based verification, so direct business contact details may still be incomplete.

7c2c858b31f7fc9f6f34e13d626c9023dafc78ce.sourceText: In the early 20th century, some members of the U.S. Congress, pressured by lobbyists, feared that setting aside land for National Forests would starve the timber industry. As such, funding was minimal and the nascent U.S. Forest Service was forced to find creative solutions to complete their directive.
7c2c858b31f7fc9f6f34e13d626c9023dafc78ce.translatedText: 20世紀初，美國國會的一些議員迫於遊說者的壓力，擔心為國家森林留出土地會使木材工業挨餓。因此，資金很少，新生的美國林務局被迫尋找創意的解決方案來完成他們的指示。

42db9e6f0480d34e2eed46215f89ffc8e03c950e.sourceText: In the Kaibab National Forest, a large area spreading across both sides of the Grand Canyon, the Forest Service lacked the budget to build towers to spot the smoke of early fires. So it used the tall structures that were already there, the massive Ponderosa pine trees.
42db9e6f0480d34e2eed46215f89ffc8e03c950e.translatedText: 在凱巴布國家森林，橫跨大峽谷兩側的大片區域，林務局缺乏預算來建造塔來發現早期火災的煙霧。因此，它使用了已經存在的高大結構，巨大的黃松樹。

5f21aa9194a662bf8025efa4727e63dd1b90cbc7.sourceText: Forest Service employees would hike up to the highest vista in an area and from there would find the tallest tree. They would then construct a ladder against the side of the tree and saw off the top, building a platform on the flattened trunk.
5f21aa9194a662bf8025efa4727e63dd1b90cbc7.translatedText: 林務局員工會徒步到一個地區最高的視野，從那裡會找到最高的樹。然後，他們會在樹的側面搭建一個梯子，鋸掉頂部，在扁平的樹幹上建造一個平台。

91e9da4321637abaf87946bd78648a43e82ef2f9.sourceText: The tree platforms were equipped with a telephone, map, and compass. Each was staffed by two people: a lookout who kept an eye on the horizon for wisps of smoke, and a patrolman who would run towards early fires and attempt to put them out. If the patrolman was unable to put the fire out on their own, the lookout would use the telephone to call for more help. Dozens of these lookout trees were constructed by the Forest Service in the name of wildfire prevention.
91e9da4321637abaf87946bd78648a43e82ef2f9.translatedText: 樹平台配備了電話、地圖和指南針。每個消防局都有兩名工作人員：一名瞭望員，負責監視地平線是否有縷縷煙霧；一名巡邏員，負責跑向早期的火災並試圖將其撲滅。如果巡警無法自行撲滅大火，瞭望員會透過電話尋求更多協助。林務局以預防野火的名義建造了數十棵這樣的瞭望樹。

ff339c7b6cbc9feddb417226e95f77b861dec927.sourceText: Beginning in the 1930s, the Civilian Conservation Corps, a government program launched during the Great Depression, began constructing steel towers in National Forests to replace the lookout trees. The use of lookout trees continued through the 1940s, but as more steel towers were constructed the trees were eventually phased out and forgotten.
ff339c7b6cbc9feddb417226e95f77b861dec927.translatedText: 從 20 世紀 30 年代開始，大蕭條期間啟動的政府計畫「民間保護團」開始在國家森林中建造鋼塔以取代瞭望樹。瞭望樹的使用一直持續到 20 世紀 40 年代，但隨著越來越多的鋼塔建成，這些樹木最終被淘汰並被遺忘。

6ad26902a373a9624d4b3a0848a40d36b5ed3a76.sourceText: In 1987, the Forest Service began a survey of disused fire towers across the National Forests and included the old lookout trees. Of the dozens of tree towers that once formed a network across the Kaibab National Forest, only 11 were located. The others either had since deteriorated and become unrecognizable from the surrounding trees or were simply not found. The 11 remaining trees were added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1992.
6ad26902a373a9624d4b3a0848a40d36b5ed3a76.translatedText: 1987 年，林業局開始對國家森林中廢棄的消防塔進行調查，其中包括了舊的瞭望樹。凱巴布國家森林中曾有數十座樹塔形成網絡，但現在只找到 11 座。其他的要么已經惡化，從周圍的樹木中無法辨認，要么根本就沒有被發現。 1992 年，剩下的 11 棵樹被列入國家歷史名勝名錄。

15fcd711ae6e329003e35cf66ba29f304b72d876.sourceText: Standing on his newly purchased patch of bare Arizona desert in 1951, Grover Cleveland Thompson found the place to make his dreams come alive. Using abundant local resources of dirt, sand, rocks, broken crockery, Halloween masks, scrap metal and other artistic essentials, Grover spent the next several decades building a Gaudí-esque wonderland in Phoenix . He continued to work on the project right up until he passed away in 1977.
15fcd711ae6e329003e35cf66ba29f304b72d876.translatedText: 1951 年，格羅弗·克利夫蘭·湯普森 (Grover Cleveland Thompson) 站在他新買的亞利桑那州荒蕪的沙漠上，找到了實現夢想的地方。格羅佛利用當地豐富的泥土、沙子、岩石、破碎的陶器、萬聖節面具、廢金屬和其他藝術必需品等資源，在接下來的幾十年裡在鳳凰城建造了一座高第式的仙境。他繼續致力於這個項目，直到 1977 年去世。

7cdfded4ceac8c8ca24678f53920605803492ac6.sourceText: Later, Marion Blake lovingly preserved Thompsons rock garden not only from the ravages of time, but also from a project to gouge up its fragile wonders and relocate them to ASU. This quirky place was once a sparsely settled desert area 10 miles north of downtown Phoenix, just east of the now aging highway business district of Cave Creek Road.
7cdfded4ceac8c8ca24678f53920605803492ac6.translatedText: 後來，Marion Blake 精心保存了 Thompsons 岩石花園，不僅使其免受時間的破壞，而且還避免了將其脆弱的奇觀挖出來並將其搬遷到亞利桑那州立大學的計劃。這個奇特的地方曾經是一片人煙稀少的沙漠地區，位於鳳凰城市中心以北 10 英里處，位於現已老化的洞溪路 (Cave Creek Road) 高速公路商業區以東。

ec80700cb9bd865f501fa63e36f42e0e5308d09a.sourceText: On your way to and from the rock garden, keep your eyes open along Cave Creek Road for glimpses of architectural and natural features from a quieter time in the desert. Today, this gem is still owned by Blake. As of early 2025, she still occasionally conducts tours of the garden.
ec80700cb9bd865f501fa63e36f42e0e5308d09a.translatedText: 在往返岩石花園的途中，請沿著洞溪路 (Cave Creek Road) 睜大眼睛，欣賞沙漠中安靜時光的建築和自然景觀。如今，這顆寶石仍歸布萊克所有。截至 2025 年初，她仍然偶爾會帶領遊客參觀花園。

388b6a070f13887ace9f1087877fea5d5d6e8cb8.sourceText: Even if you can't get a personal tour with Blake, visitors are generally welcome to just drop by.
388b6a070f13887ace9f1087877fea5d5d6e8cb8.translatedText: 即使您無法與布萊克一起進行個人遊覽，通常也歡迎遊客順便過來。

d3d371b5ff548d45bf5adecbb5f590c505869e64.sourceText: Mosey down a long bumpy dirt road in Arizona's San Pedro Valley, and you'll find the Singing Wind Bookstore, located on a working cattle ranch and focusing on books of the American Southwest.
d3d371b5ff548d45bf5adecbb5f590c505869e64.translatedText: 沿著亞利桑那州聖佩德羅谷一條長長的、崎嶇不平的土路走下去，你會發現風歌書店，它位於一個正在運營的牧場上，主營美國西南部的書籍。

da3354468ff995fccffed546996ec30ee530a6b0.sourceText: The Singing Wind Bookstore is over 40 years old and specializes in books that celebrate the culture and writers of the southwest, including non-fiction, fiction, journalism, and more.
da3354468ff995fccffed546996ec30ee530a6b0.translatedText: 風歌書店已有 40 多年的歷史，專門銷售頌揚西南部文化和作家的書籍，包括非小說類、小說、新聞和文學作品。

f953ce5d14f01e0e2a8d205809574d1eb559a1dc.sourceText: Winifred Bundy and her husband purchased the Singing Wind Ranch in 1956 and after completion of a Master's Degree in library science and working to compile all the inventory, the Singing Wind Bookstore opened its doors in 1974.
f953ce5d14f01e0e2a8d205809574d1eb559a1dc.translatedText: Winifred Bundy 和她的丈夫於 1956 年購買了 Singing Wind Ranch，在完成圖書館學碩士學位並致力於編制所有庫存後，Singing Wind 書店於 1974 年開業。

9fdc1063e54db71f25a53dced0a30ce2ff59806b.sourceText: Bundy knows just about every regional author around, and her shop sells signed copies of most of her books. The shelves aren't labeled, and visitors must rely on a tour from Bundy or one of her staff to find what they are looking for.
9fdc1063e54db71f25a53dced0a30ce2ff59806b.translatedText: Bundy 幾乎認識周圍的每一位地區作家，她的書店出售她大部分書籍的簽名副本。書架上沒有標籤，遊客必須依靠邦迪或她的一名員工的帶領才能找到他們想要的東西。

e3f94e38ef7cad56c9e9b839386dab8344664777.sourceText: In the age of Amazon and Kindles, the Singing Wind Bookstore continues to stand the test of time, relying on nothing more than word-of-mouth marketing.
e3f94e38ef7cad56c9e9b839386dab8344664777.translatedText: 在亞馬遜和 Kindle 時代，歌風書店繼續經受住時間的考驗，僅依靠口碑行銷。

51444540270ab980a9c6a5f1bf97cfbe16ff97b5.sourceText: Find a summer evening adventure by visiting the Campbell Ave bridge over the Rillito river. Thousands of Mexican Free-Tailed bats take flight at sunset, filling the sky. You can stand above and watch them take flight or go on the Loop path and listen to them under the bridge.
51444540270ab980a9c6a5f1bf97cfbe16ff97b5.translatedText: 參觀裡利托河上的坎貝爾大道大橋，體驗夏日傍晚的冒險。數以千計的墨西哥無尾蝙蝠在日落時分飛翔，佈滿天空。您可以站在上面觀看它們飛行，也可以沿著環路在橋下聆聽它們的聲音。

bbf0a47a2456ee47e4f4b012c06f563226954c1b.sourceText: Tucson has bats under many bridges, but this one and the one at Pantano and Broadway bridge are marked with awesome bat art and informative signs. Great places to watch these amazing animals.
bbf0a47a2456ee47e4f4b012c06f563226954c1b.translatedText: 圖森的許多橋樑下都有蝙蝠，但這一座以及潘塔諾橋和百老匯橋上的那座都標有精美的蝙蝠藝術和資訊豐富的標誌。觀看這些神奇動物的好地方。

9ebbf0fd5bda320158fc9d4ee56f131f89e6059b.sourceText: There is a public parking zone right at the bridge site, on the southeast intersection, sometimes there are docents/students there to share more information with people around, never handle bats, but watching is wonderful.
9ebbf0fd5bda320158fc9d4ee56f131f89e6059b.translatedText: 橋邊有一個公共停車區，位於東南路口，有時會有講解員/學生在那裡與周圍的人分享更多信息，從不接觸蝙蝠，但觀看很精彩。

83dc3af3857c2ae283eaa21e0746b0741db65741.sourceText: "Giganticus Headicus," is a giant, tiki-style head constructed in 2004 by area artist Gregg Arnold. The statue is 14 feet tall and crafted from cement, chicken wire, and styrofoam. This unique work of art can be found in Antares Point near Kingman, Arizona , along Route 66. It's adjacent to the former Kozy Corner Trailer Park.
83dc3af3857c2ae283eaa21e0746b0741db65741.translatedText: 「Giganticus Headicus」是一個巨大的提基風格頭像，由地區藝術家 Gregg Arnold 於 2004 年製作。這座雕像高 14 英尺，由水泥、鐵絲網和聚苯乙烯泡沫塑膠製成。這件獨特的藝術品位於亞利桑那州金曼附近的 Antares Point，沿著 66 號公路。它毗鄰前 Kozy Corner 拖車公園。

0c9d4a8a514c6d8a6a389032c2e8383fc1cecb7b.sourceText: The main A-frame building where the head sits was originally a location for Nickerson Farms, a popular chain of restaurants/gift shops that existed between 1960 and early 1980. It was later repurposed into a gift shop that featured some Route 66 memorabilia and "Giganticus Headicus" themed gifts until it closed in 2020. There are also several old cars on the property and vintage gas pumps.
0c9d4a8a514c6d8a6a389032c2e8383fc1cecb7b.translatedText: 頭部所在的 A 框架主建築最初是尼克森農場 (Nickerson Farms) 的所在地，尼克森農場是一家受歡迎的連鎖餐廳/禮品店，存在於 1960 年至 1980 年初。後來被改造成禮品店，以一些路線為特色66 件紀念品和“Giganticus Headicus”主題禮品，直至 2020 年關閉。店內還有幾輛舊車和老式加油泵。

8edc2df8484dbd6ae3633a7d98a805def29f0e1b.sourceText: While the storefront is vacant as of 2021, the site is set to reopen as a gift shop and sculpture garden featuring more of Arnold's pieces in the near future.
8edc2df8484dbd6ae3633a7d98a805def29f0e1b.translatedText: 雖然店面截至 2021 年仍空置，但該網站將在不久的將來作為禮品店和雕塑花園重新開放，展示更多阿諾德的作品。

636e80876fe27cd437cc18d33fc13487cb3a6bd9.sourceText: While the ASU Art Museum primarily contains temporary exhibits, one of them is expected to remain there until the year 3015. That is because the Millennium Camera, installed in 2015, has the world’s longest exposure time of 1,000 years. (The current record for a completed exposure photo is a mere eight years and one month.) If successful, it will show a millennium of change at a single Tempe intersection in just one photograph. The ASU Art Museum has ambitiously committed to displaying the final photo in March 3015.
636e80876fe27cd437cc18d33fc13487cb3a6bd9.translatedText: 雖然亞利桑那州立大學藝術博物館主要展出臨時展品，但其中一件展品預計將保留到 3015 年。這是因為 2015 年安裝的千年相機擁有世界上最長的曝光時間，可達 1000 年。 （目前一張完整曝光照片的記錄僅為八年零一個月。）如果成功，只需一張照片即可顯示坦佩單一十字路口千年來的變化。亞利桑那州立大學藝術博物館雄心勃勃地承諾在 3015 年 3 月展示最終照片。

215e681b9e6f0d5074b0f633ce68a715acbff2d8.sourceText: Creator Jonathon Keats is an experimental philosopher and conceptual artist whose art and thought experiments often push the boundaries of traditional media and thought. This was evident from his debut work, “Twenty Four Hour Cogito,” in which he sat and thought in a gallery for 24 hours straight. One could buy his thoughts by the minute for an amount indexed to one’s own per-minute income. Among his other projects are a choreographed ballet for honeybees, an attempt at genetically engineering God, and copyrighting his mind as a unique neural network he himself had created.
215e681b9e6f0d5074b0f633ce68a715acbff2d8.translatedText: 創作者喬納森·濟慈 (Jonathon Keats) 是一位實驗哲學家和概念藝術家，他的藝術和思想實驗經常突破傳統媒體和思想的界限。這一點從他的處女作《二十四小時我思》中可以看出，在這幅作品中，他連續 24 小時坐在畫廊裡思考。人們可以按分鐘購買他的想法，費用與自己的每分鐘收入掛鉤。他的其他項目包括為蜜蜂編排的芭蕾舞、對上帝進行基因工程的嘗試，以及將他的思想版權為他自己創建的獨特神經網絡。

78b770091c1a3488f7aa7d558642f1ed3ab5a826.sourceText: The Millennium Camera was inspired by San Francisco, where Keats lives. Noticing rapid change due to gentrification, he wanted to create a medium that makes people more aware of gradual change. This way, he hopes that we become more aware of what we want to see preserved around us. He chose a pinhole camera design that was as low-tech as possible to prevent it from breaking. It is made of copper, which develops an oxidized protective layer over time, and the front interior is also covered with 24-karat gold which does not corrode. Rose madder is used as a pigment because it fades very slowly in the sunlight. Although there is no guarantee that the camera will work the first time, Keats hopes that future generations will improve on his design if it fails.
78b770091c1a3488f7aa7d558642f1ed3ab5a826.translatedText: 千年相機的靈感來自濟慈居住的舊金山。注意到中產階級化帶來的快速變化，他想創造一種媒介，讓人們更意識到漸進的改變。透過這種方式，他希望我們能夠更加意識到我們希望看到我們周圍保存什麼。他選擇了技術含量盡可能低的針孔相機設計，以防止其破裂。它由銅製成，隨著時間的推移會形成氧化保護層，正面內部也覆蓋有不會腐蝕的 24 克拉黃金。玫瑰茜草被用作顏料，因為它在陽光下褪色非常緩慢。雖然不能保證相機第一次就能工作，但濟慈希望未來的世代能夠改進他的設計，如果失敗的話。

f2a4ebad3a028800a192e7cc6b32efae96f32296.sourceText: Keats chose to install the Millennium Camera in Tempe because Arizona could be especially hard hit by climate change and a scarcity of water. He has also since created additional millennium cameras at Amherst College in Massachusetts, Lake Tahoe, and Tumamoc Hill in Tempe, and hopes to install more cameras in Los Angeles, China, and the Austrian Alps. Keats refers to all of them as a “global network observing our changing environment.”
f2a4ebad3a028800a192e7cc6b32efae96f32296.translatedText: 濟慈選擇在坦佩安裝千禧年相機，因為亞利桑那州可能受到氣候變遷和缺水的嚴重打擊。此後，他還在馬薩諸塞州的阿默斯特學院、太浩湖和坦佩的圖馬莫克山安裝了更多的千年相機，並希望在洛杉磯、中國和奧地利阿爾卑斯山安裝更多相機。濟慈將它們稱為「觀察我們不斷變化的環境的全球網絡」。

0acf4d168578682f6d448ea125272ee5e5974ad6.sourceText: One of the sources of fascination with this sundial goes back to the original claim that it was the largest sundial in the world when it was commemorated in 1959. Many claims have disputed this from the City of San Francisco to Sun City in Arizona, which both have sundials that are larger by measure.
0acf4d168578682f6d448ea125272ee5e5974ad6.translatedText: 這個日晷令人著迷的根源之一可以追溯到 1959 年紀念日最初聲稱它是世界上最大的日晷。從舊金山市到亞利桑那州太陽城，許多說法對此都存在爭議，這兩個城市都有更大的日晷。

c333f393737db6f23ec7098045bcf8b50d086191.sourceText: The 90-inch diameter base holds the gnomon which is 72 inches in length. The steel frame is covered with anodized copper. Designed by solar engineer John Yellot and architect Joe Wong, the sundial is time adjusted for local time at 27.7 minutes behind the meridian which is Mountain Standard Time. A smaller 1/48th scale model is on the site along with an equation of the timetable.
c333f393737db6f23ec7098045bcf8b50d086191.translatedText: 直徑 90 英吋的底座容納長度為 72 英吋的晷針。鋼框架覆蓋陽極氧化銅。日晷由太陽能工程師 John Yellot 和建築師 Joe Wong 設計，按照當地時間比子午線晚 27.7 分鐘（山地標準時間）進行時間調整。現場有一個較小的 1/48 比例模型以及時間表方程式。

63051998d2fda4ab2b35f3397b1dde3f6d9ada3a.sourceText: According to the local Kiwanis Club, the sundial property was acquired in 1976 and is maintained by the Kiwanis Club of Carefree. It is dedicated to the memory of a fellow member, Kenyon Turner Palmer.
63051998d2fda4ab2b35f3397b1dde3f6d9ada3a.translatedText: 根據當地 Kiwanis 俱樂部的說法，日晷財產於 1976 年獲得，並由 Carefree 的 Kiwanis 俱樂部維護。謹以此紀念一位會員凱尼恩‧特納‧帕爾默 (Kenyon Turner Palmer)。

99ecf5bc03cde1d09bb08979b1f30d5e6f707dd2.sourceText: A small mausoleum located on a windswept mountainside is the final resting place of a businessman-turned-astronomer whose work led to the discovery of Pluto.
99ecf5bc03cde1d09bb08979b1f30d5e6f707dd2.translatedText: 位于风吹拂的山腰上的一座小陵墓是一位商人出身的天文学家的最后安息之地，他的工作导致了冥王星的发现。

724368c14abce5eabca95882095eb7a4dddf0a10.sourceText: Just steps away from a historic telescope on the property of Flagstaff's Lowell Observatory , the small, domed structure contains the remains of Percival Lowell, a wealthy and connected member of a prominent Boston family. While his background included running cotton mills and diplomatic visits to Asia, Lowell became fascinated by what he thought were “canals” on Mars and decided, in his late 30s, to study astronomy and map them.
724368c14abce5eabca95882095eb7a4dddf0a10.translatedText: 距离弗拉格斯塔夫洛厄尔天文台的一台历史悠久的望远镜仅几步之遥，这座小型圆顶建筑内埋葬着珀西瓦尔·洛厄尔的遗体，珀西瓦尔·洛厄尔是波士顿一个显赫家族的富有且人脉广泛的成员。虽然洛厄尔的背景包括经营棉纺厂和对亚洲进行外交访问，但他对火星上的“运河”着迷，并在 30 多岁的时候决定研究天文学并绘制它们的地图。

ce62fd43cac82d12b3dc6123f7a3a154cf5e8898.sourceText: After building an observatory in 1894, Lowell spent the rest of his life studying the sky. And while his maps of the Martian canals have been disproved, his facility and research greatly added to our knowledge of our universe and led to the discovery of Pluto. Lowell theorized there was an unseen ninth planet and, though he died before Pluto was discovered, a member of his observatory staff, Clyde Tombaugh, was the one to do so.
ce62fd43cac82d12b3dc6123f7a3a154cf5e8898.translatedText: 在 1894 年建造了一座天文台後，洛威爾將餘生都花在了研究天空上。虽然他的火星运河地图已被证明是错误的，但他的设施和研究极大地增加了我们对宇宙的了解，并导致了冥王星的发现。洛厄尔推测存在一颗看不见的第九行星，尽管他在冥王星被发现之前就去世了，但他的天文台工作人员克莱德·汤博却是这样做的人。

2ef3bed34b504a7ec2d13aae89023cba199fbf89.sourceText: Lowell died in 1916. As his mausoleum was being constructed, his coffin sat out on the hill nearby in a burial vault. He was finally interred in 1923. Later on, the framework surrounding the pieces of stained glass in the mausoleum’s dome started to leak and rust in the Flagstaff weather, resulting in reddish color tracks that ran down its sides. While that tint was pretty scenic on fall evenings, the observatory trust decided in the late 1990s to add a cover for protection and weather-proofing, and they cleaned up the red streaks.
2ef3bed34b504a7ec2d13aae89023cba199fbf89.translatedText: 洛威爾於 1916 年去世。在建造他的陵墓時，他的棺材放在附近山上的一個墓穴裡。他最終於 1923 年被埋葬。後來，在弗拉格斯塔夫的天氣下，陵墓圓頂彩色玻璃周圍的框架開始洩漏並生鏽，導致其兩側出現淡紅色的痕跡。雖然這種色調在秋天的夜晚非常美麗，但天文台信託基金在 20 世紀 90 年代末決定添加一個保護罩和防風雨罩，並清除了紅色條紋。

042275eb5e2b152d0e8b337b027defeabc9ae89a.sourceText: You can still peek through the grate covering the door and look up at the blue and purple panes of stained glass that let in the light of the night sky that fascinated Percival so much.
042275eb5e2b152d0e8b337b027defeabc9ae89a.translatedText: 您仍然可以透過門上的格柵窺視，抬頭看到藍色和紫色的彩色玻璃窗，夜空的光線讓珀西瓦爾著迷。

9a4158cc43b42842d634c29a74efaceaa7d0deb5.sourceText: After Rose Eisendrath was refused entry to an Arizona resort for being Jewish, she bought 44 acres in the Valley of the Sun on which she built her own private paradise in 1930. The house changed hands several times and fell into disrepair after Eisendrath’s death in 1936, but today this architectural gem has been fully restored and serves as a center for studying water conservation.
9a4158cc43b42842d634c29a74efaceaa7d0deb5.translatedText: 羅絲·艾森德拉斯 (Rose Eisendrath) 因是猶太人而被拒絕進入亞利桑那州的一處度假勝地後，她在太陽谷購買了 44 英畝土地，並於 1930 年在上面建造了自己的私人天堂。 1936 年艾森德拉斯 (Eisendrath) 去世後，這棟房子幾經轉手，年久失修，但今天，這座建築瑰寶已得到全面修復，並成為水利研究中心。

5e327856c1ac601e137eb447ba77c875a2927a67.sourceText: Long before Frank Lloyd Wright discovered the beauty and potential of the desert surrounding Phoenix , Arizona, wealthy Chicagoans like Eisendrath flocked to winter getaways in the Southwest. The widow of a wealthy glove maker, Eisendrath hired architect Robert T. Evans to build her a desert oasis overlooking the Salt River and the Superstition Mountains in what is now known as the “Pueblo Revival” style.
5e327856c1ac601e137eb447ba77c875a2927a67.translatedText: 早在弗蘭克·勞埃德·賴特 (Frank Lloyd Wright) 發現水利之美和潛力之前在亞利桑那州菲尼克斯周圍的沙漠中，像艾森德拉斯這樣的富有的芝加哥人紛紛湧向西南部的冬季度假勝地。艾森德拉斯是一位富有的手套製造商的遺孀，她聘請建築師羅伯特·T·埃文斯 (Robert T. Evans) 為她建造了一片沙漠綠洲，俯瞰著鹽河和迷信山脈，這種風格現在被稱為“普韋布洛復興”風格。

96c2a7456854ba7dbdd3e9b3e1861ad31d37fef4.sourceText: She called her Sonoran retreat Lomaki which in the Hopi language translates to “beautiful home.” With 5,500 square feet of living space, a dumbwaiter, citrus grove, and swimming pool, the house was designed to entertain. All were welcome in Rose’s home, including the hotel manager who had turned her away.
96c2a7456854ba7dbdd3e9b3e1861ad31d37fef4.translatedText: 她將她的索諾蘭度假勝地稱為洛馬基 (Lomaki)，在霍皮語中意為「美麗的家園」。這棟房子擁有 5,500 平方英尺的起居空間、升降機、柑橘園和游泳池，專為娛樂而設計。羅斯的家裡歡迎所有人，包括拒絕她的酒店經理。

d9eb9e0efa39d9b70e48399d620d84d05d852cef.sourceText: The Eisendrath house was the first of Evans’ pueblo-style homes in Phoenix, where he had been living since 1923 and building an impressive list of wealthy clients. Famous for designing the Jokake Resort, Evans also designed the pool at the Arizona Biltmore, an iconic Frank Lloyd Wright commission. Sadly, many of the homes designed by Evans have been lost, a fate narrowly escaped by the Eisendrath house.
d9eb9e0efa39d9b70e48399d620d84d05d852cef.translatedText: 艾森德拉斯別墅是埃文斯在菲尼克斯的第一座普韋布洛風格住宅，他自 1923 年以來一直住在那裡，並建立了一系列令人印象深刻的富有客戶。埃文斯因設計 Jokake 度假村而聞名，他還設計了標誌性的弗蘭克·勞埃德·賴特 (Frank Lloyd Wright) 委託項目亞利桑那比爾特莫爾 (Arizona Biltmore) 的游泳池。遺憾的是，埃文斯設計的許多房屋都已遺失，艾森德拉斯房屋僥倖逃脫了命運。

5001abf11685abd99e6a902b55bb77baca0d5457.sourceText: When it was bought by the City of Tempe in 2001, the house was an erstwhile artist colony that had been inadequately maintained for decades. The adobe was “melting” back into the desert and the home had even become a hideaway for a marijuana hydroponics operation. The Tempe community and the Rio Salado Foundation spent 10 years and $4.3 million to preserve this home, which is now on the National Register of Historic Places.
5001abf11685abd99e6a902b55bb77baca0d5457.translatedText: 當它在 2001 年被坦佩市購買時，這棟房子以前是藝術家的聚集地，幾十年來一直沒有充分的維護。土坯「融化」回沙漠，家裡甚至成為大麻水耕作業的藏身處。坦佩社區和 Rio Salado 基金會花了 10 年和 430 萬美元來保護這棟住宅，現在已列入國家歷史名勝名錄。

6525cdf8a513cb56e275b910ad13a7c3e12555e8.sourceText: Historic preservation, however, is only part of the Eisendrath house’s resurrection story. Redesigned to educate desert dwellers about water conservation, it is now a centerpiece of the Carl Hayden Campus for Sustainability. In partnership with the local power company and nearby water treatment plant, the house sponsors conservation classes and features exhibit galleries on sustainable living, education desperately needed by a desert region population that has grown from 61,000 in 1930 to over 4.2 million today.
6525cdf8a513cb56e275b910ad13a7c3e12555e8.translatedText: 歷史保護只是艾森德拉斯住宅復興故事的一部分。它經過重新設計，旨在對沙漠居民進行節水教育，現在是卡爾海登永續發展園區的核心。該住宅與當地電力公司和附近的水處理廠合作，主辦保護課程，並設有關於可持續生活和沙漠地區迫切需要的教育的展覽館，該地區的人口已從 1930 年的 61,000 人增加到今天的 420 萬以上。

d09a9ad2e6aa0b7f1626a596b4830b6adecb653e.sourceText: Listed in the Chinese section of the AZ AANHPI Directory for Glendale, Arizona. Public contact phone: 623-215-4478.
d09a9ad2e6aa0b7f1626a596b4830b6adecb653e.translatedText: 列於亞利桑那州格倫代爾市 AZ AANHPI 名錄的中文部分。公共聯絡電話：623-215-4478。

8ac098d4bc7015de49a284380bc09018d2ed94ba.sourceText: More than most Arizona cities, Florence, Arizona is closely tied to the Old West. Many of the buildings in its historic downtown date back to Arizona’s days as a territory, and there may be no finer example than the old Pinal County Courthouse that is now known today as McFarland State Historic Park.
8ac098d4bc7015de49a284380bc09018d2ed94ba.translatedText: 與亞利桑那州的大多數城市相比，亞利桑那州的佛羅倫薩與老西部的聯繫更加緊密。歷史悠久的市中心的許多建築都可以追溯到亞利桑那州作為一個領土的時代，其中最好的例子莫過於舊皮納爾縣法院，現在被稱為麥克法蘭州立歷史公園。

acb315bd75e190e592424e8fb6acec2519f78165.sourceText: The building was designed by Levi Ruggles, known as the “Father of Florence, Arizona.” (Coincidentally, he was also the father of Florence Ruggles. He liked the name.) Like many territory buildings, the courthouse was made of adobe bricks sourced from nearby soil and lumber came by wagon from northern Arizona. The goal was to create a building grand enough to give Florence some heft as more than a frontier outpost. It was completed in 1878 at the cost of $2,700 and remained the city’s courthouse until a newer building opened in 1891.
acb315bd75e190e592424e8fb6acec2519f78165.translatedText: 該建築由被譽為「亞利桑那州佛羅倫薩之父」的萊維·拉格斯 (Levi Ruggles) 設計。 （巧合的是，他也是弗洛倫斯·拉格爾斯的父親。他喜歡這個名字。）像許多領地建築一樣，法院大樓是用來自附近土壤的土坯磚和從亞利桑那州北部運來的木材建造的。我們的目標是建造一座足夠宏偉的建築，讓佛羅倫薩不僅僅是一個邊境前哨基地。它於 1878 年竣工，耗資 2,700 美元，一直是該市的法院大樓，直到 1891 年一座新建築投入使用。

a39f9d11905ff5d446df6fce6db4947caccae9d2.sourceText: After its days as a courthouse, the building was used as a jail and county hospital for nearly 40 years, and then later as a welfare center and boarding home. It fell vacant until a movement sprang up to turn it into a museum, led by one of the most significant figures in Arizona history, Ernest W. McFarland. After moving to Arizona, he got his political start in Pinal County, being elected county attorney and later judge. “Mac” McFarland had designs on higher office, though, and ran for the United States Senate as a Democrat. He won the race, becoming “Freshman Senator of the Baby State,” and would serve two terms in the Senate, eventually becoming Majority Leader until losing to Barry Goldwater in 1952. He would then run for Governor of Arizona, and win, and would eventually be named to the Arizona Supreme Court, making him the only figure known to serve his state in the highest office of all three branches of government.
a39f9d11905ff5d446df6fce6db4947caccae9d2.translatedText: 這棟建築在作為法院大樓後，被用作監獄和縣立醫院近 40 年，後來又被用作福利中心和寄宿之家。它一直空著，直到一場運動興起，將其變成博物館，由亞利桑那州歷史上最重要的人物之一歐內斯特·W·麥克法蘭領導。搬到亞利桑那州後，他在皮納爾縣開始了自己的政治生涯，當選為縣檢察官，後來被選為法官。不過，「麥克」麥克法蘭有意擔任更高的職務，並以民主黨人身分競選美國參議員。他贏得了競選，成為“嬰兒州的新參議員”，並在參議院任職兩屆，最終成為多數黨領袖，直到 1952 年輸給巴里·戈德華特。然後，他競選亞利桑那州州長，獲勝，最終被任命為亞利桑那州最高法院法官，使他成為已知的唯一一位在政府三個部門的最高職位上為該州服務的人物。

026e34373819622fc05877a459e822b68a0deb22.sourceText: Among many passions, Mac signed a bill to create a State Parks system in 1957. He had one site in mind. He bought the courthouse personally and donated it to Arizona State Parks along with personal effects. Today, the park has the dubious honor of being Arizona’s least visited state park . Those who do make it will learn about the story of Ernest McFarland, the courthouse, and the early history of Arizona. As Mac himself said at the 1979 dedication, “this old building…stands as an example of the ability and the character of those who built it. It is also a place to see where history was made in Arizona.”
026e34373819622fc05877a459e822b68a0deb22.translatedText: 在眾多熱情中，麥克簽署了一項創建州的法案1957 年的公園系統。他心中有一個地點。他親自購買了法院大樓，並將其與個人物品一起捐贈給亞利桑那州立公園。如今，該公園有幸成為亞利桑那州遊客最少的州立公園。那些成功的人將了解歐內斯特·麥克法蘭的故事、法院和亞利桑那州的早期歷史。正如 Mac 本人在 1979 年的落成典禮上所說，“這座古老的建築……是建造它的人的能力和品格的典範。它也是見證亞​​利桑那州創造歷史的地方。”

344a64dc5097938c61cbff3a181f9e33fee0a831.sourceText: The small mining town of Clifton, Arizona , had a problem. When people were convicted of crimes there or in the neighboring town of Morenci, they weren't sentenced to time in prison. Instead, they were ordered to work for a certain amount of time in the copper mines that fueled the area's economy.
344a64dc5097938c61cbff3a181f9e33fee0a831.translatedText: 亞利桑那州的採礦小鎮克利夫頓遇到了一個問題。當人們在那裡或鄰近的莫倫西鎮被定罪時，他們不會被判處監禁。相反，他們被命令在銅礦工作一段時間，為該地區的經濟提供動力。

d31ca0a58505ea394658b4dcc937909118d5e330.sourceText: The problem was that many of the convicted criminals would simply flee the area rather than report to work and toil in the subterranean tunnels. So, in 1881, Clifton decided to build a prison that no one would be able to escape from. One that was built underground, and into the side of a granite cliff.
d31ca0a58505ea394658b4dcc937909118d5e330.translatedText: 問題是，許多被定罪的罪犯只是逃離該地區，而不是去上班並在地下隧道中勞動。因此，1881年，克利夫頓決定建造一座無人能逃脫的監獄。監獄建在地下，位於花崗岩懸崖的一側。

09db27f4148fa25ad7e2f10b51cc441b20e508d7.sourceText: The town hired local stonemason Margarito Varela to construct the jail. Using a pickax and explosives, Varela constructed a tunnel that led below ground and into a cavernous room. The cavern was split into two cells: a smaller one for dangerous criminals and a larger one for those charged with less serious crimes. Each had a window to let in fresh air and some light, but the windows were located 10 feet above the cavern floor and connected to the cells by small tunnels. To finish it up, Varela bolted heavy iron bars and doors into the rock.
09db27f4148fa25ad7e2f10b51cc441b20e508d7.translatedText: 鎮上聘請了當地石匠 Margarito Varela 來建造監獄。瓦雷拉用鎬和炸藥建造了一條通往地下並進入洞穴房間的隧道。洞穴被分成兩間牢房：一間較小的牢房關押危險的罪犯，另一間較大的牢房關押犯有較輕罪行的人。每個房間都有一個窗戶，可以讓新鮮空氣和一些光線進入，但窗戶位於洞穴地面上方 10 英尺處，並透過小隧道與牢房連接。為了完成它，瓦雷拉將沉重的鐵柵欄和門用螺栓固定在岩石上。

d4b6428303b74e4e6b4b43917439c476adf180a6.sourceText: Unverified local tradition says that when Varela finished constructing the jail, he was paid for his work and went to a local dance hall to drink and celebrate. Later, a very drunk Varela reportedly began happily firing his gun up into the air to get people's attention to tell them about his completed project. The owner of the dance hall was also a deputy sheriff and arrested Varela, making him the first occupant of the jail he built.
d4b6428303b74e4e6b4b43917439c476adf180a6.translatedText: 未經證實的當地傳統稱，當巴雷拉建成監獄後，他獲得了工作報酬，並前往當地的舞廳喝酒慶祝。據報道，後來，喝得酩酊大醉的瓦雷拉開始高興地向空中開槍，以引起人們的注意，告訴他們他已完成的項目。舞廳的老闆也是一名副警長，他逮捕了瓦雷拉，使他成為他建造的監獄的第一位居住者。

47c627d4e5d46f11cb00ab8abc33158b5155815b.sourceText: The jail was used until 1906 when a massive flood struck the area. The subterranean jail began to fill with water and the people incarcerated within had to be saved by breaking the bars off the windows and lowering ropes down to pull them out. The prison was filled with so much sediment and debris afterward that it was abandoned.
47c627d4e5d46f11cb00ab8abc33158b5155815b.translatedText: 這座監獄一直使用到 1906 年該地區發生大洪水時。地下監獄開始充滿水，被關在裡面的人必須透過打破窗戶上的柵欄並放下繩索將他們拉出來來拯救。這座監獄後來充滿瞭如此多的沉積物和碎片，最終被廢棄。

4f6af46a346b596348e7681ceb743950fa143221.sourceText: In 1929, the town began the process of restoring the old jail as a preserved piece of history, and in 1962, the state of Arizona placed a historic plaque out in front. The jail, along with the rest of Clifton's historic downtown, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1990.
4f6af46a346b596348e7681ceb743950fa143221.translatedText: 1929 年，該鎮開始修復舊監獄，將其作為歷史的一部分，1962 年，亞利桑那州在監獄前放置了一塊歷史牌匾。 1990 年，這座監獄與克利夫頓歷史悠久的市中心的其他地方一起被列入國家歷史名勝名錄。

66d1c1c6bd97768d1a9ba41b78b41aff74a7fc2f.sourceText: YZ's KTV Karaoke Cafe is listed within Three Fountains Plaza in Mesa. This profile was generated from plaza directory sources and map-based verification, so direct business contact details may still be incomplete.
66d1c1c6bd97768d1a9ba41b78b41aff74a7fc2f.translatedText: YZ的KTV卡拉OK咖啡廳位於梅薩三泉廣場內。此設定檔是根據廣場目錄來源和基於地圖的驗證產生的，因此直接業務聯絡詳細資訊可能仍然不完整。

f43c44d643c38d85866859feae50b457543f0f22.sourceText: Heart of the Rocks Loop (part of the Chiricahua National Monument), is a trail that allows access to a hidden geological gem near the border of Mexico and Arizona.
f43c44d643c38d85866859feae50b457543f0f22.translatedText: 岩石之心環路（奇里卡瓦國家紀念碑的一部分）是一條小徑，可通往墨西哥和亞利桑那州邊境附近隱藏的地質瑰寶。

4ee5e72dec63ba78f32cdbfa41177e5831e84e5d.sourceText: For an easy and quick experience, just drive to Massai Point for some cool historical facts, spectacular views, and interactive equipment. Then take the Heart of the Rock Loop which goes deep down into a canyon-like structure, then leads you upwards and back into the astonishing rock formations!
4ee5e72dec63ba78f32cdbfa41177e5831e84e5d.translatedText: 要輕鬆快速地體驗，只需開車前往馬賽角即可了解一些很酷的歷史事實、壯觀的景色和互動設備。然後走“岩石之心環路”，深入峽谷狀結構，然後帶您向上並返回令人驚嘆的岩層！

e80811d6a92195a088d95aa89042a77db2d79722.sourceText: Once you arrive at the National Park (no fee to enter), there is a gift shop, running water, clean bathrooms, and maps. Be sure to wear shoes with good grips as the trail has a lot of rocks and uneven ground.
e80811d6a92195a088d95aa89042a77db2d79722.translatedText: 到達國家公園（免費進入）後，這裡有一家禮品店、自來水、乾淨的浴室和地圖。請務必穿著抓地力好的鞋子，因為步道上有許多岩石且地面不平坦。

e5889a18147fad9302eaccf873128fbd94506e8b.sourceText: Quartzsite, Arizona, is a small town with a thing for camels. The town’s welcome sign is adorned with camels; its graveyard is the final resting place for Hadji Ali, a camel herder for the U.S. military; and just off of the 10 freeway sits Georgette, a scrap metal camel with ties to a fascinating bit of folklore: Arizona's Red Ghost.
e5889a18147fad9302eaccf873128fbd94506e8b.translatedText: 亞利桑那州的誇茨賽特 (Quartzsite) 是一座以駱駝為生的小鎮。小鎮的歡迎標誌上裝飾著駱駝；它的墓地是美軍駱駝牧人哈吉·阿里的最後安息之地； 10 號高速公路旁停著一隻廢金屬駱駝喬吉特，它與一個迷人的民間傳說有關：亞利桑那州的紅幽靈。

ac7dfc97d209c7b8dc0ef994b6022deff9893556.sourceText: In the 1880s, stories spread throughout Arizona of a giant red horse with a devil on its back. The Red Ghost trampled a woman to death at one campground, tore through a second campground, and supposedly flipped over two freight wagons at a third. At the scene of each event were signs of the creature: enormous hoof marks larger than any horse, and strands of red hair.
ac7dfc97d209c7b8dc0ef994b6022deff9893556.translatedText: 在 1880 年代，亞利桑那州各地流傳著一匹巨大的紅馬背上騎著魔鬼的故事。紅鬼在一個露營地踩死了一名婦女，撕毀了第二個露營地，據稱還在第三個露營地掀翻了兩輛貨車。每次事件的現場都有這種生物的痕跡：比任何馬都大的巨大蹄印，以及一縷紅毛。

ffef96a268e5eba73eb327515f02c45e623b40e7.sourceText: Stories of the Red Ghost rampaging all over the territory lasted for a decade, until a farmer found it: a red camel grazing with the skeletal remains of a man strapped to its back. The camel was likely a straggler, released from Hadji Ali’s team after the government abandoned the U.S. Camel Corps. The Red Ghost mystery was mostly solved, though no one knows who roped the corpse to the camel’s back, or why.
ffef96a268e5eba73eb327515f02c45e623b40e7.translatedText: 紅鬼在這片土地上肆虐的故事持續了十年，直到一位農民發現了它：一頭紅駱駝正在吃草，背上綁著一個人的骸骨。這頭駱駝很可能是一隻掉隊的駱駝，是在政府放棄美國駱駝軍團後從哈吉·阿里的團隊中釋放出來的。紅幽靈之謎已基本解開，但沒有人知道是誰將屍體用繩子綁在駱駝背上，也不知道為什麼。

058f8264814a3a88111913fc79293b8942f7131b.sourceText: Quartzsite, which became known for its camel crossings, bears two reminders of that infamous ruby camel. One is a marker on top of Hadji Ali’s grave. Just around the corner and down the road from “Hi Jolly’s” grave, guarding a local gem store, stands the other. Her name is Georgette, a life-sized camel sculpture created from assorted car and motorcycle parts, and painted a deep red.
058f8264814a3a88111913fc79293b8942f7131b.translatedText: 因駱駝穿越而聞名的石英岩上有兩個關於那隻臭名昭著的紅寶石駱駝的遺跡。其中一個是哈吉·阿里墳墓頂上的一個標記。就在「Hi Jolly」墳墓的轉角處，沿著路走下去，守護著當地的一家寶石店。她的名字叫喬吉特，這是一座真人大小的駱駝雕塑，由各種汽車和摩托車零件製成，並塗成深紅色。

5ba78ae13c0605107e206194f056b049aca953a1.sourceText: Hung's Hair Design by Victor is listed within Mekong Plaza in Mesa. This profile was generated from plaza directory sources and map-based verification, so direct business contact details may still be incomplete.
5ba78ae13c0605107e206194f056b049aca953a1.translatedText: Hung's Hair Design by Victor 位於梅薩的湄公河廣場內。此設定檔是根據廣場目錄來源和基於地圖的驗證產生的，因此直接業務聯絡詳細資訊可能仍然不完整。

2626405a83d389f558d906f527bdcfd100f03032.sourceText: Located within the University of Arizona’s Fine Arts Complex in Tucson , the Center for Creative Photography (CCP) is a major institution dedicated to the study and preservation of photography. The center opened in 1975, after a meeting between legendary photographer Ansel Adams and university president John Schaefer. Today, the 55,000-square-foot facility houses a massive collection of materials celebrating the art and history of photography .
2626405a83d389f558d906f527bdcfd100f03032.translatedText: 創意攝影中心 (CCP) 位於圖森的亞利桑那大學美術中心內，是致力於研究和保存攝影的主要機構。傳奇攝影師安塞爾亞當斯 (Ansel Adams) 與大學校長約翰謝弗 (John Schaefer) 會面後，該中心於 1975 年開業。如今，這個佔地 55,000 平方英尺的設施收藏了大量慶祝攝影藝術和歷史的資料。

23f3f170226a4973214ab1ea3a4b2e6391f7ab01.sourceText: The center maintains more than 270 archival collections and more than 110,000 individual works by some of the most renowned photographers in history, including the aforementioned Adams, as well as Edward Steichen, Paul Strand, W. Eugene Smith, Richard Avedon, Louise Dahl-Wolfe, and more. All told, there are more than 8 million archival objects here—including negatives, memorabilia, and correspondence—making the center one of the most significant institutions dedicated to the history and preservation of the medium.
23f3f170226a4973214ab1ea3a4b2e6391f7ab01.translatedText: 該中心保存著 270 多個檔案藏品和 110,000 多件歷史上最著名的攝影師的個人作品，包括前面提到的 Adams，以及 Edward Steichen、Paul Strand、W. Eugene Smith、Richard Avedon、Louise達爾-沃爾夫等。總而言之，這裡有超過 800 萬件檔案物品，包括底片、紀念品和信件，使該中心成為致力於媒介歷史和保護的最重要機構之一。

fcbd8e1d0c778d9e6c9782378fdb14e89d6c0ad0.sourceText: While the CCP is an academic institution—supporting researchers and students alike—it also has a public gallery with rotating exhibitions so visitors can engage with the vast collection, learning not only about photography’s aesthetic value but the way it can shed light on social movements and tell compelling stories.
fcbd8e1d0c778d9e6c9782378fdb14e89d6c0ad0.translatedText: 雖然 CCP 是一個學術機構，為研究人員和學生提供支持，但它還設有一個輪流展覽的公共畫廊，以便遊客可以與大量藏品互動，不僅了解攝影的美學價值，還了解攝影如何揭示社會運動和社會運動。講述引人入勝的故事。

5355350981098e92f3038a0246eb34e196c19ea0.sourceText: Visitors hours are Wednesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
5355350981098e92f3038a0246eb34e196c19ea0.translatedText: 訪客開放時間為週三至週六，上午 10 點至下午 4:30。

c08f89581edc069c625fe74b6e16af42f8d73950.sourceText: Step into this museum, and you'll find a dynamic showcase that tells the story of how ancient populations moved through the region. You'll see ancient artifacts from throughout Arizona , as the museum is made of exhibits featuring displays of items such as pottery, arrowheads, textiles, and more. The building also holds a working archaeological lab where volunteer curators provide assistance to fellow archaeologists and researchers working in the field.
c08f89581edc069c625fe74b6e16af42f8d73950.translatedText: 走進這個博物館，您會發現一個充滿活力的展示，講述古代人口如何穿越該地區的故事。您將看到來自亞利桑那州各地的古代文物，因為博物館的展品包括陶器、箭頭、紡織品等。該建築還設有一個工作考古實驗室，志工館長為在該領域工作的考古學家和研究人員提供協助。

e6a7720a39025a1c6799526d8576bd6e80fbfbd0.sourceText: The Verde Valley Archaeology Center is a nonprofit organization comprised of a museum and archaeological lab facility. The center opened its doors in a building given by the Town of Camp Verde in 2009. Since its opening, the organization has widened public access to historic items found in the Verde Valley.
e6a7720a39025a1c6799526d8576bd6e80fbfbd0.translatedText: 佛得谷考古中心是一個非營利組織，由博物館和考古實驗室設施組成。該中心於 2009 年在佛得角鎮捐贈的一棟建築內開業。自開放以來，該組織擴大了公眾對佛得角山谷中發現的歷史物品的接觸範圍。

e652b1cb612b71398234d948e154b4c85f6a559f.sourceText: A timeline exhibit provides information on the inhabitants of the Verde Valley from Paleo-Indians (11,500 to 9,000 BC) through the current Native American presence of the Yavapai-Apache Nation. A Sinagua Exhibit showcases artifacts illustrating the Sinaguan history and culture from 650 to 1450. This is supplemented with a U.S. Forest Service Honanki Exhibit of artifacts from the Honanki Heritage Site within the Coconino National Forest.
e652b1cb612b71398234d948e154b4c85f6a559f.translatedText: 時間軸展覽提供了關於佛得角山谷居民從古印第安人（公元前 11,500 至 9,000 年）到目前美洲原住民亞瓦派-阿帕奇民族的資訊。西納瓜展覽展示了 650 年至 1450 年西納瓜歷史和文化的文物。美國林務局 Honanki 展覽則對來自可科尼諾國家森林內 Honanki 遺址的文物進行了補充。

936162092cb1c49ddb1b7e31b0a2b91dca0f29ac.sourceText: An adornments exhibit displays various items worn by the Sinagua Culture, such as shell bracelets and necklaces, as well as pendants made from a variety of materials. The tools of archaeology exhibit provides information on the diagnostic value of various types of pottery sherds found throughout the area. A map illustrates the vast distances from which pottery has been found in the Verde Valley. This exhibit also includes a tree ring sample on loanfrom the Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research at the University of Arizona in Tucson .
936162092cb1c49ddb1b7e31b0a2b91dca0f29ac.translatedText: 装饰品展览展示了西纳瓜文化所佩戴的各种物品，例如贝壳手镯和项链，以及由各种材料制成的吊坠。考古工具展览提供了有关该地区发现的各种类型陶片的诊断价值的信息。一张地图显示了在维德山谷发现陶器的遥远距离。本次展览还包括从位于图森的亚利桑那大学年轮研究实验室借来的年轮样本。

1443605d7a6bc4cbde153ccbfef1a9ad742301ae.sourceText: Exhibits are rotating throughout the year and even include art displays and masterpieces by artists such as Paul Dyck, American painter of Southwestern themes.
1443605d7a6bc4cbde153ccbfef1a9ad742301ae.translatedText: 展品全年輪換，甚至包括美國西南主題畫家保羅·戴克 (Paul Dyck) 等藝術家的藝術展覽和傑作。

369febdf8c804c1a17cc39e750fa08fc0bb43236.sourceText: SP Crater gets overlooked for a few reasons. The neighboring volcano, Sunset Crater, is a bit more picturesque with its forest setting, and has national park status. SP Crater is off by itself on private ranchland, but the landowners permit visitors to check out this perfect example of a cinder cone and its 4.5-mile lava flow.
369febdf8c804c1a17cc39e750fa08fc0bb43236.translatedText: SP Crater 因一些原因而被忽視。鄰近的日落火山口火山風景如畫，擁有森林環境，並具有國家公園地位。 SP 火山口位於私人牧場上，但土地所有者允許遊客參觀這個火山灰錐的完美範例及其 4.5 英里的熔岩流。

d98ae5a696a559bb680be8c85ba7ec1f4d733da2.sourceText: The crater was eloquently named by 1880s rancher and landowner of the cinder cone C.J Babbit after what he felt the extinct volcano resembled: shit pot. This became the name that locals used to call the mountain, but mapmakers chose to not spell this out explicitly, instead opting for modesty and abbreviating it. Unlike the volcano in nearby Sunset Crater National Monument, you can climb to the top of SP Crater, and if you're sure-footed, you can even drop down inside of it.
d98ae5a696a559bb680be8c85ba7ec1f4d733da2.translatedText: 1880 年代的牧場主兼火山灰錐地主 C.J Babbit 根據他認為這座死火山的相似之處，將火山口命名為「屎罐」。這成為當地人用來稱呼這座山的名字，但地圖製作者選擇不明確地拼寫出來，而是選擇謙虛地縮寫它。與附近的日落火山口國家保護區 (Sunset Crater National Monument) 的火山不同，您可以爬到 SP 火山口 (SP Crater) 的頂部，如果您腳步穩健，甚至可以從裡面掉下來。

190d067e56def8587c5669d8d53689a649f6393f.sourceText: The peak rises up from the surrounding desert to a height of 820 feet. Volcanologists estimate SP Crater is between 65,000 and 71,000 years old.
190d067e56def8587c5669d8d53689a649f6393f.translatedText: 山峰從周圍的沙漠中拔地而起，高達 820 英尺。火山學家估計 SP 火山口的年齡在 65,000 到 71,000 年。

750f3adaafdbd020088f646eef2be45c11974551.sourceText: A sign reads "No Trespassing," though it is evident that few heed the notice.
750f3adaafdbd020088f646eef2be45c11974551.translatedText: 一塊牌子上寫著“禁止侵入”，但顯然很少有人注意到這個通知。

5940205d40de751dca61ba92f6ce57874bf0af6a.sourceText: The Domes were built to facilitate the manufacturing of computers back in the late 1970s to the early 1980s but were never completed, as is evident from a couple of foundations that were started and left to molder. One of the buildings is shaped like a flying saucer, and the other three are as if spheres were joined together, looking like huge concrete caterpillars.
5940205d40de751dca61ba92f6ce57874bf0af6a.translatedText: 圓頂是在 20 世紀 70 年代末到 80 年代初為了方便電腦的製造而建造的，但從未完工，從幾個已啟動並留待模製的地基可以明顯看出。其中一棟建築形狀像飛碟，另外三棟建築彷彿球體連接在一起，看起來像巨大的混凝土毛毛蟲。

0ae890502a4d8b6c97be974302698650dcea191b.sourceText: Talk from the locals about the domes concerns ritualistic witchcraft and satanic worship. "Stay out of there and don't go into the tunnels" is the refrain, and indeed there are tunnels under the eastern end of this facility. But despite all the stories, whether anything more sinister than underage beer-drinking, ghost stories, and the occasional squatter spending the night has ever happened is unknown.
0ae890502a4d8b6c97be974302698650dcea191b.translatedText: 當地人談論這些圓頂涉及儀式巫術和撒旦崇拜。人們常說“遠離那裡，不要進入隧道”，事實上，該設施的東端下方有隧道。但儘管有這些故事，是否還有比未成年人喝啤酒、鬼故事和偶爾佔屋者過夜更險惡的事情發生過，我們不得而知。

4010feebf70ea725e69b41fac4213df34ebcd9ea.sourceText: Nonetheless, staying out of the tunnels is probably good advice.
4010feebf70ea725e69b41fac4213df34ebcd9ea.translatedText: 儘管如此，遠離隧道可能是個好建議。

294f1f5b869014c8c4ba110aa5f58dcfdbfe755f.sourceText: Update January 2018: One dome has collapsed, and the city has ordered the destruction of the domes. They will not stand much longer and have been gated in now as well.
294f1f5b869014c8c4ba110aa5f58dcfdbfe755f.translatedText: 2018 年 1 月更新：一個圓頂已經倒塌，市政府已下令摧毀這些圓頂。它們不會再存在太久，現在也已被封閉。

15bbd4bc158de3f4895e0496582c36bf39a7ef65.sourceText: Update November 2019: The domes, despite being ordered for demolition, are still standing. For any potential visitors, please note that the domes are on private property, and being on the property without permission and paying an entry fee will (according to reports by other visitors) result in local law enforcement trespassing you, with the potential for arrest or fine.
15bbd4bc158de3f4895e0496582c36bf39a7ef65.translatedText: 2019 年 11 月更新：儘管已下令拆除，但圓頂仍矗立著。對於任何潛在的遊客，請注意，圓頂屬於私人財產，未經許可進入該財產並支付入場費將（根據其他遊客的報告）導致當地執法部門侵入您，並可能被逮捕或罰款。

b89299fa2f2c27125e55b6d945b689ef4b4e19f9.sourceText: According to some sources, frybread was a result of the “Long Walk'' in 1864, in which the United States government forced Navajo peoples living in modern-day Arizona to march 300 miles to eastern New Mexico. Unable to feed themselves in unfamiliar terrain, the Navajo starved until the government shipped rations of flour, salt, and lard—the primary ingredients in frybread. While it’s simply salted dough fried in oil, frybread today occupies a place of great—if not, complicated—significance in indigenous food culture, one you can taste for yourself at a roadside eatery just outside of Scottsdale.
b89299fa2f2c27125e55b6d945b689ef4b4e19f9.translatedText: 據一些消息來源稱，炸麵包是 1864 年「長途跋涉」的結果，當時美國政府強迫居住在現代亞利桑那州的納瓦霍人行軍 300 英里到新墨西哥州東部。由於無法在陌生的地形中養活自己，納瓦霍人挨餓，直到政府運送了定量的麵粉、鹽和豬油（炸麵包的主要成分）。雖然炸麵包只是用油煎的鹹麵團，但今天的炸麵包佔據了這個地方在本土飲食文化中具有重要意義（如果不是複雜的話），您可以在斯科茨代爾郊外的路邊餐館親自品嚐。

c45e24a2fb70c678dd8a18bfc5cbaa8deef3ca5d.sourceText: The Stand places frybread at the heart of its menu. This handmade stand constructed from arrowroot and cactus ribs serves rich, homemade toppings on frybread that’s always made to order. Visitors can select from red chili, green chili, or “Christmas-style”—a combination of both—as well as “Indian tacos” (beans, hamburger meat, cheese, lettuce, tomato, and onions), bean & cheese tacos, or menudo (beef tripe). On the sweet side, The Stand offers frybread topped with honey and powdered sugar as well as a colorful strawberry jello poke cake (a fluffy sponge cake with swirls of strawberry jello and whipped cream).
c45e24a2fb70c678dd8a18bfc5cbaa8deef3ca5d.translatedText: The Stand 將炸麵包放在其菜單的中心位置，這種手工製作的炸麵包攤位由葛根和仙人掌排骨製成，提供豐富的自製配料，並且總是按訂單製作。兩者的組合，還有“印度炸玉米餅”（豆子、漢堡肉、起司、生菜、番茄和洋蔥）、豆子和起司炸玉米餅或 menudo（牛肚）。 甜食方面，The Stand 提供淋上蜂蜜和糖粉的炸麵包以及色彩繽紛的草莓果凍蛋糕（一種鬆軟的海綿蛋糕，上面有草莓果凍和攪打的漩渦）。

9811f7bf84f12a3f25a3af7ea537345e676c44a7.sourceText: Located within the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community, this quaint eatery has a grassroots following among those living on the reservation as well as Phoenix-area eaters in-the-know. On a given day, other local vendors may be selling lemonade, popcorn, blankets, or jewelry from neighboring stands.
9811f7bf84f12a3f25a3af7ea537345e676c44a7.translatedText: 這家古色古香的餐廳位於鹽湖城皮馬-馬里科帕印第安社區內，在保留地的居民和鳳凰城地區的知情者中擁有一批草根追隨者。在某一天，其他當地攤販可能會在附近的攤位上出售檸檬水、爆米花、毯子或珠寶。

ebc63d31d0fb91fb011e4a8abbfec83a51deddc7.sourceText: In keeping with the rustic theme, The Stand is cash-only and offers no bathroom on the premises. The only “seats” to speak of are stumps placed in the shade of a nearby tree, but diners are invited to bring their own seating if they wish.
ebc63d31d0fb91fb011e4a8abbfec83a51deddc7.translatedText: 為了與鄉村主題保持一致，The Stand 只收現金，並且店內不提供浴室。唯一值得一提的「座位」是放置在附近樹蔭下的樹樁，但如果食客願意，可以自備座位。

ecf78887e4c348f5d4a2913b6d7089a8c27eb9ce.sourceText: This abandoned former open pit copper mine and processing facility, easily found on a map and not difficult to access, is an ideal destination for rockhounds and mining history enthusiasts.
ecf78887e4c348f5d4a2913b6d7089a8c27eb9ce.translatedText: 這個廢棄的前露天銅礦和加工設施在地圖上很容易找到，而且不難到達，是岩石獵人和採礦歷史愛好者的理想目的地。

4312c13d908c0334026af363798be38febf1ea07.sourceText: Based on reports, this mine was worked at various times from 1917 all the way up until 1998 by companies including the Emerald Isle Copper Co. and the Lewin-Mathes Co. During 1943-48 alone, 55,000 tons of copper was recovered from the ores.
4312c13d908c0334026af363798be38febf1ea07.translatedText: 根據報告，從 1917 年到 1998 年，該礦曾由 Emerald Isle Copper Co. 和 Lewin-Mathes Co. 等公司多次開採。僅在 1943-48 年期間，就有 55,000 人在開採該礦。從礦石中回收了數噸銅。

60d076236ee35010b287fc2f40d6184c4789f830.sourceText: Mining was originally done underground, but switched to the now open pit in 1943. It was intermittently worked up until 1993 when it was mothballed for possible future operations. Visitors can glimpse an open tunnel on the side of the open pit when driving down into it, but the sides of the pit are too steep to enter the tunnel safely.
60d076236ee35010b287fc2f40d6184c4789f830.translatedText: 採礦最初是在地下進行的，但在 1943 年改為現在的露天礦坑。它間歇性地進行開採，直到 1993 年才被封存以備將來可能的作業。遊客開車進入露天礦坑時，可以看到露天礦坑側面有一條開放的隧道，但坑壁太陡，無法安全進入隧道。

8ce0751557a4005bc2eeeb907d1148851a359cc2.sourceText: The entrance road leads to a few giant storage tanks which are open, one of them harboring an old car inside. From the storage tanks, visitors can explore an old building full of miscellaneous papers, supplies, and tool's from the mine's working days.
8ce0751557a4005bc2eeeb907d1148851a359cc2.translatedText: 入口道路通往幾個露天的巨型儲罐，其中一個儲罐裡停著一輛舊汽車。從儲罐中，遊客可以探索一座古老的建築，裡面裝滿了礦山工作日的各種紙張、用品和工具。

fea3444169a491898fa9cf4cb9e53d726b4959db.sourceText: Outside of the building are the former processing machines which extracted valuable minerals from the mined rock. Within the open pit mine, accessible via a sturdy high-clearance vehicle or four-wheel drive, visitors will find beautifully turquoise-colored rocks of copper mineral ore known as chrysocolla.
fea3444169a491898fa9cf4cb9e53d726b4959db.translatedText: 建築物外面是以前的加工機器，從開採的岩石中提取有價值的礦物。在露天礦場內，遊客可以透過堅固的高間隙車輛或四輪驅動車進入，在那裡您會發現美麗的綠松石色銅礦岩石，稱為矽孔雀石。

3bcbfaef68a9e90050fd66f4c67ab65362399a02.sourceText: Between the processing facility and the road that leads down into the pit, it will be hard to miss the large pool of bright turquoise copper-ore-infused water which sports odd turquoise-colored foam on the surface.
3bcbfaef68a9e90050fd66f4c67ab65362399a02.translatedText: 在加工設施和通往礦坑的道路之間，很難錯過一大片明亮的綠松石色銅礦石注入水，表面上有奇怪的綠松石色泡沫。
