ee4112f8c86ded16a3be15209d2b254b554d40c8.sourceText: The Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department is sponsoring and hosting a series of free or low-cost fun family events to celebrate Halloween and the arrival of fall. Many of the Halloween event locations* also are drop off sites for Emily’s Toys 4 Joy (online: emilystoys4joy.com), a local nonprofit that collects toys to distribute to hospitalized children.
ee4112f8c86ded16a3be15209d2b254b554d40c8.translatedText: 鳳凰城公園和休閒部正在贊助和舉辦一系列免費或低成本的有趣家庭活動，以慶祝萬聖節和秋季的到來。許多萬聖節活動地點*也是 Emily’s Toys 4 Joy（線上：emilystoys4joy.com）的下車地點，這是一個當地非營利組織，收集玩具分發給住院兒童。

acd43a97778ba3ca6a1b2d9ddee5d60e34477540.sourceText: Enchanted Trail, Nina Mason Pulliam Rio Salado Audubon Center, 3131 S. Central Ave. Friday?nbsp;Sunday, Oct. 18-20, 5:30 to 8 p.m. each day This free family event is produced by the Audubon Center at Phoenix’s Rio Salado Habitat Restoration Area. It features trick or treating, a scary bat cave, crafts, guided night hikes, nature by night exhibits, live Arizona animals and more. Information is available by phone at 602-468-6470.
acd43a97778ba3ca6a1b2d9ddee5d60e34477540.translatedText: Enchanted Trail，Nina Mason Pulliam Rio Salado Audubon Center，3131 S. Central Ave。週五？ nbsp;週日，10 月 18 日至 20 日，下午 5:30 至晚上 8 點每天 這項免費的家庭活動由鳳凰城裡約薩拉多棲息地恢復區的奧杜邦中心舉辦。其特色包括“不給糖就搗蛋”、可怕的蝙蝠洞、工藝品、帶導遊的夜間徒步旅行、夜間自然展覽、亞利桑那州的活動物等等。如需了解信息，請致電 602-468-6470。

edcf3c789bfa33cddf2a0f1f19d2bd7c228b3325.sourceText: Boo Fest, Beuf Community Center/Paseo Highlands Park, 3425 W. Pinnacle Peak Rd. Saturday, Oct. 26, 6 to 9 p.m. Boo Fest is a free, family event that features horse drawn hayrides, a pumpkin patch (for kids 15 and under), inflatable bouncers, climbing wall, carnival games, live entertainment and a costume parade with judging. Each child 15 and under gets a goodie bag. All activities are free. *This year’s event is being produced in partnership with Emily’s Toys for Joy; everyone who donates a new toy at the event will receive a free raffle ticket for a chance to win great prizes. More information: 602-534-4754. No registration is required.
edcf3c789bfa33cddf2a0f1f19d2bd7c228b3325.translatedText: Boo Fest，Beuf 社區中心/Paseo Highlands Park，3425 W. Pinnacle Peak Rd。 10 月 26 日星期六下午 6 點至 9 點Boo Fest 是一項免費的家庭活動，包括馬拉乾草車、南瓜田（適合 15 歲及以下兒童）、充氣彈跳器、攀岩牆、嘉年華遊戲、現場娛樂表演和帶評審的服裝遊行。每個 15 歲及以下的兒童都會獲得一個禮品袋。所有活動都是免費的。 *今年的活動是與 Emily’s Toys for Joy 合作舉辦的；每個在活動中捐贈新玩具的人都將獲得一張免費抽獎券，有機會贏得大獎。更多資訊：602-534-4754。無需註冊。

d8b5536ce88420f4d5026ae16a0393ade01b30c7.sourceText: Halloween & Zombie Walk, Heritage & Science Park, 115 N. 6th St. Saturday, Oct. 26, 2 to 11 p.m. This free, family-friendly event features live music, a Rose & Crown Beer garden, makeup artists, Bookmans?nbsp;Little Zombie Zone, vendors, a canned food drive and a march of over 10,000 zombies through the streets of Downtown (actual zombie walk takes place at approx. 6pm). Don’t know how to become a zombie? No problem! There will be makeup artists on hand to make you beautiful. All they ask in exchange is that you bring non-perishable food items or make a cash donation to benefit St. Mary’s Food Bank in exchange for a ghoulish makeover. The historic Rosson House Museum will also be open for special ticketed tours during the festival. Information on tours is available by phone at 602-262-5070 or by phone at www.rossonhousemuseum.org. Event information is available from event sponsor Downtown Phoenix Partnership by phone at 602-254-8696 or online at http://www.downtownphoenix.com/zombie/.
d8b5536ce88420f4d5026ae16a0393ade01b30c7.translatedText: 萬聖節和殭屍漫步，Heritage & Science Park, 115 N. 6th St. 10 月 26 日星期六，下午 2 點至 11 點這項免費、適合家庭的活動包括現場音樂、Rose & Crown 啤酒花園、化妝師、Bookmans?nbsp;小殭屍區、攤販、罐頭食品活動以及 10,000 多場殭屍在市中心遊行（殭屍市中心的遊行中只發生殭屍街道（殭屍市中心的遊行）。不知道怎麼變成殭屍？沒問題！會有化妝師為您化妝。他們所要求的交換條件是，你攜帶不易腐爛的食物或捐贈現金給聖瑪麗食品銀行，以換取殘忍的改造。歷史悠久的羅森故居博物館也將在節慶期間開放，提供特殊門票遊覽。有關旅遊信息，請致電 602-262-5070 或訪問 www.rossonhousemuseum.org。您可以透過電話 602-254-8696 或造訪 http://www.downtownphoenix.com/zombie/ 向活動贊助商 Downtown Phoenix Partnership 取得活動資訊。

fe26f447ffadc96f7af8d2bc52f724e185bac788.sourceText: Approximately equidistant from the cities of Tucson and Phoenix lies Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, a park that abuts the border of the United States and Mexico . The park was set aside to protect the rare cactus for which it was named, and hundreds of miles of trails wind through the arid landscape.
fe26f447ffadc96f7af8d2bc52f724e185bac788.translatedText: 風琴管仙人掌國家紀念碑距離圖森市和菲尼克斯市大約等距，是一個毗鄰美國和墨西哥邊境的公園。該公園是為了保護其命名的稀有仙人掌而設立的，數百英里的小徑蜿蜒穿過乾旱的土地。

d4e87e2a474f7eee3802c310b882cf3dcc7d9df9.sourceText: One of those trails is the Arch Canyon Trail. The official listing for the trail is only 1.2 miles, which takes visitors briefly into a beautiful canyon which the arch overlooks. However, intrepid climbers have taken things into their own hands and fashioned a trail up a near-vertical cliff to get to the arches themselves. A steep, rocky 2.4-mile hike (more of a climb, really) leads to a set of natural arches and stunning views of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Arizona , and Mexico.
d4e87e2a474f7eee3802c310b882cf3dcc7d9df9.translatedText: 拱門峽谷步道就是其中之一。官方列出的這條步道只有 1.2 英里，遊客可以短暫進入拱門俯瞰的美麗峽谷。然而，勇敢的登山者已經親自動手，在近乎垂直的懸崖上開闢了一條小路，以到達拱門。一段 2.4 英里的陡峭岩石徒步旅行（實際上更像是一次攀登）通往一系列天然拱門，欣賞風琴管仙人掌國家紀念碑、亞利桑那州和墨西哥的壯麗景色。

a41321f843e8d8ca2ec9e143e896e7d615e688c4.sourceText: The only clue that this trail exists is a sign that reads, ominously, "CAUTION: STEEP ROCKY ROUTE AHEAD." Heed the sign's warnings, and carry a first aid kit and plenty of water if you choose to find your way to the arches.
a41321f843e8d8ca2ec9e143e896e7d615e688c4.translatedText: 這條小徑存在的唯一線索是一個標誌，上面寫著不祥的字樣：「注意：前面有陡峭的岩石路線。」請留意標誌牌上的警告，如果您選擇前往拱門，請攜帶急救箱和充足的水。

8911720db6367b7a3dae48a7f22ec109e8b559af.sourceText: Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument charges at $25/vehicle fee for day-use of the park. Additionally, unless you are an experienced navigator, leave the cairns as they are. Do not build additional cairns. You will confuse future hikers.
8911720db6367b7a3dae48a7f22ec109e8b559af.translatedText: 風琴管仙人掌國家紀念碑的公園日間使用費為每輛車 25 美元。此外，除非您是經驗豐富的航海家，否則請保持凱恩斯原樣。不要建造額外的石塚。你會讓未來的徒步旅行者感到困惑。

77f6baffd2b01ab12466c946f662fc92dca684cc.sourceText: Just an hour southeast of Page, Arizona , a hidden gem stands over a canyon in the Navajo Nation. Eggshell Arch is a natural sandstone arch formed over thousands of years by erosion. The arch is not well known (yet) so it is likely you won't see other visitors in the area.
77f6baffd2b01ab12466c946f662fc92dca684cc.translatedText: 距離亞利桑那州佩吉東南僅一小時路程，納瓦荷族保留地的峽谷上矗立著一顆隱藏的寶石。蛋殼拱門是經過數千年侵蝕形成的天然砂岩拱門。該拱門目前還不太為人所知，因此您很可能不會在該地區看到其他遊客。

68cc4b9ecdff8b67b9affe4b183f0bd2697430a9.sourceText: The arch glows during sunset from October to January, a phenomenon known as the "Thanksgiving Glow." This glow effect is created by the sun rays reflecting off of the canyon wall and onto the arch during sunset. The arch is located in Ts’ah Bii Kin ("House in the field of Sagebrush" in Dine) in northwestern Arizona. The area is unspoiled with very rugged terrain.
68cc4b9ecdff8b67b9affe4b183f0bd2697430a9.translatedText: 從十月到一月的日落期間，拱門會發光，這種現像被稱為「感恩節發光」。這種發光效果是由日落時太陽光線從峽谷壁反射到拱門上而產生的。這座拱門位於亞利桑那州西北部的 Ts’ah Bii Kin（迪恩語中的“山艾樹田裡的房子”）。該地區未受破壞，地勢非常崎嶇。

b054f83d66d05a838434a031e59110d37f070966.sourceText: This natural sandstone arch is only accessible by a certified guided tour. Please be respectful when visiting the Navajo Nation by following Leave No Trace principles.
b054f83d66d05a838434a031e59110d37f070966.translatedText: 這個天然砂岩拱門只能透過經過認證的導遊才能進入。造訪納瓦荷族保留區時，請遵守「不留痕跡」原則，保持尊重。

dc6ffd5674b2435679c858c2473601ec4e3c2a25.sourceText: Located on the Navajo Nation in Arizona , about halfway between Kayenta and Tuba City, Cow Springs Trading Post sees few outsiders. Most tourists who come through, passing between Monument Valley and Flagstaff , would barely give it a second glance out their car window. Its defining feature is a peeling brown and white Standard Oil sign that probably dates back to the 1960s, but the trading post below is now nothing more than a few crumbling stone walls covered in graffiti.
dc6ffd5674b2435679c858c2473601ec4e3c2a25.translatedText: 考斯普林斯貿易站 (Cow Springs Trading Post) 位於亞利桑那州納瓦霍族保留地，大約位於凱恩塔 (Kayenta) 和圖巴市 (Tuba City) 之間的中間位置，很少有外來者。大多數在紀念碑谷和弗拉格斯塔夫之間經過的遊客幾乎不會再看車窗外的它第二眼。它的標誌性特徵是剝落的棕白色標準石油標誌，其歷史可能可以追溯到 1960 年代，但下面的貿易站現在只不過是幾塊佈滿塗鴉的搖搖欲墜的石牆。

222af0c5586ee2e34624d6e278a7e334b51014cd.sourceText: There were once several trading posts in the area, which served as stores where reservation residents could trade things like wool, crafts, and agricultural products for dry goods and tools, and also acted as banks, courthouses, and meeting places. The Navajo Nation’s isolation in the northeastern corner of Arizona left its people open to abuse by the European traders who operated the trading posts. Usury, price-fixing, and withholding of government-issued checks were all standard practices during their heyday. Because few retailers have set up shop on the reservation, the tribe is still forced to rely on these trading posts for some basic goods.
222af0c5586ee2e34624d6e278a7e334b51014cd.translatedText: 該地區曾經有幾個貿易站，它們是保留地居民可以用羊毛、工藝品和農產品等物品交換乾貨和工具的商店，同時也充當銀行、法院和聚會場所。納瓦荷族部落位於亞利桑那州東北角，與世隔絕，使其人民容易受到經營貿易站的歐洲商人的虐待。高利貸、操縱價格和扣留政府簽發的支票都是其鼎盛時期的標準做法。由於很少零售商在保留地開設商店，部落仍然被迫依賴這些貿易站購買一些基本商品。

59ca4bd4bb7137fae6a5b43c0847a6a414f839a6.sourceText: There are no known photos of the Cow Springs Trading Post during its operational period, and little has been written about it. It was owned by the Babbitt Family, who owned several other trading posts in the area, and then it was shuttered in the 1970s.
59ca4bd4bb7137fae6a5b43c0847a6a414f839a6.translatedText: 沒有已知的考斯普林斯貿易站運作期間的照片，也很少有相關報告。它的所有者是巴比特家族 (Babbitt Family)，該家族在該地區擁有其他幾個貿易站，但在 1920 世紀 1970 年代被關閉。

6761e8f8aa2da3e28f7d262a5659f23d08ba67ea.sourceText: In the 50 or so years since Cow Springs Trading Post closed its doors, most of what was there has been removed. It’s believed that all of the wooden beams were taken for firewood and any kind of metal was stripped away for scrap. Only the concrete blocks remain, providing an ample canvas for artists.
6761e8f8aa2da3e28f7d262a5659f23d08ba67ea.translatedText: 自從考斯普林斯貿易站關閉以來的 50 多年裡，那裡的大部分東西都被拆除了。據信，所有木樑都被當作柴火，所有金屬都被剝去當作廢料。只剩下混凝土塊，為藝術家提供了充足的畫布。

b545341bcfa670fc4b24c7f441d32d019ca87256.sourceText: While much of the graffiti consists of simple tags and gang signs, a few of the pieces are more elaborate and express deeper feelings about politics and life on the reservation. Some are political messages, others hint at feelings of hopelessness, but a few strive for a more positive outlook.
b545341bcfa670fc4b24c7f441d32d019ca87256.translatedText: 雖然大部分塗鴉由簡單的標籤和幫派標誌組成，但其中一些作品更加精緻，表達了對保留地政治和生活的更深層次的感受。其中一些是政治訊息，有些則暗示著絕望的感覺，但也有一些力求更積極的前景。

23de656529e9fc3a0901069f79cd1f1f7062af91.sourceText: Several years ago, an artist by the name of Jetsonorama created some beautiful murals at Cow Springs by enlarging sections of his photographs documenting life on the reservation and meticulously assembling them into a mosaic. Unfortunately, his murals, consisting of nothing more than office paper wheatpasted to the concrete walls, have long since been lost to the elements and the passage of time.
23de656529e9fc3a0901069f79cd1f1f7062af91.translatedText: 幾年前，一位名叫 Jetsonorama 的藝術家在考斯普林斯創作了一些美麗的壁畫，他放大了記錄保留地生活的照片，並將它們精心組裝成馬賽克。不幸的是，他的壁畫只不過是貼在混凝土牆上的辦公用紙，早已隨著時間的流逝而消失了。

36173963ea9642cf07dc2495bd5da3b4897f8a2b.sourceText: Deep in the Sonoran Desert, in a remote corner of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument and only a few hundred feet away from the United States - Mexico border, is a surprising sight. Surrounded by arid desert to the horizons and beyond in every direction is a lush and lively freshwater pond. This is Quitobaquito Springs.
36173963ea9642cf07dc2495bd5da3b4897f8a2b.translatedText: 在索諾蘭沙漠深處，風琴管仙人掌國家紀念碑的一個偏遠角落，距離美國和墨西哥邊境僅幾百英尺，有令人驚訝的景象。周圍是乾旱的沙漠，一直延伸到地平線，四面八方都是鬱鬱蔥蔥、生機勃勃的淡水池塘。這裡是基多巴基託泉。

80ef918fbb4d99c2df6ef40f3115b4012016331a.sourceText: Humans have visited Quitobaquito for thousands of years. Artifacts found there have been dated to at least 16,000 years ago. The first recorded European to visit the springs was Father Eusebio Francisco Kino, a Jesuit missionary, explorer, and cartographer in 1698. He named the springs San Sergio and established a Catholic mission in nearby Sonoyta, Mexico.
80ef918fbb4d99c2df6ef40f3115b4012016331a.translatedText: 人類已經造訪基多巴基托數千年了。在那裡發現的文物至少可以追溯到 16,000 年前。第一個有記載的歐洲人參觀泉水是 1698 年耶穌會傳教士、探險家和製圖師尤西比奧·弗朗西斯科·基諾 (Eusebio Francisco Kino) 神父。他將泉水命名為聖塞爾吉奧 (San Sergio)，並在墨西哥索諾伊塔附近建立了一個天主教傳教團。

5702cf9c03322c7b6142f9c4e58984a54de3cc53.sourceText: In 1937, President Franklin Delano Roosevelt established Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument and 20 years later, in 1957, the Orosco family sold their adjacent land, including Quitobaquito Springs, to the government and it was added to the national monument.
5702cf9c03322c7b6142f9c4e58984a54de3cc53.translatedText: 1937 年，富蘭克林·德拉諾·羅斯福總統建立了風琴管仙人掌國家紀念碑，20 年後的 1957 年，奧羅斯科家族將其出售他們的鄰近土地，包括基托巴基托溫泉，已交給政府，並被添加到國家紀念碑中。

6b2556281e6c0d43a8ed2e964511644f275d1174.sourceText: These protected springs are the only place to find several endangered and threatened species within the United States. The Quitobaquito pupfish, the Sonoyta mud turtle, and the Quitobaquito spring snail only live there and within a small number of other springs in Mexico.
6b2556281e6c0d43a8ed2e964511644f275d1174.translatedText: 這些受保護的溫泉是美國境內發現多種瀕危和受威脅物種的唯一地方。基多巴基托鱂魚、索諾伊塔泥龜和基多巴基托泉蝸​​牛隻生活在那裡以及墨西哥的少數其他泉水中。

683a4f71cad2d3b78ab3ddab3f66cb56f360cdd5.sourceText: Today, however, this rare and fragile habitat is under threat because of its proximity to the border. Planned construction of a wall along the border could disrupt both the aboveground ecosystems and the underground water sources that feed the springs. The Department of Homeland Security has stated that it will not pump underground water for the production of concrete within five miles of Quitobaquito Springs, but scientists are still concerned that the aquifer will be damaged and that a wall will threaten the fragile ecology of the area by limiting the natural migrations of wildlife.
683a4f71cad2d3b78ab3ddab3f66cb56f360cdd5.translatedText: 然而如今，這個稀有而脆弱的棲息地由於靠近邊境而受到威脅。計劃沿著邊境建造隔離牆可能會破壞地上生態系統和供應泉水的地下水源。美國國土安全部表示，不會在基多巴基托泉五英里範圍內抽取地下水用於生產混凝土，但科學家仍然擔心含水層會受到破壞，而且隔離牆會限制野生動物的自然遷徙，從而威脅到該地區脆弱的生態。

6451773a0c7f89aa65c91d02cafdc92a33f6c63a.sourceText: One of the largest open-pit copper mining operations in the entire country, ASARCO is one of the only Arizona giants to provide a tour. Highly recommended if you're in the Tucson area, the tour welcomes both those in favor of and opposed to open-pit copper mining and its environmental consequences.
6451773a0c7f89aa65c91d02cafdc92a33f6c63a.translatedText: ASARCO 是全國最大的露天銅礦開採企業之一，也是亞利桑那州僅有的提供遊覽服務的巨頭之一。如果您在圖森地區，強烈建議您參加這次旅行，歡迎支持和反對露天銅礦開採及其環境後果的人。

e2153b9ff60678b6e303870b62c8b1af3445156f.sourceText: The Mineral Discovery Center screens a short film called "Mining for Music" and the science exhibits and displays of historic mining equipment from what was once Arizona's biggest industry are impressive in scope and scale. Some of the exhibits demonstrate how copper deposits are formed naturally in the earth, how miners extract copper minerals from the rock to produce nearly pure metal, and more. The Mission Mine has an average grade of only about 0.67 percent copper, which means that every ton - or 2,000 pounds - of ore that comes out of the mine produces only 13 pounds of copper.
e2153b9ff60678b6e303870b62c8b1af3445156f.translatedText: 礦物探索中心放映一部名為「音樂採礦」的短片，科學展覽和曾經亞利桑那州最大工業的歷史採礦設備的展示在範圍和規模上都令人印象深刻。一些展品展示了銅礦床如何在地球中自然形成，礦工如何從岩石中提取銅礦物以生產近乎純淨的金屬等等。 Mission 礦的平均銅品位僅為 0.67% 左右，這意味著從礦場產出的每噸（即 2,000 磅）礦石只能產出 13 磅銅。

f66bfe3f4632ccebd8b0fdec1398afe63d4ecc25.sourceText: In addition, for every ton of ore, about three tons of waste rock must be removed. To keep the pit economically feasible, engineers use sophisticated equipment that tracks progress. When the price of copper is low, miners work on excavating areas with higher-grade ore. The Mission Mine is about two miles across and a quarter-mile deep. About six times the amount of earth that was moved to form the Panama Canal has been mined at this site.
f66bfe3f4632ccebd8b0fdec1398afe63d4ecc25.translatedText: 此外，每生產一噸礦石，必須清除約三噸廢石。為了保持礦坑在經濟上可行，工程師使用先進的設備來追蹤進度。當銅價較低時，礦工會在礦石品位較高的地區進行開採。 Mission 礦井寬約兩英里，深度四分之一英里。該地點開採的土方量約為為形成巴拿馬運河而移動的土方量的六倍。

7beeaf64fd22e33016e477d98a24052a34b6b2cf.sourceText: One of southern Arizona’s most prominent petroglyph sites is Signal Hill in the Tucson Mountain District of Saguaro National Park. This location features over 200 petroglyphs created by the Hohokam (the predecessors to today’s Akimel O’odham and Tohono O’odham tribes). The exact dates have been difficult to establish, but archeologists believe the petroglyphs were first etched sometime between 550 and 1,550 years ago.
7beeaf64fd22e33016e477d98a24052a34b6b2cf.translatedText: 亞利桑那州南部最著名的岩畫遺址之一是仙人掌國家公園圖森山區的號誌山。该地点拥有 Hohokam（当今 Akimel O’odham 部落和 Tohono O’odham 部落的前身）创作的 200 多处岩画。確切的日期很難確定，但考古學家認為這些岩畫是在 550 到 1,550 年前的某個時候首次蝕刻的。

2a1b536935fc4747ac46fef6683ef2ec91738eeb.sourceText: The designs, which were created by pecking into the desert varnish coating the rocks on the hills, feature depictions of people, animals including bighorn sheep, snakes, and lizards as well as many geometric symbols such as segmented circles and spirals. The most notable petroglyph at the site is a very large spiral on a rock near the hill’s summit. As with many petroglyphs, the exact purpose and meaning of the artwork has been lost to time.
2a1b536935fc4747ac46fef6683ef2ec91738eeb.translatedText: 這些圖案是透過啄食山上岩石上的沙漠清漆而形成的，描繪了人物、包括大角羊、蛇和蜥蜴在內的動物，以及許多幾何符號，如分段圓圈和螺旋。該地點最著名的岩畫是山頂附近岩石上的一個非常大的螺旋。與許多岩畫一樣，這件藝術品的確切目的和意義已經隨著時間的推移而消失。

7ed36c259fb0c33d186efe034c75e8024471e574.sourceText: In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, visitors began to travel west into the desert and over the Tucson Mountains to see the petroglyphs. In the 1930s, the Civilian Conservation Corps created both the picnic area at the base of the hill as well as the trail to the top that are now as much a part of the history of the park as the petroglyphs themselves.
7ed36c259fb0c33d186efe034c75e8024471e574.translatedText: 在 19 世纪末和 20 世纪初，游客开始向西进入沙漠，越过图森山脉来观赏岩画。 1920 世紀 30 年代，民間保護團在山腳下建造了野餐區以及通往山頂的小徑，如今它們與岩畫本身一樣成為了公園歷史的一部分。

4b82a8aafdde1cd4be6da18cff9b60a37d3b5d15.sourceText: The area was incorporated into Saguaro National Monument in 1961, and the monument became a park in 1994. Tourists visiting today can now follow this trail to the top to see the site’s petroglyphs and to admire the views of the surrounding Sonoran Desert wilderness.
4b82a8aafdde1cd4be6da18cff9b60a37d3b5d15.translatedText: 該地區於 1961 年併入仙人掌國家紀念碑，該紀念碑於 1994 年成為公園。今天參觀的遊客現在可以沿著這條小徑到達山頂觀賞風景欣賞該地點的岩畫並欣賞周圍索諾蘭沙漠荒野的景色。

94cf0e8aee3a2fede36166fe3ce1798afa03b067.sourceText: At Sears Point, near the Gila River in Arizona , around two miles of basalt cliff edges are filled with ancient art. There are more than 2,000 panels of rock art, with an estimated 10,000 petroglyphs elements. The area also contains a number of geoglyphs and other features of archaeological interest.
94cf0e8aee3a2fede36166fe3ce1798afa03b067.translatedText: 在亞利桑那州希拉河附近的西爾斯角，大約兩英里長的玄武岩懸崖邊緣充滿了古代藝術品。這裡有 2,000 多塊岩畫，估計有 10,000 個岩畫元素。該地區還包含許多地質符號和其他具有考古價值的特徵。

7a00cc0af15842b13f851b85bed0db3279275cc1.sourceText: Archaeologists consider Sears Point one of the most significant collections of rock art in the American Southwest. This is due to the sheer density of petroglyphs, as well as the unique style of art. Many of the petroglyphs have been attributed to the Patayan culture tradition. Many different design elements are visible on these panels, including curvilinear, rectilinear, anthropomorphic, zoomorphic, abstract, and stylistic figures. In some places, flat basalt rocks were used for petroglyphs to mark trails. Several major petroglyph panels may be associated with Native American myths and legends. This area around Sears Point has been utilized for centuries by many cultures. Today, there are 15 tribes that claim cultural affiliation with the area.
7a00cc0af15842b13f851b85bed0db3279275cc1.translatedText: 考古學家認為西爾斯角是美國西南部最重要的岩石藝術收藏之一。這是由於岩畫的絕對密度以及獨特的藝術風格。許多岩畫都歸因於帕塔次文化傳統。這些面板上可以看到許多不同的設計元素，包括曲線、直線、擬人、動物、抽象和風格圖形。在一些地方，平坦的玄武岩被用來刻畫岩畫來標記小徑。幾個主要的岩畫面板可能與美洲原住民的神話和傳說有關。西爾斯角周圍的這個地區幾個世紀以來一直被多種文化所利用。如今，有 15 個部落聲稱與該地區有文化聯繫。

051366e5750f4a543b7fb3eb7c26e965dfc94bbd.sourceText: The Sears Point area also features examples of historic graffiti. Names and dates carved into the rock have been affiliated with early trappers, "49er" gold rush groups, and settlers who passed through the area between 1840 and 1900.
051366e5750f4a543b7fb3eb7c26e965dfc94bbd.translatedText: 西爾斯角地區也擁有歷史塗鴉的例子。刻在岩石上的名字和日期與早期捕獵者、「49er」淘金熱團體以及 1840 年至 1900 年間途經該地區的定居者有關。

76a1f86883cfddeabe0e4dafc7356888d7f3870c.sourceText: The area embraces a wide array of archaeological sites, including rock alignments, cleared areas, intaglios, petroglyphs, and aboriginal foot trails. The Arizona BLM has designated Sears Point an Area of Critical Environmental Concern, where special attention is required to protect and prevent damage to the site.
76a1f86883cfddeabe0e4dafc7356888d7f3870c.translatedText: 該地區擁有大量考古遺址，包括岩石排列、清理區域、凹雕、岩畫和原住民步道。亞利桑那州土地管理局已將西爾斯角指定為關鍵環境關注區域，需要特別注意保護和防止對該地點的破壞。

c5b444674b8f66964c041f51041f00717e40d2ed.sourceText: The early exploration and settlement of northern Arizona was dominated by thousands of miles of cliffs and canyons cut by the Colorado River and its tributaries. The Little Colorado River’s name is misleading. It is one of the Colorado River’s largest tributaries and forms impassable canyons for miles across the Navajo Nation before becoming shallower as it approaches what is now Cameron, Arizona. When a bridge was built there in 1911, it created the first easy access over the canyon and became the ideal place for a trading post.
c5b444674b8f66964c041f51041f00717e40d2ed.translatedText: 亞利桑那州北部的早期探索和定居主要是由科羅拉多河及其支流切割的數千英里的懸崖和峽谷。小科羅拉多河的名字具有誤導性。它是科羅拉多河最大的支流之一，在納瓦霍族保留地形成數英里長的無法通行的峽谷，然後在接近現在的亞利桑那州卡梅倫時變得越來越淺。 1911 年，那裡建造了一座橋樑，為穿越峽谷開闢了第一條便捷通道，並成為建立貿易站的理想地點。

4b34f3e55b8a888925cc4e532408289abc4a99f1.sourceText: Brothers Hubert and C.D. Richardson established the Little Colorado Trading Post in 1916, which was later renamed the Cameron Trading Post. A century later, it's one of approximately ten trading posts still operating in the Navajo Nation. The historical suspension bridge is no longer in use but still spans the canyon next to the trading post and can be seen from the highway.
4b34f3e55b8a888925cc4e532408289abc4a99f1.translatedText: Hubert 和 C.D. 兄弟理查森於 1916 年建立了小科羅拉多貿易站，後來更名為卡梅倫貿易站。一個世紀後，它是納瓦荷族保留地仍在運作的大約十個貿易站之一。這座歷史悠久的吊橋已不再使用，但仍橫跨貿易站旁的峽谷，從高速公路就可以看到。

05eeb4dc83ed83249946cc356254ea82b924206a.sourceText: Originally established so the Navajo and Hopi could barter their commodities, the trading post’s location near the Grand Canyon made it popular with travelers. A hotel was added in 1928. Over the years, the trading post continued to expand and in addition to the market and hotel, now includes an RV park, gift shop, restaurant, and a Native American fine arts gallery.
05eeb4dc83ed83249946cc356254ea82b924206a.translatedText: 貿易站最初是為了讓納瓦霍人和霍皮人交換商品而建立的，它靠近大峽谷的位置使其深受遊客歡迎。 1928 年增設了一家旅館。多年來，貿易站不斷擴大，除了市場和酒店外，現在還包括房車公園、禮品店、餐廳和美洲原住民藝術畫廊。

030d0406c4fdb1e9ff7aa6f81b2052322266a78c.sourceText: In addition to typical trinkets and souvenirs, the gift shop still sells a lot of the same products that were the basis of their original trade, including Navajo rugs, silver and turquoise jewelry, Hopi pottery, and kachinas. In the “Cameron Corral of Weaving,” Navajo weavers demonstrate traditional textile weaving techniques.
030d0406c4fdb1e9ff7aa6f81b2052322266a78c.translatedText: 除了典型的小飾品和紀念品外，禮品店還出售許多與原始貿易相同的產品，包括納瓦霍地毯、銀和綠松石珠寶、霍皮陶器和卡奇納斯。在「卡梅倫編織畜欄」中，納瓦荷織工展示傳統的紡織編織技術。

3296728da0a7e6a7948b6fc121fa435682bd6f84.sourceText: The Gadsden Pacific Toy Train Operating Museum is a volunteer-run museum with trains operating on various layouts. The layout range from tiny Z scale trains, to outdoor garden railroads. The exhibits cover more than 6000 square feet of indoor space. They even have a small train that gives rides during open houses. The museum has been around for nearly 20 years and is remembered from its days in the Foothills Mall. The museum's gift shop has souvenirs for visitors, as well as a large selection of model trains and hobby supplies
3296728da0a7e6a7948b6fc121fa435682bd6f84.translatedText: 加茲登太平洋玩具火車營運博物館是一個由志工營運的博物館，裡面有各種佈置的火車。佈局範圍從微型 Z 比例火車到戶外花園鐵路。展品覆蓋室內空間超過6000平方英尺。他們甚至還有一列小火車，可以在開放日期間搭乘。博物館已有近 20 年歷史，從位於山麓購物中心 (Foothills Mall) 的時代起就為人們所銘記。博物館的禮品店為遊客提供紀念品，以及大量精選的模型火車和業餘愛好用品

5766e54b667937cf3071a9cced5f0c1cd545a4ae.sourceText: This is a must-see when in Tucson. The museum also hosts several community events each year including a Polar Express event, train shows, and birthday parties. You can even rent out the museum for weddings.
5766e54b667937cf3071a9cced5f0c1cd545a4ae.translatedText: 這是在圖森時必看的地方。博物館每年還會舉辦多項社區活動，包括極地特快活動、火車表演和生日派對。您甚至可以出租博物館舉辦婚禮。

ac669fecd0eea14fc3bdaa69c9a9bcf8802accf4.sourceText: The museum is open on Sundays from 1 p.m. - 4 p.m.
ac669fecd0eea14fc3bdaa69c9a9bcf8802accf4.translatedText: 博物館每週日下午 1 點至 1 點開放。 - 下午 4 點

25d1b2e323ab06de961106b9e198bcc01f98495c.sourceText: Just west of downtown Tuscon stands Tumamoc Hill, also known as Chemamagi Du’ag , or Horned Lizard Mountain. It is a volcanic butte with deep scientific and historic significance.
25d1b2e323ab06de961106b9e198bcc01f98495c.translatedText: 圖森市中心西邊矗立著圖馬莫克山 (Tumamoc Hill)，也稱為 Chemmagi Du’ag 或角蜥蜴山。它是一座具有深刻科學和歷史意義的火山孤峰。

9ede0622505978f2ebc58747d3cf0ad79f44cfc4.sourceText: The site is an 860-acre ecological reserve and U.S. National Historic Landmark. Established by the Carnegie Institution in 1903, it became home to an early desert laboratory, created to study how plants adapt to desert conditions. The University of Arizona owns and manages much of the site, and it is still an active research location.
9ede0622505978f2ebc58747d3cf0ad79f44cfc4.translatedText: 該遺址是一個佔地 860 英畝的生態保護區和美國國家歷史地標。它由卡內基研究所於 1903 年建立，是早期沙漠實驗室的所在地，旨在研究植物如何適應沙漠條件。亞利桑那大學擁有並管理該地點的大部分，並且它仍然是一個活躍的研究場所。

cd5dfef031dd87871e5430ac95225573c71cd190.sourceText: Not just a spot for ecological research , Tumamoc Hill has a history of human activity that runs much deeper. Radiocarbon dating places early maize cultivation at around 4,100 years ago, which makes it the longest continuously inhabited site in the United States. The area was also once home to the Hohokam people, starting around the the year 400; this culture left behind petroglyphs and pottery fragments. The Tohono O’odham Nation, for whom Tumamoc Hill still holds sacred significance, descends from this group.
cd5dfef031dd87871e5430ac95225573c71cd190.translatedText: 圖馬莫克山不僅僅是一個生態研究場所，它還擁有更深厚的人類活動歷史。放射性碳定年法表明，早期玉米種植時間約為 4,100 年前，這使其成為美國連續居住時間最長的地區。從公元 400 年左右開始，該地區曾經是霍霍卡姆人的家園。這種文化留下了岩畫和陶器碎片。圖馬莫克山對他們來說仍然具有神聖意義的托霍諾·奧德姆民族就是這個群體的後裔。

4f8d2184e55d91a191d1fab572ade612b1a3c00b.sourceText: Today, the site is not just used for research—but recreation. About one-thousand people walk the hill each day, taking in the scenic views of the surrounding desert landscape. It is a three-mile round trip walk, with a 700-foot rise in elevation from bottom to top.
4f8d2184e55d91a191d1fab572ade612b1a3c00b.translatedText: 如今，該遺址不僅用於研究，也用於娛樂。每天大約有一千人在山上行走，欣賞周圍沙漠景觀的美景。這是一條往返三英里的步道，從下到上海拔有 700 英尺。

15dd340d40a519a14283350817101b3f7db142d5.sourceText: Since 1986, Casa Goofy has been a haven for travelers, artists, and transients. The property is strewn with industrial, post-apocalyptic metal yard art and clown-themed coffins, amongst other things. A massive dome covers the main house, but the volunteers who run the farm live in refurbished bread trucks, school buses, and shipping containers. The owner, Dennis, is a 79-year-old HVAC tech and former clown, often seen driving around town in a large yellow van painted like a banana spaceship. You’re welcome to explore the farm, meet the animals or even pitch in and help on a project.
15dd340d40a519a14283350817101b3f7db142d5.translatedText: 自 1986 年以來，Casa Goofy 一直是旅行者、藝術家和短暫停留的人的天堂。該物業遍布工業、後世界末日金屬庭院藝術品和小丑主題棺材等。主屋被一個巨大的圓頂覆蓋，但經營農場的志工住在翻新的麵包車、校車和貨櫃裡。車主丹尼斯 (Dennis) 是一名 79 歲的暖通空調技術人員，曾經是一名小丑，人們經常看到他開著一輛漆成香蕉太空船的黃色大貨車在城裡行駛。歡迎您探索農場、與動物見面，甚至參與專案並提供協助。

57caa75953c4a132291c1dae4d9c66f6201ce4fb.sourceText: By appointment only. Set up your visit at casagoofyintl@gmx.com. We ask that you wear close-toed shoes and be mindful of the nature of the property. It is a scrap yard in addition to a commune, farm, and petting zoo.
57caa75953c4a132291c1dae4d9c66f6201ce4fb.translatedText: 僅限預約。請透過 casagoofyintl@gmx.com 安排您的造訪。我們要求您穿著不露趾的鞋子，並注意房屋的性質。除了公社、農場和寵物動物園外，它還是一個廢料場。

72662245ee35f1c7a4f6532e8240fbca733b7d68.sourceText: If you're hiking through the forests of the Kaibab Plateau and hear a rustling in the trees or leaves, pause and look around. If you're lucky, you may be in for a rare treat.
72662245ee35f1c7a4f6532e8240fbca733b7d68.translatedText: 如果您在凱巴布高原的森林中健行，聽到樹木或樹葉的沙沙聲，請停下來環顧四周。幸運的話，您可能會享受到難得的享受。

b8b9b5cd43a8f97ac5c4a7c996b796fd0af28d66.sourceText: The Kaibab Plateau, an elevated region within the much larger Colorado Plateau, is a remote and largely undeveloped region of Northern Arizona flanked by the Grand Canyon on one side and lower elevation deserts on the others. Unlike the surrounding area, which is much more arid, the Kaibab Plateau is home to dense conifer forests and groves of aspen trees, which thrive in the cooler, windier, and wetter elevated region.
b8b9b5cd43a8f97ac5c4a7c996b796fd0af28d66.translatedText: 凱巴布高原是更大的科羅拉多高原內的一個高地區域，是亞利桑那州北部的一個偏遠且基本上未開發的地區，一側是大峽谷，另一側是低海拔沙漠。與乾旱得多的周邊地區不同，凱巴布高原擁有茂密的針葉林和白楊樹林，它們在涼爽、多風、濕潤的高地地區繁衍生息。

9983fefed7b7c94d0db2e66a4478eb4bd3f255a6.sourceText: One result of the plateau's ecological isolation was the evolution of a unique squirrel. Related to the much more common Abert's squirrel, which calls much of the the mountainous regions of western United States and Mexico home, the Kaibab squirrel became separated from its genetic cousins at some point in history atop the Kaibab Plateau.
9983fefed7b7c94d0db2e66a4478eb4bd3f255a6.translatedText: 高原生態隔離的一個結果是進化出了一種獨特的松鼠。凱巴布高原上的松鼠與更常見的阿伯特松鼠有關，阿伯特松鼠居住在美國西部和墨西哥的大部分山區，凱巴布松鼠在歷史上的某個時刻與它的近親在凱巴布高原頂部分離。

ae5aca4eb503ebe19d29ee2594f926d7c73c2829.sourceText: Only able to survive in ponderosa pine forests, the squirrels on the Kaibab Plateau are removed from their brethren by canyons and deserts and are now a genetically unique subspecies, confined to an area of only about 638 square miles. They're noted for their distinctive charcoal-colored bodies and strikingly white tails.
ae5aca4eb503ebe19d29ee2594f926d7c73c2829.translatedText: 凱巴布高原上的松鼠只能在黃松林中生存，它們被峽谷和沙漠從它們的兄弟中分離出來，現在是基因獨特的亞種，其生存範圍僅約 638 平方英里。它們以其獨特的炭色身體和醒目的白色尾巴而聞名。

c71fe75b6fdc90967e63425d4128041c2666def5.sourceText: Unlike squirrels living in many other more developed areas, the Kaibab squirrel doesn't interact with humans frequently, and largely still avoid crossing paths with any people they notice. So although the Kaibab squirrels are not facing an immediate threat of habitat loss or extinction, they're elusive, making spotting a Kaibab squirrel a semi-rare event.
c71fe75b6fdc90967e63425d4128041c2666def5.translatedText: 與生活在許多其他較發達地區的松鼠不同，凱巴布松鼠並不經常與人類互動，而且基本上仍然避免與它們注意到的任何人交叉。因此，儘管凱巴布松鼠沒有面臨棲息地喪失或滅絕的直接威脅，但它們難以捉摸，因此發現凱巴布松鼠成為半罕見的事件。

6a95ddf819351a9504bea5a11da1c924d5c2b9ca.sourceText: Still, despite their tendency to keep to themselves, the Kaibab squirrels have become locally beloved and iconic, gracing the imagery of logos, stickers, coffee mugs, and more on the Kaibab Plateau. In 1965, the Kaibab squirrels and their isolated habitat were recognized for their uniqueness and placed on the National Natural Landmarks Register.
6a95ddf819351a9504bea5a11da1c924d5c2b9ca.translatedText: 儘管如此，儘管凱巴布松鼠傾向於獨來獨往，但凱巴布松鼠已成為當地人喜愛的標誌性建築，為凱巴布高原上的徽標、貼紙、咖啡杯等圖案增光添彩。 1965 年，凱巴布松鼠及其與世隔絕的棲息地因其獨特性而受到認可，並被列入國家自然地標名錄。

97a90506edd1acd6e2dc22bc39897ab121fc7666.sourceText: Not far from the south rim of the Grand Canyon, a small building stands among a grove of ponderosa pines. Now a multipurpose center, it was envisioned as a grand, multi-faith chapel with impressive canyon views. Known as the Shrine of the Ages, this building's story dates back more than a century.
97a90506edd1acd6e2dc22bc39897ab121fc7666.translatedText: 距離大峽谷南緣不遠，一座小建築矗立在一片黃松林中。現在它是一個多功能中心，被設想為一座宏偉的多信仰教堂，享有令人印象深刻的峽谷景色。這座建築被稱為“時代神殿”，其故事可以追溯到一個多世紀前。

02898f568d37806438e15e2b1b29d5684017060a.sourceText: The idea of an interfaith chapel at the Grand Canyon was proposed as early as 1917—even before the canyon was formally established as a national park in 1919. Several decades passed before plans were actually drawn up. In 1952, a corporation made up of representatives from Catholic, Jewish, and Protestant groups came together to put together resources to build what they would call the Shrine of the Ages. They proposed building a permanent structure near a site on the canyon rim that was already being used for religious services.
02898f568d37806438e15e2b1b29d5684017060a.translatedText: 早在 1917 年，就有人提出在大峽谷建造跨宗教教堂的想法，甚至早在 1919 年峽谷正式建立為國家公園之前。幾十年後，規劃才真正制定出來。 1952 年，一個由天主教、猶太教和新教團體代表組成的公司聚集在一起，匯集資源建造他們所謂的「時代神殿」。他們提議在峽谷邊緣的一處地點附近建造一座永久性建築，該建築已用於宗教儀式。

3896f0d56e31a92bdadca2bc286ad9e8c443629b.sourceText: Harold E. Wagoner was selected as the architect of the shrine. He was tasked with designing a center that could be used by all faiths, respected the surrounding environment, and honored the history and culture of the region's Native American tribes. Wagoner's plans were inspired by the kiva, a type building commonly used by Pueblo Native Americans in the Southwest.
3896f0d56e31a92bdadca2bc286ad9e8c443629b.translatedText: 哈羅德·E·瓦格納 (Harold E. Wagoner) 被選為神社的建築師。他的任務是設計一個可供所有信仰使用的中心，尊重周圍的環境，並尊重該地區美洲原住民部落的歷史和文化。瓦格納的計劃受到 kiva 的啟發，kiva 是西南部普韋布洛美洲原住民常用的建築類型。

c2bfb5ba91a7360e5499aafc566eb31e3fb62f91.sourceText: According to Wagoner's original plan, the shrine was to house an auditorium, where a massive window would provide a sweeping view of the canyon. Altar configurations for different types of services would be raised and lowered via a hydraulic lift, and an organ would have wind chests and pipes located at different sections of the chapels.
c2bfb5ba91a7360e5499aafc566eb31e3fb62f91.translatedText: 根據瓦格納最初的計劃，這座神社將設有一個禮堂，在那裡有一扇巨大的窗戶可以將峽谷的景色一覽無餘。用於不同類型服務的祭壇配置將通過液壓升降機升降，風琴將在教堂的不同部分設置風箱和管道。

48b74fd9b503b08052d5d27c2869a25a26f484dc.sourceText: But Wagoner's dream for the shrine proved a bit too ambitious, and conservationists raised concerns about structure's location on the rim of the canyon. The chapel was redesigned and relocated to a site near the Grand Canyon Pioneer Cemetery, which serves as a resting place for many early settlers.
48b74fd9b503b08052d5d27c2869a25a26f484dc.translatedText: 但事實證明，瓦格納對神殿的夢想有點過於雄心勃勃，自然資源保護主義者對結構位於峽谷邊緣的位置表示擔憂。教堂經過重新設計並搬遷至大峽谷先鋒公墓附近的地點，該墓地是許多早期定居者的安息之地。

0c441920ab1d62e3e62e671ff933158ea6d26674.sourceText: By 1970, construction finished on the Shrine of the Ages. In 1975, the National Park Service took ownership of the building. Today, it's a not just a chapel but a multi-purpose building used for educational sessions, concerts, private events, and religious services.
0c441920ab1d62e3e62e671ff933158ea6d26674.translatedText: 到 1970 年，時代神殿的建設完成。 1975 年，國家公園管理局接管了該建築。如今，它不僅僅是一座教堂，也是一座多功能建築，用於舉辦教育課程、音樂會、私人活動和宗教服務。

2667ba18f818e458e1a0085e0fe8507baf2d9b3b.sourceText: Driving on the lonely U.S Route 93 between Wikieup and Wickenburg, Arizona, travelers will stumble upon a surprising sight: On a high tower, a wooden sign with red painted letters that says “Nothing.” There, the little ghost town of Nothing slowly fades under the blazing desert sun.
2667ba18f818e458e1a0085e0fe8507baf2d9b3b.translatedText: 在維基厄普和亞利桑那州威肯堡之間孤獨的美國 93 號公路上行駛時，旅行者會偶然發現令人驚訝的景象：在一座高塔上，有一個木製標誌，上面寫著紅色字母，上面寫著「什麼都沒有」。在那裡，Nothing 的小鬼城在沙漠的烈日下慢慢褪色。

f53bf305b27435566f4b8954b75a0b638c5f594c.sourceText: Established in 1977, Nothing had, at its peak, only four inhabitants. It was composed of a simple gas station and a small market (ironically named “All-Mart.”) The now-gone town sign once read: “ Town of Nothing Arizona. Founded 1977. Elevation 3269 ft. The staunch citizens of Nothing are full of Hope, Faith, and Believe in the work ethic. Thru the years, these dedicated people had faith in Nothing, hoped for Nothing, worked at Nothing, for Nothing .”
f53bf305b27435566f4b8954b75a0b638c5f594c.translatedText: Nothing 成立於 1977 年，鼎盛時期只有四名居民。它由一個簡單的加油站和一個小市場（諷刺地命名為“All-Mart”）組成。現已消失的小鎮標誌上曾經寫著：「亞利桑那州虛無鎮。成立於 1977 年。海拔 3269 英尺。虛無鎮堅定的公民充滿了希望、信念，並相信職業道德。多年來，這些敬業的人們對虛無有信心，對虛無希望，為虛無而工作。 」

7cafd2fff9ac1e4ff9e5ff5c0df1297aeec87ffc.sourceText: In 2016, the real estate company Century 21, with the participation of Nothing’s current owner, gave away free certificate of temporary ownership for plots of land in Nothing. These certificates, valid for a single day during Father’s Day, allowed kids to give their dads what they seem to want each year: “Nothing.”
7cafd2fff9ac1e4ff9e5ff5c0df1297aeec87ffc.translatedText: 2016年，21世紀房地產公司在Nothing現任業主的參與下，免費贈送Nothing地塊臨時所有權證。這些證書在父親節期間的一天內有效，允許孩子們給他們的父親他們每年似乎想要的東西：「什麼都沒有。」

6b37ab97f3233d0e5acfa1a21bbafd4e3f26a859.sourceText: Nothing, Arizona is located on U.S. Road 93, between Wickenburg and Wikieup. A truck rest area is situated in front of the remnant of the abandoned small town, allowing to park and explore the place. The buildings are surrounded by a crumbling fence and are easily accessible.
6b37ab97f3233d0e5acfa1a21bbafd4e3f26a859.translatedText: 什麼都沒有，亞利桑那州位於美國 93 號公路上，威肯堡和維基普之間。卡車休息區位於廢棄小鎮遺跡的前面，可以停車並探索這個地方。這些建築物周圍有搖搖欲墜的柵欄，交通便利。

e3a09de30d6b8af14d481e42ee45fde50fe35f09.sourceText: Located on the Colorado River in the Mojave Desert, Lake Havasu City is home to more lighthouses than any other city in the United States . There are 28 fully-functional scale replicas of famous lighthouses, built and maintained by the Lake Havasu Lighthouse Club.
e3a09de30d6b8af14d481e42ee45fde50fe35f09.translatedText: 哈瓦蘇湖城位於莫哈維沙漠的科羅拉多河畔，是美國燈塔數量最多的城市。這裡有 28 座按比例縮小的全功能著名燈塔複製品，由哈瓦蘇湖​​燈塔俱樂部建造和維護。

40adcd799641d190bf0c360618e27d967a589056.sourceText: Originally conceived as a way to improve safety for the many boaters on Lake Havasu, the lighthouses became an attraction of their own and a labor of love for the Lake Havasu Lighthouse Club. The first lighthouse was dedicated in the year 2000 and the newest as recently as 2020.
40adcd799641d190bf0c360618e27d967a589056.translatedText: 最初的構想是為了提高哈瓦蘇湖上許多划船者的安全，這些燈塔本身就成為了一個景點，也是哈瓦蘇湖燈塔俱樂部的一項熱愛勞動。第一座燈塔於 2000 年落成，最新的一座於 2020 年落成。

58e651a312aa4b873cecf914c478083ea337e380.sourceText: The lighthouses, while both cute and impressive, are working lighthouses and have become important aids to navigation. Local emergency services have come to rely on them in certain situations – first responders can ask people in trouble to describe nearby lighthouses and are able to locate victims based on their descriptions.
58e651a312aa4b873cecf914c478083ea337e380.translatedText: 燈塔雖然可愛又令人印象深刻，但它們仍然是工作中的燈塔，已成為重要的導航輔助設施。在某些情況下，當地緊急服務部門已經開始依賴它們——急救人員可以要求遇到麻煩的人描述附近的燈塔，並能夠根據他們的描述來定位受害者。

d67f4b364ada6c4bf503dcf46fc53f74893ea269.sourceText: Replica lighthouses on the Arizona side of the river are models of lighthouses from the East Coast of the United States, while those on the California side of the river replicate lighthouses on the U.S. West Coast. Lighthouses on the city's island, accessed via the London Bridge , are replicas of lighthouses on the Great Lakes.
d67f4b364ada6c4bf503dcf46fc53f74893ea269.translatedText: 亞利桑那州一側的燈塔複製品是美國東海岸燈塔的模型，而加州一側的燈塔則是美國西海岸燈塔的複製品。通過倫敦橋進入城市島上的燈塔是五大湖燈塔的複製品。

25a3aa1cbf5828be4de1551206d6353265c2fc26.sourceText: In accordance with Coast Guard regulations, lighthouses on the west side feature a green beacon while east side lighthouses use red. The lighthouse club maintains a website with descriptions of each lighthouse, including GPS location, historical data, and sponsoring organizations or families.
25a3aa1cbf5828be4de1551206d6353265c2fc26.translatedText: 根據海岸防衛隊的規定，西側燈塔採用綠色燈塔，東側燈塔採用紅色燈塔。燈塔俱樂部維護一個網站，其中包含每個燈塔的描述，包括 GPS 位置、歷史資料以及贊助組織或家庭。

186c8967cc0ed883219fd9769173a41b2968becf.sourceText: Marcos de Niza was born in Nice, which is today in France but was at the time part of the Duchy of Savoy, in approximately 1495. It is unknown whether Marcos was ethnically Italian or French – the Duchy of Savoy was a largely Italian state, but with a sizable French population. He would have likely originally been known as either Marco da Nizza or as Marc de Nice. He was ordained as a Franciscan priest in the Catholic Church, moved to Spain, and entered that country’s service. Adopting the language and naming customs of his new home, he became known as Marcos de Niza, which is the name history remembers him as.
186c8967cc0ed883219fd9769173a41b2968becf.translatedText: 大約在 1495 年，馬科斯·德尼扎出生於尼斯，尼斯位於今天的法國，但當時是薩伏伊公國的一部分。目前尚不清楚馬可斯是義大利人還是法國人——薩伏伊公國主要是義大利國家，但也有相當多的法國人口。他最初可能被稱為馬可·達·尼扎 (Marco da Nizza) 或馬克·德·尼斯 (Marc de Nice)。他被任命為天主教會的方濟會牧師，搬到西班牙並開始為該國服務。他採用了新家的語言和命名習慣，被稱為馬科斯·德·尼扎（Marcos de Niza），這是歷史所銘記的名字。

8e39b2d7349cfd2d34e113338a967f5ed6e8815c.sourceText: In 1530, Marcos was dispatched to the new Spanish colonies in the Americas and traveled widely. He accompanied conquistadors in what would become Nicaragua, Peru, Ecuador, and Guatemala, serving as a priest alongside the conquering armies but also speaking out against atrocities committed against the native population. Marcos rose quickly through the priestly ranks and was appointed to a prominent position in Mexico.
8e39b2d7349cfd2d34e113338a967f5ed6e8815c.translatedText: 1530 年，馬可斯被派往西班牙在美洲的新殖民地，並進行了廣泛的旅行。他陪同征服者前往後來的尼加拉瓜、秘魯、厄瓜多和瓜地馬拉，在征服軍隊中擔任牧師，但也公開反對針對當地居民的暴行。馬科斯在神職人員中迅速晉升，並被任命為墨西哥的要職。

8eebe90278a6614e15bd56b61efcd44f9af27d45.sourceText: In 1536, four men from the doomed Narváez Expedition reached Mexico City, the only survivors out of around 600 that had gone missing eight years earlier. They had been stranded on the western coast of Florida and over the years had slowly managed to make their way along the Gulf Coast and down through what is now Texas and northern Mexico, before eventually returning to Spanish-controlled territory. The survivors chronicled their journey, recounting observations of foreign tribes, geography, plants, and animals. Most enticing to the Spaniards, however, were the rumors the survivors had about magnificently wealthy tribes and cities to the north of the area Spain controlled.
8eebe90278a6614e15bd56b61efcd44f9af27d45.translatedText: 1536 年，注定失敗的納爾瓦埃斯探險隊的四名男子抵達墨西哥城，他們是八年前失踪的約 600 人中唯一的倖存者。他們被困在佛羅裡達州西海岸，多年來慢慢地沿著墨西哥灣沿岸前進，穿過現在的德克薩斯州和墨西哥北部，最終返回西班牙控制的領土。倖存者記錄了他們的旅程，講述了對外國部落、地理、植物和動物的觀察。然而，對西班牙人來說，最有吸引力的是倖存者關於西班牙控制地區北部極其富裕的部落和城市的謠言。

10053de3aafa66efae8739611dcca5d0409e4c1a.sourceText: Today it is believed that the rumors of fabulously wealthy cities in the American Southwest were clever lies by the Native Americans, designed to encourage the pillaging Spaniards to seek their treasure elsewhere, but Spain took the bait. In 1538, Marcos de Niza was chosen to lead a scouting expedition to find the alleged cities of gold.
10053de3aafa66efae8739611dcca5d0409e4c1a.translatedText: 今天，人們認為美國西南部極其富裕的城市的謠言是美洲原住民的巧妙謊言，旨在鼓勵掠奪的西班牙人到其他地方尋找寶藏，但西班牙上鉤了。 1538 年，馬科斯·德·尼扎被選中率領一支偵察隊尋找所謂的黃金之城。

1a157650d1f554be9926ca2604fe63698a487b97.sourceText: Marcos de Niza returned from his expedition to Mexico City in 1539. He claimed to have seen from a distance a city larger than Mexico City, with buildings many stories high, and that his native guides told him that this was the smallest and poorest of the legendarily wealthy cities. Marcos’ fame grew and he was appointed to become head of the Franciscan order in the Spanish colonies. Meanwhile, Spain’s desire to conquer the cities of gold intensified and Marcos de Niza’s report added credibility to the rumors that they were real.
1a157650d1f554be9926ca2604fe63698a487b97.translatedText: 1539 年，馬科斯·德尼扎從墨西哥城探險歸來。他聲稱從遠處看到了一座比墨西哥城還要大的城市，裡面有很多層樓高的建築，而他的本土嚮導告訴他，這是傳說中的富裕城市中最小、最貧窮的一個。馬科斯的名氣越來越大，他被任命為西班牙殖民地方濟各會的領袖。同時，西班牙征服黃金之城的慾望愈演愈烈，馬科斯·德尼扎的報告增加了這些傳聞的可信度。

76eeb9c4f60fb952486b2ee859ce51de07cf7ace.sourceText: The conquistador Francisco Vázquez de Coronado was chosen to lead a much larger expedition of nearly 2,000 people to plunge into the area north of the colonies, claim the territory for Spain, and capture its great wealth in 1540. Despite his new position with administrative duties in Mexico City, Marcos de Niza was chosen to help guide the Coronado Expedition. Following his directions, the expedition was led to a small native village with only a handful of earthen houses, nothing at all like the fabulous city described in his report. Outraged, Coronado sent Marcos de Niza back to Mexico City in disgrace.
76eeb9c4f60fb952486b2ee859ce51de07cf7ace.translatedText: 征服者弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科羅納多被選為率領近 2,000 人的更大規模的探險隊，深入殖民地北部地區，為西班牙佔領領土，並在 1540 年奪取其巨額財富。儘管他的新職位擔負著行政職責在墨西哥城，馬科斯·德尼扎被選為科羅納多探險隊的嚮導。按照他的指示，探險隊來到了一個只有幾間土屋的小村莊，與他報告中描述的神話般的城市完全不同。憤怒的科羅納多將馬科斯·德尼扎遣送回墨西哥城，這讓他蒙羞。

1f023197907eeefb3ac9d525c5912082803f3f6f.sourceText: Outside Sierra Vista, Arizona is a quiet desert trail, scarcely distinguishable from the surrounding landscape. Plants are dry and hardy here, relying on infrequent rainstorms for water. It's hard to imagine that just 12,000 years ago, this place was an Ice Age paradise—a place where mammoths came for water and humans came to hunt.
1f023197907eeefb3ac9d525c5912082803f3f6f.translatedText: 亞利桑那州謝拉維斯塔外是一條安靜的沙漠小徑，與周圍的景觀幾乎沒有區別。這裡的植物乾燥而耐寒，依靠罕見的暴雨獲取水分。很難想像，僅僅 12,000 年前，這裡還是冰河時期的天堂——猛獁象來這裡取水，人類來這裡狩獵。

9737dd556a2d48ae1778c1a9d8c2ab9b21b32d3f.sourceText: The Murray Springs site was discovered by archaeologists C. Vance Haynes and Peter Mehringer from the University of Arizona in 1966. The types of tools found across the site were left behind by the Clovis Culture. It is believed that megafauna such as bison, horses, and mammoths came to drink along the now-dry riverbed, becoming easy prey for the well-armed humans camped nearby.
9737dd556a2d48ae1778c1a9d8c2ab9b21b32d3f.translatedText: 墨累泉遺址是由亞利桑那大學的考古學家 C. Vance Haynes 和 Peter Mehringer 於 1966 年發現的。在遺址中發現的工具類型是克洛維斯文化留下的。據信，野牛、馬和猛獁像等巨型動物來到現在乾涸的河床上喝水，很容易成為在附近露營的裝備精良的人類的獵物。

c02375885bc2e406b1f38e781f14866e22bcb6df.sourceText: These days, you won’t find any flint tools or mammoth bones at Murray Springs. What you will find is a trail between some of the dig sites, and interpretive signs describing the discoveries made there and the daily lives of the Clovis people. As you explore the trail, consider the stark contrast between the present and the ancient past. Perhaps the solitude of the desert trail will give you just enough perspective to envision their world, old and new and timeless all at once.
c02375885bc2e406b1f38e781f14866e22bcb6df.translatedText: 如今，您在墨累泉 (Murray Springs) 找不到任何燧石工具或猛獁象的骨頭。您會發現一些挖掘地點之間有一條小路，還有描述那裡的發現和克洛維斯人日常生活的解說牌。當您探索這條小路時，請考慮現在和古代之間的鮮明對比。也許沙漠小徑的孤獨會給您足夠的視角來想像他們的世界，新舊和永恆。

84b88a2500e4cb7e46064bf6e7076e7e114695f7.sourceText: The Murray Springs Clovis site is managed by the Bureau of Land Management. Admission is free, and the site is open from dawn until dusk. Always remember to stay on the trail and adhere to Leave No Trace principles.
84b88a2500e4cb7e46064bf6e7076e7e114695f7.translatedText: 墨累泉克洛維斯遺址由土地管理局管理。入場免費，該地點從黎明到黃昏開放。永遠記得要堅持走下去並遵守「不留痕跡」原則。

355e27af37cc9ce67f008dcbe372be7806982083.sourceText: Sinkholes typically occur in humid climates with limestone bedrock, where rainfall dissolves the limestone over time, leading to the collapse of the overlying rock into the void. They are less expected in arid country, where limestone is resistant to weathering.
355e27af37cc9ce67f008dcbe372be7806982083.translatedText: 天坑通常發生在有石灰岩基岩的潮濕氣候中，隨著時間的推移，降雨會溶解石灰岩，導致上覆岩石塌陷到空隙中。在乾旱國家，這種情況發生的可能性較小，因為那裡的石灰岩具有抗風化能力。

6f6d2936af9e5331e35078fa75f6abd38265ee93.sourceText: Other rocks can dissolve over time, however, and they can also cause sinkholes. The mineral gypsum, in particular, is soluble in water and common in some sedimentary rocks. Under the right conditions, it can be dissolved out by groundwater to create a void that then collapses. That is what's happened here. Also called the Littlefield or Beaver Dam sinkhole, after nearby villages, this spectacular collapse feature occurs in sediments on the eastern flank of the Beaver Dam Mountains.
6f6d2936af9e5331e35078fa75f6abd38265ee93.translatedText: 但是，其他岩石會隨著時間的推移而溶解，它們也可能導致天坑。尤其是礦物石膏，可溶於水，常見於一些沉積岩。在適當的條件下，它可以被地下水溶解，形成空隙，然後塌陷。這就是這裡發生的事情。這種壯觀的塌陷特徵也被稱為利特菲爾德或海狸水壩天坑，以附近的村莊命名，它發生在海狸水壩山脈東側的沉積物中。

3bfaf6452391d16aa7b518668bf0bb1a5484e76e.sourceText: The sinkhole probably formed as groundwater flowed down to Beaver Dam Wash, a tributary to the Virgin River coming in from the north. The sinkhole is in basin-fill sediments which in this area are known to be rich in gypsum locally. Other sinkholes occur in the general area, including Devils Throat in Gold Butte National Monument some 40 miles to the south.
3bfaf6452391d16aa7b518668bf0bb1a5484e76e.translatedText: 天坑可能是在地下水流向比弗水壩瓦什（Beaver Dam Wash）時形成的，海狸水壩瓦什是從北部流入的維爾京河的一條支流。該天坑位於盆地沉積物中，已知該地區富含石膏。其他天坑也出現在整個地區，包括以南約 40 英里處的金山國家保護區 (Gold Butte National Monument) 的魔鬼喉嚨 (Devils Throat)。

00e3832e6149fc6c2ceb15be9d3dda74af7cd8d5.sourceText: Unlike many sinkholes the walls of Cedar Pocket Sinkhole have partly collapsed, the west side having fallen in to form a steep slope leading to the bottom. This provides problematic access to the bottom of the sinkhole; a top-rope is strongly recommended if attempting to descend it.
00e3832e6149fc6c2ceb15be9d3dda74af7cd8d5.translatedText: 與許多天坑不同，雪鬆口袋天坑的牆壁已部分倒塌，西側已塌陷，形成通往底部的陡坡。這給進入天坑底部帶來了問題；如果嘗試下降，強烈建議使用頂部繩索。

250bb049cc247af1107bbc44941668ab901cff95.sourceText: Soldiers Hole was a well-known watering place of early stage days. Nothing here now but wide open beauty, a monument to the place, and an old chair, perhaps to provide rest for the rare, weary traveler.
250bb049cc247af1107bbc44941668ab901cff95.translatedText: 士兵洞是早期著名的飲水場所。現在這裡什麼都沒有，只有開闊的美景、一座紀念碑和一把舊椅子，也許是為難得的疲憊旅行者提供休息的地方。

a2c6150c0353d7451cd70bcaf9bcd92e6e5c03b8.sourceText: According to the inscription on the plaque, cavalry troops camped here during the Chiricahua Apache Campaign (1861-1886) because of a source of water known as Soldiers Hole. W. C. Sanderson and Ambrose Lyall struck artesian water nearby in 1883. A small settlement existed nearby in the 1890s, but after the railroad bypassed the site in 1909, it was largely abandoned.
a2c6150c0353d7451cd70bcaf9bcd92e6e5c03b8.translatedText: 根據牌匾上的銘文，在奇里卡瓦阿帕奇戰役（1861-1886）期間，騎兵部隊在這裡紮營，因為這裡有一個被稱為“士兵洞”的水源。 W. C. Sanderson 和 Ambrose Lyall 於 1883 年在附近發現了自流水。 1890 年代附近存在一個小型定居點，但在 1909 年鐵路繞過該地點後，該地區基本上被廢棄。

dc9d480b557eb1462baf9fc297a80a1d1c078898.sourceText: Interstate 17 is a busy corridor that crosses Arizona and serves as the primary artery connecting the high-elevation mountainous regions in the north with the low-lying desert regions in the south. And for more than 35 years, an unknown group has been decorating a juniper tree between the northbound and southbound lanes, about 55 miles north of Phoenix , for the holiday season.
dc9d480b557eb1462baf9fc297a80a1d1c078898.translatedText: 17 號州際公路是一條穿越亞利桑那州的繁忙走廊，是連接北部高海拔山區和南部低窪沙漠地區的主要動脈。 35 年來，一個不知名的組織一直在鳳凰城以北約 55 英里處的南北車道之間裝飾一棵杜松樹，以迎接節日。

a145ffea2d3df4e2e4e248b3a8e6796f1cb221f9.sourceText: The juniper in question is quite isolated, surrounded only by low grasses and cacti, so it stands out from the surrounding flora. Each year, sometime before Thanksgiving, it is decorated with ribbons, tinsel, flags, ornaments, and topped with a star. A rain barrel irrigation system that helps to water the tree in the parched environment is also suspected to have been installed by the unknown decorators. The decorations are quietly removed sometime after New Year's Day each year. Occasionally the tree is also decorated for the Fourth of July.
a145ffea2d3df4e2e4e248b3a8e6796f1cb221f9.translatedText: 這棵杜松樹非常孤立，周圍只有低矮的草叢和仙人掌，因此它從周圍的植物群中脫穎而出。每年感恩節前的某個時候，它都會用絲帶、金屬絲、旗幟、裝飾品裝飾，並在頂部裝飾一顆星星。身份不明的裝飾者也懷疑安裝了一個雨水桶灌溉系統，可以幫助在乾燥的環境中澆水。每年元旦後的某個時候，裝飾品都會被悄悄拆除。有時，這棵樹也會在七月四日裝飾。

9475d4c761dab6ca5d5432c6bb571b5a2c1e8d9f.sourceText: The tree sits on land managed by the Arizona Department of Transportation. A spokesman for the agency has indicated that they don't know who does the annual decorating, but that since they clean up after themselves each year, they don't interfere or investigate. Over the years wildfires have threatened the juniper but each time the tree miraculously emerges unscathed, including back in 2011 when the flames seemingly stopped right at the base of the tree itself. The tree has become a famous roadside landmark in Arizona, so much so that the official state balladeer, Dolan Ellis, wrote a song about the tree called “Scrubby.”
9475d4c761dab6ca5d5432c6bb571b5a2c1e8d9f.translatedText: 這棵樹坐落在由亞利桑那州交通部管理的土地上。該機構的發言人表示，他們不知道是誰進行年度裝飾，但由於他們每年都會自己清理，因此他們不會幹預或調查。多年來，野火一直威脅著杜松樹，但每次這棵樹都奇蹟般地毫髮無傷，包括 2011 年，當時火焰似乎就在樹根處停止了。這棵樹已成為亞利桑那州著名的路邊地標，以至於該州官方民謠歌手多蘭·埃利斯 (Dolan Ellis) 寫了一首關於這棵樹的歌曲，名為“Scrubby”。

f6d8be4d86d400f6e4d992876d3ec43c24378864.sourceText: Update June 2022: After being badly damaged in a brush fire in 2020, the I-17 Mystery Christmas Tree died .
f6d8be4d86d400f6e4d992876d3ec43c24378864.translatedText: 2022 年 6 月更新：在 2020 年的一場灌木叢火災中嚴重受損後，I-17 神秘聖誕樹死亡了。

4c434eb938523fbfeba92d658abadfaeac93902c.sourceText: The Hopi village of Oraibi has been continuously inhabited since its founding, which is estimated to have been around 1100, and even today the small village holds to their traditional way of living, and they don't especially appreciate visitors coming by to gawk.
4c434eb938523fbfeba92d658abadfaeac93902c.translatedText: 奧萊比 (Oraibi) 的霍皮族村莊自建立以來就一直有人居住，估計已有 1100 年左右的歷史，即使在今天，這個小村莊仍然保留著他們的傳統生活方式，他們並不特別歡迎遊客前來參觀。

07f5e3e97e8f8b6ee11445a9869afdcf762ced4c.sourceText: People have been living in the Arizona village for almost 1,000 years, which probably makes it the oldest continuously inhabited village in the United States. As America pushed west in the 1800s, bringing with it a new, modern way of life. In the mid-1800s a divide grew between the Hopi at Oraibi with those who took to the oncoming modernity breaking away from their more fiercely traditionalist brethren. By the latter part of the century, Kykotsmovi Village had been established by those wishing to move closer to the new trading posts, and this new village was colloquially named, "New Oraibi."
07f5e3e97e8f8b6ee11445a9869afdcf762ced4c.translatedText: 人們在亞利桑那州的村莊裡生活了近 1000 年，這可能使其成為美國最古老的持續有人居住的村莊。 1800 年代，美國向西推進，帶來了全新的現代生活方式。 1800 年代中期，奧萊比的霍皮人和那些接受即將到來的現代性、脫離了更為激烈的傳統主義同胞的人之間的分歧日益擴大。到本世紀後半葉，那些希望靠近新貿易站的人建立了 Kykotsmovi 村，這個新村莊俗稱「新奧萊比」。

aebafd64f95087ba3bb8ac00fd8aab645c5f7b59.sourceText: Today Kykotsmovi Village is the seat of the Hopi Tribal Council, however "Old Oraibi" is also still populated by Hopi traditionalists who have changed their way of life very little over the centuries. While the village is not off limits, visitors are not exactly welcomed with open arms, and photography is strictly prohibited. Given the self-imposed information lockdown, figures on the population and daily life are scarce, but seeing as how they have been living life their own way for a thousand years, it must be working out.
aebafd64f95087ba3bb8ac00fd8aab645c5f7b59.translatedText: 如今，Kykotsmovi 村是霍皮部落理事會的所在地，但「老奧萊比」仍然居住著霍皮傳統主義者，幾個世紀以來他們的生活方式幾乎沒有改變。雖然這個村莊不是禁區，但並沒有張開雙臂歡迎遊客，而且嚴格禁止拍照。鑑於自我實施的資訊封鎖，關於人口和日常生活的數據很少，但考慮到他們一千年來一直以自己的方式生活，它一定會成功。

fbedaaf94c5fc38f653607a7d05622555708afde.sourceText: Located within the third Mesa of the Hopi Reservation in Arizona, off State Route 264 approximately two hours northeast of Flagstaff.
fbedaaf94c5fc38f653607a7d05622555708afde.translatedText: 位於亞利桑那州霍皮保留地的第三台梅薩內，靠近 264 號國道，距離弗拉格斯塔夫東北約兩小時車程。

e977a8b6aa509d2275b7fdb7d62f4fa284933c57.sourceText: Built in the 1970s to cash in on some of that sweet F Troop money, Fort Courage is a replica fort built to resemble the one from the classic show. The trading post also included a gift shop, Armco gas station, and coffee house/Taco Bell.
e977a8b6aa509d2275b7fdb7d62f4fa284933c57.translatedText: 勇氣堡建於 20 世紀 70 年代，是為了從 F 部隊的一些豐厚收入中獲利而建造的，它是一座複製品，模仿了經典劇中的堡壘。貿易站還包括一家禮品店、Armco 加油站和咖啡館/Taco Bell。

5ec2aa3c0403b940588985c9b2789eb5da7013e3.sourceText: F Troop was a television series that ran from 1965-67, set in the fictional Fort Courage, an Army outpost (and neighboring town) out in the wilderness of the 1860s. The bumbling troop (hey, Larry Storch!) got into all manner of pickles and hijinks during its two seasons, before finally going off the air in 1967. However, the show's legacy lived on at the roadside attraction Fort Courage... sort of.
5ec2aa3c0403b940588985c9b2789eb5da7013e3.translatedText: F Troop 是一部 1965 年至 67 年間播出的電視連續劇，以虛構的勇氣堡為背景，這是 1860 年代荒野中的一個陸軍前哨基地（及鄰近城鎮）。這支笨手笨腳的隊伍（嘿，Larry Storch！）在兩季中搞了各種各樣的泡菜和狂歡，最終於 1967 年停播。然而，該劇的遺產在路邊景點勇氣堡繼續存在......有點。

4620499f7f25d150e2bb66940c4f3737c30272c0.sourceText: The replica fort, while not officially affiliated with the show, did not let this potential legal hurdle stop them, selling official merchandise and proudly displaying actual F Troop props. Because there was only so long that F Troop impersonating could be considered even vaguely financially viable, there was also a general store that sold groceries and Native American arts and crafts.
4620499f7f25d150e2bb66940c4f3737c30272c0.translatedText: 複製品堡壘雖然沒有正式隸屬於該劇，但並沒有讓這種潛在的法律障礙阻止他們，銷售官方商品並自豪地展示真實的商品。 F 部隊道具。因為模仿 F 部隊的時間很短，甚至可以被認為在經濟上是模糊的，所以還有一家雜貨店，出售雜貨和美洲原住民藝術品和工藝品。

2206ecf2014531b6648c940093d30259db395390.sourceText: Also on the trading post property were an Armco gas station and a pancake house, both now, like the fort itself, abandoned. The fort and general store are in remarkably good shape, while the now-fenced-off pancake house looks significantly more desolate. The coffee shop may or may not also have acted as a Taco Bell at one point in its life. A faded sign hangs above the door, but there's not much else to go by. Similarly, for an attraction with as many signs still dotting the interstate as Fort Courage does, there does not seem to be much in the way of history available for this possibly once mighty tourist trap.
2206ecf2014531b6648c940093d30259db395390.translatedText: 貿易站的地產上還有一個阿姆科加油站和一家煎餅店，現在這兩間都像堡壘本身一樣被廢棄了。堡壘和雜貨店的狀況非常好，現在被圍起來的煎餅屋看起來更荒涼。這家咖啡店在生命的某個階段可能也扮演過塔可鐘的角色，也可能沒有。門上方掛著一塊褪色的標牌，但沒有什麼好看的。同樣，對於像勇氣堡這樣在州際公路上仍然點綴著如此多標誌的景點來說，對於這個可能曾經強大的旅遊陷阱來說，似乎沒有太多的歷史可資借鑒。

66b6eeaae10402e6610c9dc30c43d3bf6fd354a6.sourceText: Ella's Frontier is one in a long line of Route 66 trading posts that the shiny new highway passed by. Despite being able to see the trucks and travelers rumbling down Interstate-40 from what’s left of the back door, the only thing left of Ella's today is a tumble-down building and a history rife with unforgettable characters.
66b6eeaae10402e6610c9dc30c43d3bf6fd354a6.translatedText: 艾拉邊境 (Ella's Frontier) 是一長串 66 號公路貿易站中的一個，閃亮的新高速公路經過這些貿易站。儘管可以從後門的殘骸中看到卡車和旅客在 40 號州際公路上隆隆駛過，但艾拉如今唯一留下的只是一座倒塌的建築和一段充滿令人難忘的人物的歷史。

8259330a50a5233288924e95b85caf39dde0af0e.sourceText: Originally built out of telephone poles, former circus clown, taxidermist, and sometimes poet Fredrick “San Diego” Rawson established San Diego's Old Frontier Trading Post in 1927. Depending on the source, the Old Frontier was either sold to Don Lorenzo Hubbell (of the Hubbell Trading Post in Ganado, Arizona, now a National Historic Site), to Hubbell’s son Ramon, or straight to Hawaiian band leader Ray Meany and his wife Ella Blackwell. However it happened, by 1947 it belonged to Ray and Ella, and they called it The Last Frontier .
8259330a50a5233288924e95b85caf39dde0af0e.translatedText: 最初是用電線桿建造的，前馬戲團小丑、動物標本剝制師、有時也是詩人弗雷德里克·“聖地亞哥”·羅森 (Fredrick “San Diego”Rawson) 於 1927 年建立了聖地亞哥舊邊境貿易站。根據消息來源，舊邊境要么賣給了唐·洛倫佐·哈貝爾（亞利桑那州加納多哈貝爾貿易站，現為國家歷史遺址），要么賣給了哈貝爾的兒子拉蒙，要么直接賣給了夏威夷樂隊領袖雷·米尼和他的妻子艾拉·布萊克威爾。然而，到了 1947 年，它屬於 Ray 和 Ella，他們稱之為「最後的邊境」。

4e0f68b793d22a7464ca9e3c5e5091409f6e292f.sourceText: In 1955 Ella and Ray divorced and she got the business in the settlement, and with a final name change it became Ella's Frontier Trading Post . A former Juilliard student, Ella was an eccentric who played her piano for travelers and, in later years, imaginary people and animals. She would often claim that Ella’s Frontier was built in 1847 or 1873 (predating the very telephone poles it was made of) and proudly proclaimed it the oldest trading post on Route 66. She stuck to that story until her death in 1984.
4e0f68b793d22a7464ca9e3c5e5091409f6e292f.translatedText: 1955 年，Ella 和 Ray 離婚，她在和解協議中獲得了該業務，最後更名後，它成為 Ella 的邊境貿易站。艾拉曾是茱莉亞音樂學院的學生，她個性古怪，她為旅行者彈奏鋼琴，後來又為想像中的人和動物彈奏鋼琴。她經常聲稱艾拉邊境建於 1847 年或 1873 年（早於構成它的電線桿），並自豪地宣稱它是 66 號公路上最古老的貿易站。她一直堅持這個說法，直到 1984 年去世。

6966eee1424b3ef0891684199deb1b17add168e6.sourceText: Since then, Ella's Frontier has been resting and rotting quietly beside another Route 66 casualty: the abandoned Big Arrow Campground.
6966eee1424b3ef0891684199deb1b17add168e6.translatedText: 從那時起，艾拉邊境就在另一名 66 號公路遇難者：被遺棄的大箭號旁靜靜地休息和腐爛。露營地。

b0fbc14ee17b36ecd3726852baef69dea858029c.sourceText: Update as of April 2023: There are no complete structures remaining on the Ella's site, but there is still a fair amount of evidence of what was once there.
b0fbc14ee17b36ecd3726852baef69dea858029c.translatedText: 截至 2023 年 4 月的更新：艾拉遺址上已沒有完整的建築，但仍有相當多的證據表明曾經存在過。

ee94925f077ef7f7a5e0b6d6c21faadc9205c520.sourceText: Update as of March 2025: The Ella's Frontier building was saved by Ed Klein of Route 66 World after the owners wanted to demolish it. After the timbers spent five years in storage, it is now being rebuilt close to the Jack Rabbit Trading Post in Joseph City.
ee94925f077ef7f7a5e0b6d6c21faadc9205c520.translatedText: 截至 2025 年 3 月的更新：埃拉的邊境建築在業主想要拆除後，被 66 號公路世界的 Ed Klein 保存。這些木材存放了五年後，現在正在約瑟夫市傑克兔貿易站附近重建。

14b6e1195a62b088c102035065de1181a4204334.sourceText: This "mountain" glitters in the sun, thanks to the small crystals that freckle its slopes. The mountain is actually an old selenite mine. It's still deeded to the mine owners, though it's managed by the Bureau of Land Management. It has a brief history and synopsis of selenite and its uses.
14b6e1195a62b088c102035065de1181a4204334.translatedText: 這座「山」在陽光下閃閃發光，這要歸功於山坡上點綴著的小晶體。這座山實際上是一個古老的亞硒酸鹽礦。儘管它由土地管理局管理，但它仍然屬於礦主。它介紹了亞硒酸鹽及其用途的簡要歷史和概要。

d7f200cacf0a1dc3beba6e525c7ffadf3bbe6471.sourceText: It's possible to wander among the small selenite deposits sparkling along the edges of the small pit.
d7f200cacf0a1dc3beba6e525c7ffadf3bbe6471.translatedText: 可以在沿著小礦坑邊緣閃閃發光的小型亞硒酸鹽礦床中漫步。

be8c9540ccad9bc8b74a1de5d91f2bab2006178e.sourceText: The active mine is not managed by the BLM. The BLM leases the mineral rights to this public property to the mine owner. The owner does not want anyone going into the pit or removing large crystals. If visitors continue to do so, he has indicated he will put a fence around it.
be8c9540ccad9bc8b74a1de5d91f2bab2006178e.translatedText: 活躍礦井不受 BLM 管理。土地管理局將這項公共財產的採礦權出租給礦主。主人不希望任何人進入坑或移除大晶體。如果遊客繼續這樣做，他已表示將在周圍設置圍欄。

31a68e4fd14c2ae12d76784167ef4100fc080786.sourceText: You can park close by the sign. You can climb down in the open pit (just 20 to 30 feet deep) and explore, and the selenite is plentifully dotted around all the mining area. It's safe to explore, though it's not handicap accessible. Please respect the landowner's wishes and do not take anything from the mine. The site's postal address is Littlefield, Ariz., but it is closer to St. George, Utah, and visitors need to approach from Utah.
31a68e4fd14c2ae12d76784167ef4100fc080786.translatedText: 您可以將車停在標誌附近。您可以爬到露天礦坑（僅 20 至 30 英尺深）進行探索，亞硒酸鹽大量分佈在整個礦區周圍。探索這裡是安全的，但不適合殘疾人士使用。請尊重土地所有者的意願，不要從礦井中拿走任何東西。該網站的郵寄地址是亞利桑那州利特菲爾德，但距離猶他州聖喬治更近，遊客需要從猶他州前往。
